_comment: Reading order, level, and per-story stretch vocabulary. Replaces the hardcoded ORDER list in index.py, which does not survive a growing corpus. Levels are defined once and stories declare one, so a new story slots into an existing rung rather than inventing another. Construction names here must match the keys in stats.py's GRAMMAR_PATTERNS.

budgets._comment: Rates, not counts, so they scale with story length: a fixed '5+ occurrences per new word' would have spent 5.7% of the shortest story's content tokens on two words, which reads as engineered. The mandatory requirement is qualitative and no script checks it — a new word's FIRST occurrence must sit in a sentence that frames its meaning. WHERE EACH NUMBER CAME FROM is ../CALIBRATION.md: the reference band against 25 authentic 児童文学 texts, why subordinate_share is measured and not gated, why min_sentence_stdev must not be raised, and five recorded corrections. That prose lived here until 2026-09-16 and was 97% of this block by weight, five values' worth, one unwrapped line per key.

defaults._comment: What a story is briefed to be when nothing is said. Resolution order is explicit argument, then this block; every parameter has a default so a bare invocation works. Defaults live here rather than in AUTHORING.md prose because a default nothing reads is a suggestion. `pages` is the unit because it is what the reader shows; tokens are derived, and every rate budget scales from tokens. null means derive from `budgets` at story length.

registers._comment: Adding a register here also adds it to the pool that `defaults.register: random` draws from, so a new type needs no other step. Five object-centred, quiet, past-tense stories closing on a concrete image is a house style that fell out of the recycling requirement rather than a decision anyone made. Naming it makes it a choice. Two of the alternatives already exist in the corpus as undeclared one-offs. Register changes voice and structure; it never relaxes the narrow-domain rule, because whatever the story is anchored on, an object or a ritual, is what its words recur on.
registers.quiet-realism: the original house style, now one register among the rest: one concrete object at the centre, close narration, ends on an image rather than a claim
registers.folktale: 城の鐘: nested time frames, a told-to-you voice, the turn stated once in dialogue
registers.procedural: 猫を探す探偵: a clue planted early and paid off late, the reader able to reach the answer from facts already on the page
registers.comic: 回覧板の返事: dramatic irony as the engine. The narrator misreads one thing consistently and the reader is a step ahead of him; the stakes stay small and social; 役割語 and dry dialogue carry the jokes rather than narration explaining them. The turn still costs the character something, and it ends on the ordinary resuming rather than on a punchline.
registers.ghost-story: none yet, the 怪談 shape: the ordinary held steady until one detail is wrong, and the wrong detail is never explained. Ends on the ordinary resuming, not on a reveal — nobody names what happened and no character theorises about it. It is the one register exempt from the stated reveal (AUTHORING § Craft, one turn): the 怪談's twist is that nothing is explained, so the afterword says what the story never does. Two guards, both from the September 2026 reviews. The dead must not be a relative the protagonist is mourning: 時計の音 and 煙突の煙 are that story twice and were rated ★2 both times, the second explicitly as derivative of the first, so grief is not what this register is for. And the wrong detail has to be retrievable — planted concretely, payable from facts already on the page — because 縁台の将棋 was marked down for a twist that was obvious and a premise that was never stated, which are the two ways this shape fails.
registers.epistolary: 六時五十分, as the counter-example: the story told only through what the characters write, notes, letters, a diary. No narrator between the reader and the page. The form is chosen first, as the way the story is told: the sheet names the in-world reason these people write instead of talking, as with notes passed in class where speaking would be caught, or one person's private diary with the whole world seen through that writer. The document is the frame and never a prop: nobody in the story finds, reads, checks or changes it, and no plant, beat or twist turns on what is on its page or that it was written. 八月の絵日記 and 六時五十分 both broke this (AUTHORING § Register). Two people who could simply talk, trading lines in a notebook, is a conversation poured into the form, and that is what 六時五十分 did (AUTHORING § Register). Each entry is dated or addressed, and voices separate by how each person writes. The twist is still stated by a writer once they understand it. Ends on a final entry, not a summary
registers.retrospective: 廊下の鏡, the 述懐 voice: an older narrator looking back, long subordinated sentences as the shape of memory, ends on a claim rather than an image. The claim is about the WORLD — a person, the object, a fact the narrator now holds — never about what the story means; that second thing is the closing-thesis defect cut from four of five stories in September 2026, and this register sits closer to it than any other. The guard that makes it safe is that the narrator earns the claim by watching a physical event, so the last page reports a correction of fact rather than a conclusion.

levels._comment: A level is a rung, not a checklist. `min_present` is how many of the level's own constructions a story must actually use; the rest are available, not required. `min_carried` is the fraction of every LOWER level's constructions the story should still exercise, which is what makes it a ladder rather than five disjoint sets. Level 5 deliberately has a low min_present: a few marked N2 forms inside otherwise-N3 prose is the 'flirting with N2' band, and requiring all of them would be the wall this is meant to avoid.

stories.title: 時計の音
stories._new_words: Declared here rather than in approved-words.json, which stays a short global list of permanent allowances. These are per-story teaching words: all four are the story's own subject matter, so they recur without the prose working at it. check.py does not flag them because the particle-splitting fallback accepts 部品 as 部+品 and 歯車 as 歯+車, so they have to be declared to be marked.

new_words.部品: watch parts — framed by the drawer of sorted boxes before it is ever used alone
new_words.歯車: gear — framed as the contents of the smallest box, too small to hold in the fingers
new_words.針: hand of a watch — framed p7 by the already-known 秒針 in the line before it, 細い秒針まではっきり見えた, so the bare 針 arrives as the set that second hand belongs to. Carries the stopped-at-three-ten thread, and the night the watch runs for hours without a hand advancing
new_words.振り子: pendulum — framed by the wall of shop clocks all swinging at the same speed

stories.title: 塩の卵焼き
stories._note: NOBODY DIES. The mother is in hospital for a few weeks and stays offstage until the climax, ill but not tragic. Written in response to two notes: 時計の音 'the hook never really hit' and 煙突の煙 'another story about a dead person, no twist'. THE TWIST IS RECOVERABLE FROM FACTS ON THE PAGE: 千秋's 卵焼き are sweet and 葵 likes them sweet (p5, said as an argument he wins); 葵 has never washed her own glass (p3, said as a habit); the hospital is next to the school (p7, said as a reproach); she comes home after seven 'with friends'. The climax realisation is three short observed facts (the box on the blanket, 千秋 eating with 葵's chopsticks, 千秋 washing the box at the room's sink), not one complex sentence. The turn is the one line 砂糖は、どのくらい入れるんだ, the first time he asks anyone how to do something; the text does not say so. NAMES: 由美 was the Gate 2 name and splits 由+美 in Ichiran, so the wife became 千秋, which segments whole and fits a woman born in the early 1980s. Peeked words reused on purpose: 渡す, 返事, 黙る, 隣, 決める.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: a weekday at four, the father leaves work early with his wife's pyjamas and walks into her hospital room unannounced. 葵 sits on the bed in uniform; his 弁当箱 is open on the blanket with only the 卵焼き left; 千秋 is eating them with 葵's chopsticks. 葵 shuts the lid too late. 千秋 finishes and says 今日のは、ちょっと塩が多いね, then washes the empty box at the room's sink. 葵 has eaten none of his 卵焼き; 千秋 has eaten all of them; the clean box he was proud of was washed here. He cannot find whom to be angry at, sits down, and asks how much sugar. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: 千秋 goes into hospital for a few weeks; her husband, who has never cooked, takes over their thirteen-year-old's lunches; 葵 never says whether it is good, but the box comes home empty and washed, and he decides that means it is. WANT: run the house alone until she is back, with 葵 eating his food. NEED: he decides everything and never asks; asking 千秋 how would mean admitting the house is hers. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2 (pp1-5), II 3-6 (pp6-9), III 7-8 (pp10-16). BEATS: 1 first morning, 卵焼き 焦げる, salted like his mother's; he hands over the box, she takes it silently and leaves her glass in the sink as always (yes-but). 2 box comes home empty and washed, he is pleased; 千秋 on the phone: 葵は、甘いのが好きなのよ; he answers 卵焼きは塩だ。もう決めた and hangs up (no-and). 3 a week of mornings, fewer burns, always a clean box, always home after seven 'with friends'; he decides not to ask (yes-but). 4 美味しかったか; she answers only that the hospital is next to school and she can see her mother's room; he hears reproach and snaps (no-and). 5 he leaves work early unannounced with the pyjamas (yes-but). 6 CLIMAX as above; he asks how much sugar (no-and: the want is gone, and he asks). 7 one big spoon, a little salt too, 退院は来週; 葵 walks beside him home. 8 next morning, sugar burns, second one right; she takes the box without a reply; that night it comes home empty and unwashed, rice on the lid, and he washes it himself.

new_words.弁当箱: lunchbox — first met p2 taken off the shelf and packed, 棚から娘の弁当箱を出して…詰める; carries every evening's empty, washed box, the climax on the blanket, and the last unwashed one
new_words.卵焼き: rolled omelette — first met p1 being cooked, 卵焼きを作り始めた; salt against sugar is the plant, the climax and the last morning
new_words.焦げる: to burn, scorch — first met p1 as the first omelette going black; recurs as the burns getting fewer and as sugar making the first one burn again

stories.title: 六時五十分
stories._premise:
Level 1 (N5/N4 core), register epistolary, 15 pages (13 to 17), new_words 3, leech seeds and repeats default.

## CULTURE

PRACTICE (looked up, not recalled: jprime.jp Hakone rules explainer, Chubu University club blog, Sportiva and Red Bull Japan pages on 箱根駅伝; the story is a fictional, unnamed university team running a Hakone-type 正月 relay, 往路 only, January 2). Procedure as the story uses it:
1. 12/29 区間エントリー: each team registers ten 区間 runners and six 補欠 (alternates); the list goes up.
2. Race morning (start 8:00): 当日変更 is accepted until 6:50, one hour ten before the start. Only a 補欠 can be swapped (per the sources) with a registered 区間 runner, never two registered runners; at most four swaps a day. The team submits it (in the story, the 監督). After 6:50 it is closed.
3. Each 区間 ends at a 中継所 where the 襷 is handed hand to hand to the next runner. Club practice, invented for the story and not a race rule: the non-running 補欠 are posted to jobs at the 中継所, carrying the jackets and keeping the times.
4. 繰り上げスタート: when the leader passes a 中継所, the team's next runner must start when the clock reaches ten minutes (the first two 中継所 of the 往路, 鶴見 and 戸塚; twenty minutes at the others) even if the runner before has not arrived. He wears a white 襷 from the organisers instead of his own (the organisers' rule keeps the own 襷 at the goal 区間s of each day; the story does not use this). The team is not disqualified and the time gap is counted.
Not found in any source and therefore NOT used by the story: the 20 m 中継線 detail, what is done with a late runner's own 襷. The story never depends on either: the 襷 is handed over before the pistol.

PRESSURE: 先輩・後輩 and 察し, held in place by 迷惑. A 後輩 cannot ask a senior or the 監督 to take him off a 区間: the 2nd-year ace saying he cannot run is a burden on a 4th-year's last race and on the chain, so he can only leave a hint and a request (内緒) and wait to be understood. A 4th-year 補欠 cannot ask for the 区間 or say his own foot hurts: a 補欠 who asks is 出しゃばり, and a hurt 補欠 is no 補欠. Both unsayable needs are "my foot hurts".

VOICES (written voices; this is an epistolary story and the only speech is writing):
- 松田 (4th year, 補欠 for four years, born about 2004): 俺, 常体 with 〜だ 〜な 〜ぞ, calls 青山 by surname without さん, writes です・ます only to the 監督.
- 青山 (2nd year, the ace, 2nd 区間): 僕, です・ます always, 松田さん, 監督, short and correct. His hesitation is his politeness.
- 監督 (about fifty): pinned notes only; bare imperatives 〜こと 〜しろ, no first person, surnames without さん. His rules note is the only place the 繰り上げ rule is stated.
- 高橋 (3rd year, 3rd 区間 runner, receives the 襷): never writes; appears only in 松田's race-day lines. 常体 in the one line quoted.
Names: all four surnames segment whole in Ichiran and fit men born 2002 to 2005 (surnames only).
Register shift as VOICES: 松田 plain with 青山 and polite to the 監督, 青山 polite upward, 監督 bare. The turn is a plain-form 松田 and a polite-form 青山 trading one line each on one page.

SEASON: 一月二日. The race cannot move: 往路 is a 正月 institution, the 寮 is half empty because families are away (the team stays), it is dark and below freezing at 6:40, hands are cold on the pen, and the 6:50 deadline is a dawn deadline. Season is the clock's setting, not a heading.

ABSENT: 沿道 crowds and flags, the TV commentary, standings and times as ranks (kept: only gaps in minutes and seconds, because the story runs on the clock), family at home and the 正月 meal (cut on purpose: a letter from a mother is the obvious epistolary item and would split attention; one line mentions the 寮's お雑煮), 襷の重み speeches and OB (cut: that is the stated theme, the story shows the 襷 being handed and nothing else), 5区's mountain and the 復路 (cut: only the 戸塚-type 中継所 with the ten-minute clock), the 湿布 and physio room (kept as one line of ice).

CARRIED: on known words: 先輩 後輩 監督 部員 寮 練習 大会 正月 足 痛い 靴 渡す 返事 隣 内緒 時間 分 秒 ノート 待つ 走る 洗う 朝 夜 氷 etc. New: 襷, 区間, 補欠 (the budget of 3). Not said at all, because unknown and not paid for: 駅伝, 箱根, 中継所, 走者, 順位, 先頭 (uses 一番前 or 一番早い人, 渡す場所, 走る人, 大会). 繰り上げ is never named; it is stated as an action in the 監督's note: after ten minutes the waiting runner runs without waiting, in a white 襷.

## CLIMAX
At the hand-off place after the second stretch, in the January cold. B has just handed the sash (襷) to C with forty-one seconds left on the ten-minute clock, having run the last two hundred metres on a foot he has hidden from the trainer and the coach (監督), and is sitting on the kerb beside A, who is there as an alternate (補欠) keeping the times in the club notebook (ノート). Neither says a word aloud. B writes one line and passes the notebook: which of A's shoes is worn down, and since when. A takes the pen and writes beneath it, in plain form: the left one, since the autumn of his first year, four years; the morning laps (朝の走り) were so nobody would see him run on it. That is the whole scene. What it reverses: four years of the cheerful alternate who was "too slow" (補欠 is slow, his joke) were four years of a hidden foot, and B, the one person who has been asking after feet, has known since the shoe-washing duty. The 6:49 silence the reader has already seen gets its second reason by being the same silence A was keeping about himself.

## AFTERWORD (full spoiler)
A fourth-year who has been the cheerful alternate for four years ends every notebook entry by asking the second-year ace about his foot, and gets "I'm fine" back. On New Year's morning the ace leaves the truth in the notebook, with a request for secrecy (内緒) and nothing else: a 後輩 cannot ask a 先輩 or the coach to take him off a stretch, he can only leave a thing where one person will find it before 6:50. The alternate has one chance in four years to be given a stretch, the swap, and keeping the secret is the same as giving it up; at 6:49 he writes "understood" and the list goes up unchanged. The ace runs on the hurt foot and gets the sash across with forty-one seconds to spare. On the kerb the ace asks the question back about a worn shoe, and the alternate answers it in writing: his own foot, four years, hidden by an early lap nobody saw. The alternate's one question was never about the ace alone, and the ace had known about the shoe all along. The last entry is the nightly question again, and this time the answer is "it hurts" (痛いです).

## PREMISE
A university relay team's club ノート is kept on the 寮 shelf, where the 4th-year 補欠 writes the night's notes and ends every entry with the same question to the 2nd-year ace, and gets the same polite answer. The relay starts at eight on New Year's morning, and the team's last chance to change its line-up closes at 6:50.

## ANCHOR
The shared ノート (a passed notebook with dated, timed entries) is the form; the 区間 hand-off and the two clocks (6:50 and ten minutes) are the engine. New words (3): 襷 (hand-offs, the white 襷, the climax), 区間 (the list, the swap, the climax), 補欠 (松田 is one for four years; the swap). Recurrence floor: max(2, round(300/150)) = 2 each; planned 5 to 8 each.

## WANT
A: to run one stretch (区間) before he graduates, in one clause: get his name on the stretch list for the New Year relay (正月).

## NEED
A is the one who is easy to be around, and in four years he has never asked for anything for himself, because an alternate (補欠) who asks is out of place (出しゃばり).

## SHAPE
Three-act. Act I beats 1-2 (about pp 1-4), Act II beats 3-5 (pp 5-11), Act III beats 6-7 (pp 12-15).

## BEATS (built backward from the climax; each with its honest join to the next)
1. (12/29 and 12/31) The coach (監督) pins the stretch list (区間): B on the second stretch, A first among the alternates (補欠) for a fourth year. A's evening entry in the club notebook (ノート) is chores and a joke (alternates are slow), and ends "B, your foot?" (足は？); B answers "I'm fine" (大丈夫です) and, politely, adds that A's left shoe is worn on one side and should be replaced (the shoe-washing duty, 靴の当番); A: "still runs" (まだ走れる), and that he runs every morning at 6:30. [no-and: the list went up without him and the one concern shown is turned aside.] JOIN: だから the coach sets the morning's rules.
2. (1/1) The coach's note in his bare voice: the line-up can be changed (当日変更) only until 6:50, and after ten minutes the waiting runner starts in a white sash (白い襷) without waiting. A is posted to the hand-off place to carry jackets and keep the times in the notebook, which goes with him. A: "understood" (了解), then again "your foot?", again "I'm fine". [yes-but: he has a job at the race and not a place in it.] JOIN: しかし, in the dark the next morning the answer is not the same.
3. (1/2, 6:32, B, notebook on the dormitory shelf) B's entry, left where A will find it after his morning run: my foot hurts (痛いです), I may not be able to run, please keep it secret (内緒にしてください), until 6:50. He has hidden it from the trainer and the coach. [no-and: the entry that asks for nothing is the request.] JOIN: だから A comes in from his laps and finds it.
4. (1/2, 6:41 to 6:51, A) He writes: the start of a note to the coach ("Coach, B's foot"), the next line "erased" (消した), the stamped times 6:48 and 6:49, then "To B. Understood. It stays secret" (内緒だ). He chooses to obey the request. 6:50 passes; the coach's list goes up at 6:55 with no change. [no-and: the chance to be given a stretch is in front of him and is the thing the request asks him to refuse.] JOIN: だから the race starts without him.
5. (1/2, 10:08 to 10:17, A at the hand-off place, notebook) Timed entries to B, who cannot read them yet: the fastest runner passes at 10:08, the ten minutes end at 10:18, C is waiting, B is not here, 10:16, the white sash is brought out, and the sash (襷) is handed over at 10:17:19 with forty-one seconds left. [yes-but: the chain holds and B goes down on the kerb.] JOIN: しかし, nobody has a word, and the notebook is open on A's knee.
6. CLIMAX as above. [no-and: the secret A kept for B is the one he has been keeping for himself, and nothing can be undone.] JOIN: だから one more line, that night.
7. (1/2, night) The nightly entry, A's: "B, your foot?" B: "It hurts" (痛いです). End on the entry.

## PLANTS and what each does at the time
- "Your foot?" / "I'm fine" (nightly): a senior's ritual and a junior's politeness; payoff: it is code, and the last entry answers it otherwise.
- Left shoe worn on one side (beat 1): a shoe-duty chore with a senior's stubborn answer; payoff: B's question in the climax.
- Morning run at 6:30 (beat 1): a fourth-year's discipline; payoff: A is out of the house when B leaves the note, and the laps are the hiding place for the foot.
- 6:50 (beat 2, stated as admin): paperwork and the premise's clock; payoff: beat 4.
- "Alternates are slow" (beat 1): a self-deprecating joke; payoff: reversed in the climax.
(The two pairs of socks were cut after the critic's note: they were the loudest clue.)
stories._gate: Gate 2 passed on round 3 of 3. The author's own pre-panel sheet went to the guesser three times: round 1 and round 2 were sent back because PREMISE and NEED leaked the situation (round 1 PREMISE named the note and the foot; round 2 said one entry was different), both rewritten; round 3 still returned 'partly', which the critic judged the unavoidable cost of stating a flaw (never asks) and not a real leak, and none of the three guesses landed on the climax in mechanism (the nearest, he never asks and the deadline passes, matches beat 4). Locator placed it in a Japanese university relay on 2 January from the rules and the seniority order; transplanter had beats 3 to 5 and the climax at BREAKS and the need said aloud in the moved version, naming 出しゃばり held by 迷惑 through 察し and 先輩・後輩 as the pressure lost. Critic PASS conditional on six edits, all applied before drafting: climax stripped of B's explanation of the note and its repeated last line, the motive at 6:49 fixed as obeying the request, the socks plant cut as too loud, beats 1 and 2 merged, the official character and the swap limits cut, leader time moved to 10:08 and the arithmetic fixed. Practice researched in sources (Hakone rules explainers on jprime.jp, Chubu University club blog, Sportiva and Red Bull Japan pages): 区間エントリー of ten plus six 補欠 on 12/29, 当日変更 until 6:50 for an 8:00 start and only 補欠 for a registered runner, 繰り上げ ten minutes at 鶴見 and 戸塚 and twenty at the others with an organiser's white 襷. Not found, so not used: the 20 m line, and what happens to a late runner's own 襷. The club-practice jobs of the 補欠 at the relay point, the shoe-washing rota, a notebook on the 寮 shelf and the 監督 pinning the list in the 寮 are invented and flagged as such. Vocabulary: 駅伝, 中継所, 繰り上げ, 走者, 順位 and 先頭 are unknown, so the story says 渡す場所 (relay point), 一番早い人, 次の人 and the coach's description of the white 襷; two draft readers called these generic and exposition-heavy. Draft stage: two Japanese-only readers and one English-only reader, naturalness 7.5 and 7.5; all three picked 痛いです as the ending, as intended; readers named 先輩・後輩 and the silent keeping of 内緒 but not 察し or 迷惑, so the pressure is partly delivered as endurance and loyalty; one reader read the 6:30 morning run as a stated motive and it was cut to 朝は、まだ誰もいない。 Fixes from the readers: stiff ことができる removed from the coach, the arithmetic line fixed, one connective cut, one blank line added. voice.py is not meaningful on this story because the headers dominate the ending counts. Dialogue percent is zero by form (no 「」), so --turns has nothing to print.

new_words.襷: relay sash — first met p4 in the coach's note, in the action 白い襷で走り出す; carries the hand-over, the white sash, and the climax's forty-one seconds
new_words.区間: stretch of the relay — first met p1 in the pinned list, 区間の紙を寮の玄関に貼った; carries the list, the swap before 6:50, and the second stretch
new_words.補欠: alternate runner — first met p1 as the name at the top of the alternates, 補欠の一番上には、また俺の名前がある; carries the joke, the swap and the post at the hand-off place

stories.title: 八月の絵日記
stories._premise:
Level 1 (N5/N4 core), register epistolary, 15 pages (14 to 16), new_words 3, leech seeds 4, repeats default. Set at Gate 1 as a re-test of the register after 六時五十分 ★2 ("I was expecting diary or journal entries from one person's perspective"). Peeked words reused on purpose: 返事, 紙, 字, 内緒. Gate 2 passed on round 3 of 3; the round-3 critic's six fix-while-there items are applied below.

TITLE: 八月の絵日記

## CULTURE

PRACTICE: 夏休みの絵日記, as a 二年生 kept it in the summer of 1983 (昭和58年). Looked up, not recalled. The procedure the story runs on:
1. 7/20, the last day of term (終業式). The 担任 sends the summer homework (夏休みの宿題) home. One item is the 絵日記, to be kept every day of the holiday, 7/21 to 8/31. Source and its era: a Yokohama school newsletter of 2026-08-28 in which the vice-principal describes the 低学年 絵日記 he found at his family home in 北九州, which recorded every day's events from 7/21 to 8/31 (毎日の出来事が記されていました); it does not say how its pages were laid out. A vice-principal now is roughly 45 to 58, which puts that diary somewhere between the mid-1970s and the late 1980s, in a western city with a 9/1 term start: the nearest source to 1983 found. Schools today set one to three loose sheets, which cannot carry a story told in daily entries; that is the first reason for 1983. In the story's notebook each day has its own page; that layout is the story's, not the source's.
2. Each page has a row of boxes the child fills in herself, 月・日・曜日・天気, with the weather written as 晴れ, 曇り or 雨 (or a mix such as 晴れ一時雨); a picture box, drawn in crayon, which cannot be rubbed out; and a few ruled lines for three to five sentences, written in です・ます, as low-grade 作文 is. A notebook of this kind is sold for grades 1 to 3. The story makes no claim about how many pages it has beyond one for each day: when 陽子 runs out of lines on 8/31 she goes on over the back of the page and onto sheets of plain paper folded into the notebook, as a child does.
3. The child writes it at home, meant to be daily. A parent looks it over at home before it goes in. Present-day school letters ask parents to check 誤字脱字, and to check a daily diary every day; this is assumed for 1983.
4. Children fall behind and fill in the missed days at the end of the holiday. The weather is the field nobody remembers, and parents are drafted to look it up in the old newspapers (新聞をひっくり返す). The newspaper is the only place a family in 1983 can find a past day's weather; that is the second reason for the year. Which weather: the morning paper's weather map, with a forecast mark beside each city's name. 陽子 copies a mark from that morning's map, and on 8/31 her mother reads the marks off the same maps, so the story compares like with like. Every capital's mark shown on a page has been checked against JMA's observed daytime record for Tokyo, 1983, and agrees with it.
5. 9/1, the first day of term (始業式). The child hands the notebook to the 担任 (先生に渡す), who reads every page, writes in red (赤ペン) and gives it back. Schools today pin loose sheets up in the 廊下 in September; a bound notebook cannot be pinned up, and the story does not claim it is. That other people might see it is the mother's fear, not a thing the story shows.
Other institutions the sheet leans on, each checked as far as a source allowed: 単身赴任, in its 1980s form, a father posted alone while the family keeps the house, which is the third reason for the year; お盆, 8/13 to 8/16, when families go to the 田舎 and fathers posted away come home; the school pool, open in the summer holiday; the cost of a long-distance call (400 yen for three minutes between Tokyo and Osaka on a weekday in 1988, against 10 yen for a local call). 1983 is also the Showa peak year for divorce. The proposed pressure, 世間体, is kept.

PRESSURE: 世間体. Her father moved out on 7/20. Her mother has told the street, the school and 陽子 that he has been posted alone to the head office in Tokyo (単身赴任, said to 陽子 as 東京にてんきん). His parents in the 田舎 know the truth. In 1983 a separation was something a family kept from the street, and the 絵日記 is where it would get out, because the 担任 reads every page. So her mother has a rule, first 「おとうさんのことは、書かないの」 and then 「うちのことも、書かないの」, and an eraser (消しゴム) that enforces it every night. The rule names writing; 陽子 extends it to her pictures herself (おとうさんの絵をかくのも、やめます), so he is out of the pictures as well as the sentences. What it forbids 陽子: to write, draw or say anything about her father beyond "Tokyo, for work"; and so to ask whether he is coming back, or why there is no call and no card, because asking opens the subject the whole house has shut. She keeps the rule by 察し: she reads her mother's face and stays quiet. An American eight-year-old would ask "Is Dad coming home?" in one line, and her mother would not have invented a posting for the neighbours in the first place.

VOICES:
- 陽子 (｜陽子《ようこ》), 8, 二年生, born 1975 (陽子 was a top-ten girls' name every year from 1966 to 1982 and first in 1974). The only writer; everyone else reaches the page as speech she reports. In the diary: わたし, です・ます throughout, short sentences ending 〜ました, 〜でした, 〜です, other people's words given as 「…」と言いました, and the 担任 addressed directly once or twice (先生、…). Kanji only from the first- and second-grade lists (天気 先生 学校 雨 空 字 赤 見る 東京 七月 八月 九月 and so on; 東 and 京 are second-grade in today's list, and whether they were in the 1977 list is unconfirmed, so the drafting rule stands that any kanji not checked against the 1977 grade list goes into kana; she copies 東京 from print either way); everything else in hiragana (しんぶん でんわ ないしょ へんじ てんきん おかあさん おとうさん). Three words are in kanji because she copies them from print: 絵日記 off the notebook's cover, お盆 off the kitchen calendar, and 八月, which is first-grade kanji anyway. This is also what the reader's segmentation needs, since えにっき splits え+にっき and おぼん splits お+ぼん in Ichiran. Her own name appears only in her mother's quoted speech; 陽子 needs its annotation because Ichiran reads it ようし. Her own reported speech is plain: 〜だよ, 〜の？. She calls her parents おかあさん and おとうさん and the teacher 先生.
- Her mother, about 36, born about 1947, 専業主婦, unnamed (a child's diary names its parents by role). To 陽子: plain form, rules given as 〜の (「書かないの」), and 〜のよ, 〜なさい, 〜でしょ; she calls herself おかあさん. She calls her daughter 陽子, bare, every time she gives a rule, and 陽子ちゃん once, on the living-room floor on 8/31. That shift is the echo of the turn, not the turn: the turn is 陽子's question. To others (the 田舎 on the phone): です・ます, bowing.
- Her father, about 40, born about 1943, a salaryman, unnamed. Never on the page in the present. Quoted once from 陽子's memory, from his breakfast habit of reading the paper's weather aloud. Plain 〜だ and a bare imperative, the Showa father's register to a child.
- The 担任, unnamed. Never speaks in the present; quoted once from last year's red ink, in です・ます: 「この日は、雨でしたよ」.
- His mother in the 田舎 is only the other end of a phone call and does not speak on the page.
Region: an unnamed city in western Japan, several hours from Tokyo, with the term starting 9/1. The family moved there for his company when 陽子 was small, as company families did, and her mother grew up near Tokyo, so the house speaks standard Japanese while the street outside does not. It also makes the cover believable: a company man from such a family being posted back to the head office alone is the most ordinary thing in the world.

SEASON: The summer holiday, 7/21 to 8/31, is the span of the practice itself, so the story exists only inside it. お盆, 8/13 to 8/16, is when a father posted away comes home and the family goes to the 田舎: the want has its date, and it fails on that date. 8/31 is the last-night cram that brings out the newspapers, and it is where the climax happens. The weather itself is summer's subject, the evening showers and the heat, and the diary's weather box is the anchor. The story cannot move to another month without losing the practice, the want's date and the climax.

ABSENT: In: お盆, as the date of the want and the phone call to the 田舎; the school pool; the summer's newspapers tied with string by the front door and kept back from the paper collection (ちり紙交換) until the diary is done; the eraser; an evening shower. The picture (絵): every page has one, and 陽子 extends the rule to it herself, so she never draws him. She draws the paper on the breakfast table, the pool, the calendar. The picture is the biggest thing on the page and the first thing her mother looks at; the weather box is two words at the top that her mother never reads. That is why he goes into the box and not into a drawing. The card (はがき): no card comes from him either, only no call, and her mother says the company keeps him busy. 陽子 notes it and asks nothing. Friends: the school pool is full of classmates, and the diary shows them only as a crowd (みんな). It names no friend, on purpose: a named friend would have to be resolved, and would ask what every child asks in August, whether her father is coming home for お盆, so 陽子 stays out of their talk for the same reason she keeps to the rule. The house is their own, bought in the city, and not 社宅: in 社宅 the neighbours are his colleagues' families and the cover would not last a week, and a bought house is also the ordinary 1980s reason for 単身赴任. Her mother's parents (実家) near Tokyo have been told the same posting; going to them this summer was out of the question, because a family in Tokyo for お盆 would be expected to see him. Neither is on the page.
Out, on purpose: the mid-holiday school day (登校日; in western Japan today often a 平和登校日 around 8/6). If her school had one, it falls in the week the story does not show, between 8/2 and 8/9. It is left unshown so that the 担任 is met once, as the reader on 9/1, and the notebook stays at home until then. Also out: the 暑中見舞い a child might send the 担任, because it would be a second written channel to the teacher and the story keeps one; ラジオ体操, which is the anchor of 号令 and would put neighbours into every morning; the other homework (夏休みの友, 自由研究, 読書感想文), which would split the domain; 盆踊り, 夏祭り and 花火, the big-event pages a diary hunts for, because the story is about what she may not write; 迎え火, 送り火, 仏壇 and 墓参り, because the family's お盆 rites happen at the 田舎 they do not go to this year, and that absence is the beat; neighbours in person, so that no character is used once and dropped; 甲子園 and 8/15 on the television, which would be season markers and not this story's subject; the father himself, who is never on the page; the separation's paperwork, an adult procedure outside a child's window; the pool card the parent stamps each morning, one parent's check too many beside the diary's own; the corridor display, which belongs to today's loose sheets and not to a 1983 notebook.

## CLIMAX

8/31, at night, the last night of the holiday, on the living-room floor. The diary has been blank since 8/16. Her mother has untied the summer's newspapers (古新聞, kept back from the paper collection, ちり紙交換) and laid them out on the floor by date, to fill in the weather for the fifteen empty pages, as parents do on the last night (夏休みの最後の日). She finds the 8/16 paper and reads 陽子 the mark beside their own city on the weather map (新聞の天気の地図): cloudy. 陽子 does not write it. "No, not that one. The capital." (「ちがうよ。東京」) Asked what she means, she points to the capital's name on the map: since 7/22 she has copied the capital's mark into the box on every page. "But it's in the paper." (「でも、しんぶんに書いてあるよ」) "I didn't write about Dad. Only the weather." (「おとうさんのことは、書いてないよ。天気だけ」) Her mother turns back through the diary against the papers, and every box from 7/22 holds the capital's mark for that day, on many days not their own. She stops at the 8/9 page, where the box says sunny above the evening shower and the last line reads "I'll show it at the holiday" with nobody named (「お盆に、見せます」). She reads it aloud and covers her face with her hands (手で、かおをかくす), and cries on the floor without hiding it, the first time 陽子 has seen it. 陽子 asks the first question she has asked all summer: "Is Dad really in the capital?" (「おとうさん、ほんとうに東京にいるの？」) Her mother calls her by the soft form of her name (陽子ちゃん), which she has not used all summer, and answers: he never went; he lives in an apartment by the station two stops down the line (二つ先のえき); he is not coming home; his mother in the country (田舎) knows. What 陽子 pays: the diary she kept for him carries his weather on every page, and he was never under it; and the homecoming it was kept for is not late, it is never.
TWIST: Kept back: the weather in the box on every page from 7/22 is the capital's, copied each morning off the newspaper's weather map so that her father's weather would be in the diary when he read it at the holiday; and her father was never in the capital. 陽子 states the first half herself, in speech, as soon as her mother reads her the wrong mark ("No, not that one. The capital." and "Only the weather."; 「ちがうよ。東京」, 「天気だけ」). Her mother states the second half, in speech, after 陽子's question ("He isn't in the capital."; 「おとうさんは、東京にはいないの」). 陽子 writes both into the 8/31 entry in plain words. Each understands what she is saying as she says it.

## PREMISE

Summer 1983, in a city a long way from Tokyo. 陽子, a second-grader, keeps the 絵日記 her class hands in on September 1st, a page for every day of the holiday, and her mother looks over each page at night. Her father has been posted to his company's head office in Tokyo, and 陽子 is keeping the diary for him to read when he comes home at お盆.

## ANCHOR

The 絵日記 page, and above all its row of boxes at the top, 月・日・曜日・天気: every entry opens on it, and the story turns on the weather box. A ritual rides with it, the morning newspaper's weather map read the way her father read it. New words carried, the brief's 3, each needing at least 2 occurrences: 絵日記, first met on page 1 in an action, as she writes the weather into the first page of the new 絵日記 (絵日記の一ページ目に天気を書きました), and on most pages after; 八月 and お盆, both first met in a sentence on 8/1 in one action, as her mother turns the kitchen calendar over to 八月 and circles お盆 (カレンダーを八月にして、お盆に丸をつけました), then 八月 in every August heading and the climax, and お盆 at the want, the line with no name in it, the day itself and the climax. (The 8/1 heading, the date she writes in the box, sits one line above that action.)

## WANT

To show her father the diary when he comes home for the mid-August holiday (お盆).

## NEED

She reads a grown-up's face, works out what is wanted, and does it before anyone has to say so.

## SHAPE

Three-act. Act I is beats 1 to 2 (pages 1 to 2), Act II beats 3 to 6 (pages 3 to 8), Act III beats 7 to 9 (pages 9 to 15): the cram and the climax on pages 9 to 12, the night's cost on pages 13 to 14, the morning on page 15. About three pages follow the climax, so the room after it is a third act's and not a second act's.
On time moving in one direction: a dated diary marches by default, and the shape breaks the march with the practice's own habits. The pages shown come in clusters with jumps between them: 7/21 and 7/22 together, then ten days missing, then 8/1 and 8/2 together, a week missing, 8/9, then 8/12 and 8/13 together, then 8/15. Then comes a fifteen-day hole she left blank, the habit every child has, and the reader feels the dates stop. Then a single night takes most of the second half, and in it the summer is read backward twice: her mother turning the pages back against the papers, and 陽子 rubbing out the capital's weather. In drafting, neither backward reading is a list of dates. Each is told as one act with one page surfacing in it: the 8/9 page for her mother, the first page for 陽子.
Which text the reader reads: each page as 陽子 wrote it that evening, before her mother read it. A line or a page her mother then rubbed out is still shown as written, and the reader learns it went from a later page shown, where 陽子 sets down in a line of her own what was rubbed out and what her mother said; that line is about the house, so it goes in its turn. Not every erasure is reported singly. The 8/9 page states her mother's nightly practice in general (anything about him or about the house is rubbed out), which covers the 7/22 opening and the unshown days. The ones the story needs are reported one by one: 7/21's line on 7/22; the 8/2 page on its own rewrite, and her mother's words that night on 8/9; and, on 8/12, which lines of 8/9 went and the one that was left. After お盆 her mother rubs out the lines about him on 8/12 and 8/13 like any others, and nothing reports it: the 8/15 page is about nothing, and what her mother reads on 8/31 is the notebook as it stands. The 8/2 rewrite reads as a rewrite on its own: it opens by saying the day is being written again, that her mother rubbed out what was there, and that the paper has gone thin; the reason arrives on 8/9 (withhold, never confuse). In the notebook every rubbed-out line survives as the groove her pencil pressed into the paper, which the eraser thins and does not take (紙がうすくなる, beat 3): the reader is reading what the grooves still hold. A rewritten page (8/2) is shown after the page it replaced. What her mother reads on 8/31 is the notebook as it stands: every box, and only the lines she let stand.

## BEATS

ACT I (beats 1 to 2, pages 1 to 2)
1. 7/21 (木), box: sunny, their own city's weather, the only page that is. The first page of the picture diary (絵日記). Her father left yesterday with his big bag for the head office in the capital (本社; 東京にてんきん; the house's story is a solo posting, 単身赴任), and 陽子 writes the capital's name, proud that she can (東京という字). Nobody read the weather out of the morning paper at breakfast (新聞の天気), so she did it herself, the way he always did. She draws the paper on the table. That night her mother looks at the picture, reads the sentences one word at a time, and rubs out (消しゴムで消す) the line about him patting her head at the front door (玄関): "You don't put your father in it." (「おとうさんのことは、書かないの」) YES-BUT: the diary is begun and she has taken over his weather, but her mother takes him out of it.
2. 7/22 (金), box: cloudy. She means to obey: the page opens by setting down what her mother said and her promise, "I won't write about Dad." (「おとうさんのことは、もう書きません」), and that opening is rubbed out the same night, since even a promise not to write about him is about him. The rest is about the school pool (学校のプール), ten metres; she means to swim twenty-five before the holiday is out. Last summer the class teacher (担任) wrote beside a weather she had guessed, in red (赤い字): "It rained this day." (「この日は、雨でしたよ」) So this year the weather comes from the paper, because what is printed in the paper cannot be wrong (「しんぶんの天気は、まちがいません」). From today the mark she copies is the capital's, and nothing on the page says which city it is. YES-BUT: she has a way to keep the box right and a goal for the pool, but the diary she is keeping for him may not have him in it.
(end of Act I)
ACT II (beats 3 to 6, pages 3 to 8)
3. 8/1 (月), box: rain; 8/2 (火), box: cloudy. On 8/1 her mother turns the kitchen calendar (カレンダー) over to August (八月) and circles the mid-August holiday (お盆に丸をつける): he comes home then (お盆の帰省), and 陽子 will go to the station to meet him (むかえに行く) and show him the diary. On 8/2 she writes that her mother sat in the kitchen late with the light off (だいどころで、でんきをつけないで). Her mother rubs out the whole page, till the paper goes thin (紙がうすくなる), and makes her write it again (書き直す): "You don't write about our house either. The teacher reads this." (「うちのことも、書かないの。先生も読むのよ」) Both versions are shown, the rubbed-out one first; her mother's words reach the reader on 8/9. The summer's newspapers are tied with string by the front door (紐でしばる) and kept back from the paper collection (ちり紙交換) until the diary is done. NO-AND: the want has its date, but the rule widens from him to the whole house, and the page has room for nothing but the pool and the box.
4. 8/9 (火), box: sunny. Twenty-five metres at last. After the pool an evening shower soaks the shirts on the line at home (夕方、雨がふってきて; シャツがぬれる). The page also sets down her mother's nightly practice and her words from 8/2, and that no call and no card (はがき) have come from him; her mother has said the capital is far, calls cost money, and the company keeps him busy (東京は遠いから、でんわは高いの). Its last line is "I'll show it at the holiday." (「お盆に、見せます」), which leaves out to whom, because she may not write him (the dropped subject). That night her mother rubs out the lines about him and the house and, for the first time, leaves a line about him standing: 「お盆に、見せます」, which has no name in it. She says he may be too busy to come this year (いそがしいかもしれない). 陽子 gives no reply (へんじをしない) and sets the remark down on her next page. YES-BUT: she has the thing to show and her mother lets that line stand, but he may not come, and his name cannot go beside it.
5. 8/12 (金), box: sunny; 8/13 (土), box: sunny, rain at times. On 8/12 she gets ready to meet him at the station tomorrow. On 8/13, the holiday (お盆), no father comes; there is no trip to his parents' house in the country (田舎) this year. Her mother phones the country and bows over and over (でんわで、あたまを下げる) to someone who cannot see her, and 陽子 writes it down as a strange thing. NO-AND: the want fails on its own date, and the only answer in the house is a bow on the phone.
6. 8/15 (月), box: rain. One page about nothing (「きょうは、なにもしませんでした」). After it, the pages are blank. NO-AND: the diary has lost its reader, so she stops keeping it, and fifteen days go unwritten.
(end of Act II)
ACT III (beats 7 to 9, pages 9 to 15)
7. CLIMAX, 8/31 (水) at night, the last-night cram (夏休みの最後の日), on the living-room floor, as on the CLIMAX line. The summer's papers laid out by date; the 8/16 paper; their own city's mark on the weather map (天気のちず), cloudy; 陽子 asks for the capital's instead ("No, not that one. The capital."), says it is in the paper, and says she never wrote about him, only the weather (天気だけ), and that the weather was her secret (天気のことは、ないしょでした). Her mother finds the capital's mark in every box from 7/22, stops at the 8/9 page and its line with nobody named (「お盆に、見せます」), reads it aloud, covers her face and cries in front of her. 陽子 asks her first question of the summer. Her mother, using the soft form of her name (陽子ちゃん), says he never went, he lives by the station two stops down the line (二つ先のえき), he is not coming home, and the country knows (田舎). NO-AND for the want: he is not coming at all. The need is faced: she asks.
8. 8/31, later that night. Fifteen blank pages need filling. 陽子 takes the papers herself and copies their own city's mark into each box, because two stations away is under the same weather (同じ天気); under each box she puts a quick picture and a line or two of what she and her mother can remember, as crammed pages are. Then she goes back through the written pages and, with her mother reading out each day's mark from the floor, rubs out every capital's weather with the eraser (消しゴム) and writes home's over it, until she reaches the first page, the only one that was right. Last, she writes the 8/31 entry: what happened tonight, in plain words, over the back of the 8/31 page and onto sheets of paper folded into the notebook. She writes it because the 8/31 page is due and she has stopped keeping the house's secret for it, and she leaves it for her mother to read in the morning like every other page. In the diary 同じ天気 stays a plain fact about the weather and is not made into a reason. YES-BUT: the diary is complete and right, and there will be no red ink this year, but every page of his capital is gone, by her own hand, and she has written down the one thing the rule was for.
9. 9/1 (木), the first day of term (九月一日; 先生に出す), on the last folded sheet. Her mother reads last night's pages and rubs out nothing: "I'll talk to your teacher myself." (「先生には、おかあさんが話すからね」) This morning 陽子 does not open the paper. The last line: she wrote the weather by opening the window and looking at the sky (天気は、まどをあけて、空を見て書きました). YES-BUT: the diary goes in true and her mother takes the telling on herself, but there is no one now to show it to except the teacher, and the weather she writes from now on is her own.

## DRAFTING NOTES

Author, drafting stage, 2026-10-30: departures from the passed sheet made in the Japanese, each for Ichiran's segmentation or the known set, for the draft panel to weigh. The beats above carry the drafted wording where it changed.

TITLE: 一番いい場所

## CULTURE

### PRACTICE

花見の場所取り: holding the spot for a company's cherry-blossom party (会社の花見), as a small, old-fashioned company still does it. Looked up, not recalled. The procedure the story runs on:

1. The Japanese company year begins on 1 April, and new graduates start that day. In the week the cherries are at or just past full bloom, a department holds its 花見 on a weekday evening after work in a public park. At a small company it doubles as the welcome for that year's new hire (新人の歓迎). The welcome-party order is sourced (step 9); the doubling with the 花見 is common, and the 2023 Tokyo Shoko Research survey counts the two together, but I found no source that states it.
2. The newest employee is the organiser (幹事) for the day and does the 場所取り. Source: matcha-jp, "会社でのお花見の場合、大抵新入社員が幹事となって場所取りをする". financial-field describes the Showa scene: 朝早くから桜の見える良い場所にブルーシートを敷き新入社員が待機.
3. He goes early in the morning. A neighbour of a park, quoted by bengo4 (弁護士ドットコム): 朝8時前から、ブルーシートの陣取り合戦が始まります. He spreads a blue tarp (ブルーシート) only as large as the group needs; claiming too much is bad manners (matcha-jp). The usual company tarp is the large size that seats about ten.
4. He weighs the corners with stones (石) or his own pegs, and never drives pegs into a cherry's roots (matcha-jp).
5. Someone must stay on the sheet. At most venues the park staff remove an unattended blue sheet without hesitation: 警備員さんが容赦なくブルーシートを片付けてしまいます (matcha-jp). So the holder cannot leave it for the toilet or for food unless someone sits on it. Neighbouring holders watching each other's sheets (お互い様) is the story's assumption, not sourced. The posted sign in the story is invented; the removal is sourced.
6. The advice he reads: take a patch about 100 m from the toilets, 100mくらい離れているのがちょうどいい; closer means smell and noise, farther is inconvenient (matcha-jp). 三浦 follows it to the letter: he paces exactly a hundred metres from the toilet, a hundred and thirty steps. The department's usual tree breaks the rule.
7. Bring something to pass the time; it is cold, at night especially (携帯カイロ) (matcha-jp).
8. The toilets at a 花見 park have queues; one report tells of more than a hundred people queuing at temporary toilets (livedoor news, summary only; the article itself is withdrawn). The story's park is a modest neighbourhood park with one public toilet, beside the bridge, and no temporary ones, and its evening queue is about twenty minutes. That geography is the story's.
9. The group arrives after work and takes off its shoes onto the sheet (靴を脱ぐ). A welcome party runs: opening word, 乾杯, 歓談, then the new hire introduced (All About's welcome-party order: 開会の言葉、はじめの挨拶、乾杯、歓談、新入社員の紹介と挨拶; the same person may give the address and the 乾杯, so the 部長 leads it). The new hire pours for his seniors (お酌), top rank first: お酌は主賓や上席など立場が上の人から順番にまわる (Mynavi News); a new graduate sits at the lowest place and watches for empty glasses (financial-field, 職場の飲み会で新卒は「お酌」や「グラスの空き」を気にするべきですか). A senior who wants no more covers his glass with his hand: general custom, not looked up.
10. Present-day context. The custom has declined and is widely called harassment (パワハラ) (financial-field; Global Voices, citing Nikkei 2013); 27.9% of firms held a 花見, welcome or social party in 2023 (Tokyo Shoko Research, via BCN Retail); some companies now forbid forced お酌 (Mynavi News). An All About writer argued that bosses use the preparation to quietly judge a new hire's competence (Global Voices: "surreptitiously evaluating your capability through your skill of preparing the feast"). 三浦 has read that last one.
11. The idiom. トイレが近い is everyday Japanese for needing the toilet often, "having a small bladder; having an overactive bladder" (JMdict 2831974, as Ichiran glosses it). トイレの近く means "near the toilet". Checked: Ichiran parses 「僕は、トイレが近いんです」, 「トイレが近いので」 and 「部長も、トイレが近いのだ」 as the idiom, and 「トイレの近くの、一番大きい桜だ」, 「トイレの近くなら、一日いられますね」 and 「ここは、トイレが近いですよ」 literally, while 「トイレが近いと、一日いられますね」 would parse as the idiom. The draft uses that split on purpose.
12. Bloom. Tokyo's normal full-bloom date is 31 March (JMA, 1991 to 2020 normals); in 2026 it was 28 March (weathernews, kumanichi). The story names no city and no year. The Friday of the new hire's first week falls just past full bloom, and the petals are coming down.

Invented, and said so: the 課長 holding the spot himself in the years the department had no new hire; the one public toilet beside the biggest tree; the sign on unattended sheets.

Unconfirmed: the 花見 doubling as the welcome (plausible, not found stated); neighbouring holders watching each other's sheets; the hand over the glass.

Sources: matcha-jp.com/jp/137; financial-field.com/household/entry-284987; financial-field.com/living/entry-236198; bengo4.com/c_5/n_5803; globalvoices.org/2013/04/24/japans-cherry-blossom-tradition-tests-rookie-employees; allabout.co.jp/gm/gc/493972; news.mynavi.jp/article/20211201-2196159; bcnretail.com/topics_detail9/20230419_324742.html; news.livedoor.com/article/detail/26210987; data.jma.go.jp/tokyo/shosai/news/pdf/2022/sakuramankai2022.pdf; kumanichi.com/articles/1974341.

### PRESSURE

面子. The 部長, ｜大野《おおの》, 63, has a small bladder (トイレが近い), and he will not let his own staff watch him go to the toilet again and again at the department's one party of the year. Each trip, he says he is going to look at the blossoms (「ちょっと、桜を見てくる」). The 課長, ｜石井《いしい》, has known for years and has kept it by choosing, every year, the big cherry by the bridge, on the side where the park's only toilet stands. He cannot tell anyone why, because the reason is the 部長's secret. On the night itself he cannot move the party either: the 部長 has just praised the new hire's spot in front of everyone, and moving would shame the new hire on his own welcome night. ｜三浦《みうら》, the new hire, is held by the same force from the other side. He cannot be seen by a superior to need anything or to get anything wrong, so he never asks why "the toilet side", never asks anyone to watch his sheet, lies to a stranger about where he went, and pours away her tea rather than refuse it or drink it.

What it forbids: the 部長 to say "I need the toilet"; the 課長 to say "we sit there for the 部長"; 三浦 to say "I need the toilet" or "why that tree?". The need is unspeakable because of it.

The American test: an American new hire would ask "why that tree?", or say "can you watch my tarp, I need the restroom". An American boss would say "I've got a small bladder, let's sit by the restrooms", and nobody would think twice. None of the story's silences would hold.

Secondary forces, named for the critic: 先輩・後輩 (a new hire does not question a 課長's instruction aloud, which is why 三浦 answers what he takes for a test silently instead of asking); 遠慮 (三浦 cannot refuse the young woman's tea or her offer).

### VOICES

- ｜三浦《みうら》, 22, born 2003. Grew up in a small town in the north and went to university in the same region, so this is the first spring he has spent anywhere the cherries bloom in early April. First job, in the 課 of a small stationery company (文房具の会社), in his first week. Narrator. First person 僕. Narration in plain form, earnest and over-exact: he counts steps, writes every instruction in his notebook (手帳) as terse notes with arrows and question marks (「トイレの近く → ×（百メートル）。わざと？ → 試験」), and scores himself. To the 課長 and the 部長: careful です・ます and stiff set phrases (「はい、承知しました」), and he addresses them by title only, 課長 and 部長, as a junior does. To the young woman, a stranger his own age: です・ます. Nobody at the company uses his given name.
- ｜石井《いしい》, the 課長, 48, born 1978. Terse and dry, and terse for a reason: he is carrying something he cannot say. Speaks in noun phrases, often without a verb (「橋の横の、一番大きい桜。トイレの近くだ」); plain form with 〜だ and 〜ぞ to juniors; first person 俺. Calls 三浦 「三浦」, bare. To the 部長: plain です・ます, 「部長」. Answers every message with one word, 「了解」. While he is worried he does not drink, and when 三浦 comes round with the beer he puts his hand over his glass.
- ｜大野《おおの》, the 部長, 63, born 1963. Loud, warm, sentimental in public, a master of 建前. Plain form with 〜ぞ, 〜な, 〜じゃないか; first person 俺. Calls 三浦 「新人」 all night and never by name; calls 石井 「石井」, bare. Loves his drink and says so (花見は、桜より酒だ, carried in 三浦's notebook from the day before). His set phrase is 「ちょっと、桜を見てくる」. Says the generous thing loudly and the true thing never.
- The young woman, about 22, a new hire at an insurance office (保険の会社), holding her own company's spot. Unnamed: 三浦 never learns her name. です・ます to him; practical, kind, and comfortable where he is rigid. Her particular habit: she has her own 場所取り list on a sheet of paper, the mirror of his notebook, and she ticks things off it with a pen as they come true (the toilet is near: ticked). She lets the people beside her watch her sheet, and she sees more than she says.
- The rest of the 課, four people, appear only as a group: they arrive, laugh, and carry things. The department is seven: the 部長, the 課長, 三浦 and the four.

Names: 三浦, 石井 and 大野 each segment whole in Ichiran (checked 2026-11-10); surnames only, so there is no given-name era to match. None appears in any story text. 号令's note records 石井 as renamed to 中島 for being unknown; today Ichiran keeps it whole. All three are outside the known set (have.py ✗), as most names are, so check.py will list them the way it listed 陽子 in 八月の絵日記. If a known name is wanted for one of them, 小林 is both known and whole; 佐藤 and 高橋 are known but split.

### SEASON

Early April, and only early April. The company year begins on 1 April, so a new hire exists only now, and the cherries are just past full bloom only now, so a 花見 exists only now; the story is the overlap. The petals are coming down: they stream across the sheet in the wind off the river all afternoon, and 三浦 brushes them off with his hand to keep the sheet clean for inspection without once looking up at the trees. The cold of a clear April evening after a mild day (花冷え, carried as 寒い and 冷える) is what drives everyone to drink and then to the toilet. At home in the north the cherries come out in May, and this is the first spring he has spent anywhere they bloom this early; the last sentence holds the first time he looks. The story cannot move: in any other month there is no 花見 and no new hire.

### ABSENT

In: the blue sheet and the stones on its corners; the rule that unattended sheets are taken away; the advice about a hundred metres from the toilets; the cold; the falling petals; shoes off onto the sheet; the 乾杯 led by the 部長; the 花見 as the new hire's welcome (新人の歓迎); the new hire pouring for his seniors (お酌), the 部長 first, and the 課長's hand over his glass; the toilet queue; the 課長's 「了解」; the new hire's notebook.

Out, on purpose:

- 入社式, earlier in the week, offstage; the notebook's page from the day before is the only scene from the office.
- The new hire's party trick (一発芸) and a self-introduction speech: a second set piece, and the 乾杯 already welcomes him.
- 二次会, and taking the rubbish home: both come after the story ends.
- Crows stealing food: a second comic thread competing with the first.
- Paid spot-holding services (場所取り代行).
- The harassment debate: it would make the 課長 a villain and the story an argument.
- 夜桜 lights and 提灯 by name (unknown words); the lights in the trees are carried by 明かり.
- Food stalls (屋台, unknown); 三浦 buys bread at a shop on the way back from the toilet.
- The 部長's condition named as an illness: no doctor, no 前立腺; the idiom carries it, and it stays a fact about an older man rather than a medical story.
- 三浦's family and his room: nobody phones; the story stays in one park.
- The 社長 and other departments.

### CARRIED

## CLIMAX

Night, on the department's blue sheet (ブルーシート) under the tree 三浦 chose that morning, exactly a hundred metres from the park's only toilet. The 部長 comes back from his second trip "to look at the blossoms" (「ちょっと、桜を見てくる」), cold, and sits on the edge of the sheet next to 三浦. As the new hire, 三浦 fills the 部長's glass (お酌, carried as コップにビールを入れる); it is his job to watch that glass, which is why he is watching it. Someone tells a joke and everyone turns toward it. 三浦, who has not been to the toilet since noon and cannot sit still, sees the 部長 tip the beer he has just poured out onto the grass behind him (草の上に流す) and lift the empty glass to his mouth.

It is exactly what 三浦 did with the young woman's tea at noon. He understands, and says it to himself in four short sentences: the 部長 did not go to look at the blossoms. The 部長 has a small bladder too (部長も、トイレが近いのだ). That is why the 課長 said near the toilet. It was never a test.

三浦 stands up in front of the whole department and says the thing he has hidden all day: 「すみません。僕は、トイレが近いんです。トイレの近くに、移ってもいいですか」 ("I'm sorry. I have a small bladder. Could we move near the toilet?") The department laughs. The 部長 laughs loudest: 「なんだ、早く言え。新人が我慢するな」 ("Then why didn't you say so! A new boy shouldn't hold it in.") The 課長 looks at 三浦 for a long moment, then stands up and lifts the box of beer without a word.

What 三浦 pays: the best spot in the park, which was his whole day; the 部長's praise, given earlier that evening in front of everyone; and his secret, which from tonight is the thing the department knows about the new boy. The reason he said it stays his and the 課長's.

TWIST: Kept back: the 部長 has a weak bladder and will not be seen to keep going to the toilet; the 課長 has chosen the cherry beside the park's only toilet for him every year; "the toilet side" was the whole of the instruction and not a trap. A misunderstanding started it: 三浦, sure the instruction was wrong on purpose to test whether the new hire knew the rule, and hiding the same weakness, did the opposite; the test is 三浦's own theory, built from an article, and nobody in the story sets one. Stated by 三浦, in thought, the moment he sees the 部長 pour his beer onto the grass: the 部長 has a weak bladder too (部長も、トイレが近いのだ); that is why the 課長 said near the toilet; there was never a test; and the 部長 cannot say so himself. The 部長 never states it. The 課長 does not share the condition. He covers his glass (「俺は、まだいい」) because he will not drink while the 部長 cannot, opens his first can only after the move, and comes to the queue only to stand with 三浦 and repeat the 部長's phrase, then leaves it. 三浦 states both in narration: 部長が飲めない間は、課長も飲まなかったのだ, and 課長は、トイレに来たのではなかった.

## PREMISE

On the third day of his first job, at a small stationery company, ｜三浦《みうら》 is sent to hold the department's spot for its 花見, a blue sheet in the park from early morning until the others arrive after work. He has read online that bosses judge a new hire by how he does this, and he means to be judged the best new hire they have ever had.

## ANCHOR

The spot: the department's blue sheet, where it lies under the cherries, and how far it is from the park's one toilet. It is a place and a ritual at once, and the phrase "near the toilet" rides with it, in the instruction, the notebook, the young woman's list, the confession and the queue.

New words carried, the brief's 3, each needing at least 2 occurrences, each first met inside an action:

- ブルーシート: first met on page 1, in his arms, folded (畳んだブルーシートを抱えて); then spread with stones on its corners, sat on by the young woman while he is gone, brushed clear of petals, the edge the 部長 sits on at the climax, and swapped across the park.
- 場所取り: first met on page 1 in the same scene, as what the 課長 handed him the sheet for (課長はきのう、このブルーシートを僕に渡して、場所取りを頼んだ); recurs in the articles he has read, in the 課長's 「去年まで、俺が場所取りをしていた」, at the top of the young woman's list, and at the climax.
- トイレが近い: first met on page 1 in a consequence, as the reason he has drunk nothing since the night before (僕は、トイレが近い。だから昨夜から、水も飲んでいない); again on page 3 as the reason he decides to drink nothing all day; at the climax about the 部長 (部長も、トイレが近いのだ); and in the confession (僕は、トイレが近いんです). The literal トイレの近く, which Ichiran parses as three known words, recurs alongside it in the instruction, the notebook and the young woman's line.

## WANT

To hold the best spot in the park until the department arrives, and be praised for it.

## NEED

He has to look capable in front of anyone above him; being seen to need anything, or to get anything wrong, is the thing he cannot stand.

## SHAPE

Three-act, eight beats. Act I is beats 1 to 2 (pages 1 to 4), Act II beats 3 to 5 (pages 5 to 10), Act III beats 6 to 8 (pages 11 to 16).

Page budget, summing to 16: beat 1, 2 pages; beat 2, 2; beat 3, 2; beat 4, 2; beat 5, 2; beat 6 (climax), 3; beat 7, 2; beat 8, 1. At four to five sentences a page that is 64 to 80 sentences; the beats below are written to about 75, and the climax's realisation is four short sentences.

On time: the story opens on Friday at the park, and the day before reaches the page only through the notebook, so the order is broken on page 1. Each beat opens on an event (the notebook page, the message, the wind, the department appearing at the far tree, the 部長 standing, the 部長 coming back, 三浦 running, the 課長 joining the queue), never on a clock. No time of day is stated in the story; the hours exist only in the physical-facts note.

## BEATS

ACT I (beats 1 to 2, pages 1 to 4)

Beat 1 (2 pages). 三浦 stands under the biggest cherry by the bridge with the department's folded blue sheet in his arms (畳んだブルーシートを抱える), the park empty, the public toilet a few steps away. He has drunk nothing since the night before, because he has a small bladder (トイレが近い), a secret nobody at the company knows. His notebook (手帳) is open at yesterday's page, where the 課長 handed him the sheet and the job (ブルーシートを渡す; 場所取り): "The biggest cherry by the bridge. The toilet side (トイレの近く). I held it myself until last year (去年まで、俺が場所取りをしていた)." Below it, the 部長: "the 花見 is for drinking, not for blossoms" (花見は、桜より酒だ). Every article he has read says sit a hundred metres from the toilets, and says the boss is judging the new hire by how he does it. A 課長 who has held the spot for years must know the rule; so he said it wrong on purpose, to see whether the new boy knows better. 三浦 writes 「トイレの近く → ×（百メートル）。わざと？ → 試験」. He is glad to believe it: by the toilet, the whole department would watch him go. A young woman from an insurance office, another new hire, spreads her sheet on the toilet-side patch and ticks it off on her list: near the toilet you can last all day (トイレの近くなら、一日いられますね, literal). He feels sorry for her. He counts a hundred and thirty steps away from the toilet, exactly a hundred metres, and spreads the sheet under a big cherry there, with river stones on the corners (角に石を置く) and no pegs. YES-BUT: he has, by the rules, the best spot in the park, but he has defied the one clear instruction he was given, on a guess.

Beat 2 (2 pages). The message arrives: "The spot?" (場所は？). 三浦 replies, proud: "The best spot in the park!" (一番いい所です！). The reply (返事) is one word: 「了解」. He is elated: passed. A sign says the park staff take away sheets left with nobody on them (人のいないブルーシートは、公園の人が片付けます), so he has resolved to drink nothing all day. The young woman comes over with a can of hot tea for him; the people beside her sheet (隣の人たち) are watching hers. He cannot refuse a kindness (遠慮), so he sips. She sits down on his sheet and says she will mind it while he buys something to eat. He cannot refuse that either. He walks the hundred metres to the toilet, then buys bread, and comes back holding the bread in front of him. She looks at it and asks whether the toilet was crowded (トイレ、混んでいましたか). "I went for bread." She smiles, ticks something on her list, and goes back to her patch. When she is out of sight he pours the rest of the tea onto the grass behind the sheet (草の上に流す), so he will not need to go again. YES-BUT: he got through the morning and the 課長 has approved, though his 「了解」 means the tree by the bridge; but a stranger has seen through him, and from here he cannot go again.

(end of Act I)

ACT II (beats 3 to 5, pages 5 to 10)

Beat 3 (2 pages). The wind turns cold off the river (花冷え). Petals (桜の花) stream across the sheet and he brushes them off again and again, keeping it clean for inspection, and never once looks up; at home in the north they come in May. Around him the sheets fill, and people ask the people beside them to keep an eye on their things. He asks nobody: not after her question. The department appears at the far tree, the one by the bridge, where every year it goes first, and finds the young woman's company there. The 課長 phones; 三浦 waves them across the park. The 部長, loud and delighted: "What a spot! Well found, new boy!" (いい場所じゃないか。よく見つけたな、新人). The 課長 looks at the 部長, looks back toward the bridge, and says nothing (黙る). YES-BUT: he has the 部長's praise in front of everyone, but the 課長, whose test he believes he has passed, is silent.

Beat 4 (2 pages). Shoes come off onto the sheet (靴を脱ぐ). The 部長 raises his glass: "To the new boy's welcome, and the blossoms" (新人の歓迎と、桜に、乾杯). 三浦 means to take a sip, and after a day without water he drains the glass before he can stop himself. Then he goes round pouring, as a new hire must (お酌), the 部長 first; the 課長 puts his hand over his glass (手でコップに蓋をする), and 三浦 reads it as a judge staying sober. The 部長 stands: 「ちょっと、桜を見てくる」 ("I'm just going to look at the blossoms"), and goes off among the trees. He comes back a long while later, cold, saying the blossoms over there were good too, and 三浦 fills his glass again. NO-AND: the beer is in him, the 課長 is still silent, and the 部長 has gone looking at other trees.

Beat 5 (2 pages). The 部長 stands again: 「ちょっと、桜を見てくる」. 三浦 reads it plainly now: the 部長 is touring the other trees and finding better ones, and the 課長's hand over his glass and his silence are the marks going down (焦る). His own body has caught up with him: the cold since the afternoon, the glass he drained, nothing since noon. He will not be seen walking off to the toilet in front of the 部長 and the 課長 on his own welcome night. NO-AND: his grade, as he reads it, is slipping, and he cannot hold out much longer, and he cannot leave.

(end of Act II)

ACT III (beats 6 to 8, pages 11 to 16)

Beat 6 (3 pages). CLIMAX, as on the CLIMAX line. The 部長 comes back cold from his second trip and sits on the edge of the sheet beside 三浦. 三浦 fills his glass (お酌; コップにビールを入れる). Everyone turns toward a joke. 三浦 sees the 部長 tip that beer out onto the grass behind him (草の上に流す) and lift the empty glass. It is the tea at noon. Four short sentences, in thought: the 部長 did not go to look at the blossoms. The 部長 has a small bladder too (部長も、トイレが近いのだ). That is why the 課長 said near the toilet. It was never a test. He stands and tells the whole department his own secret instead: 「すみません。僕は、トイレが近いんです。トイレの近くに、移ってもいいですか」. Laughter. The 部長: 「なんだ、早く言え。新人が我慢するな」. The 課長 looks at him a long moment, then stands and lifts the box of beer without a word. NO-AND for the want: the best spot, the praise and his secret are all gone in one sentence, and everyone is laughing at him. The need is faced: he has let himself be seen to need something, and to have got it wrong, in front of everyone above him.

Beat 7 (2 pages). 三浦 runs. At the bridge tree the toilet queue now runs along the edge of the young woman's sheet, and her ten are cramped on it and tired of being stepped on. He asks for a swap: their patch by the toilet for his spot in the middle of the park, which has room to spare (その代わり、僕たちの場所をどうぞ). She looks at him: 「ここは、トイレが近いですよ」 ("It's right by the toilet here," literal). "Yes. That's why." She ticks something on her list. Then he joins the end of the queue (列の最後に並ぶ) at once, and from it he watches the swap: both sheets are the same large company size, so each goes into the other's gap; her group spreads out in the middle of the park with a cheer, and his department settles under the bridge tree, the 部長 at the end nearest the toilet, saying the cherry here is the best in the park after all (やっぱり、ここの桜が一番だな). The 課長 opens his first can. YES-BUT: the 部長 has his tree back and nobody but 三浦 and the 課長 knows why, but 三浦 is now the new boy who got the spot wrong and could not hold it, and that is how the department will tell it.

Beat 8 (1 page). The 課長 joins the queue behind him, his one can open. 「桜を見に来た」 ("Came to look at the blossoms."). 「僕もです」 ("Me too."). Neither says anything else. The last sentence holds 三浦 looking up into the cherry for the first time that day and lands on the ordinary: he moves up one place with the queue (初めて桜を上まで見ながら、僕は列と一緒に、一つ前に進んだ, or similar; the look inside the sentence, the step at its end). YES-BUT: he and the 課長 now share the department's way of not saying it, and at last he is looking at the blossoms, from a toilet queue that is still moving.

Physical facts checked (hours here only, never in the story):

- Geography: one public toilet, beside the bridge tree. 三浦's sheet is exactly a hundred metres from it, a hundred and thirty of his steps, as the rule he follows says. A trip from his sheet is about a minute and a half each way plus the queue: five minutes at noon, about twenty in the evening, so about twenty-five minutes in all.
- 三浦's day: last drink the night before; one trip at noon, while the young woman sits on his sheet; one sip of her tea, the rest poured away; nothing more until the 乾杯 glass, drained at about a quarter to seven. By the cold evening, some eight hours after his noon trip and with the beer in him, he is desperate by about eight, and has not gone because he will not be seen leaving in front of his seniors on his welcome night.
- The evening: the department reaches the bridge tree about half past six, phones, crosses the hundred metres, takes off its shoes, and drinks the 乾杯 at about a quarter to seven. The 部長's first trip is about seven to twenty-five past, his second about twenty to eight to five past eight, and the climax about ten past eight.
- The 課長's silence: his noon 「了解」 cannot catch the error, because "the best spot in the park" is the bridge tree to him; he cannot move the party once the 部長 has praised the spot; the 部長 cannot refuse drink without being asked why, so he pours it away while 三浦 keeps his glass filled, as a new hire must.
- The headcount and the swap: the department is seven (部長, 課長, 三浦 and four), on the large company tarp that seats about ten; the young woman's group is ten on the same size of tarp. Each sheet goes into the gap the other leaves, so nothing has to fit a smaller space in a full park.
- After the confession, 三浦 asks for the swap on the way to the toilet and queues at once while the others carry; the 課長 opens his first can at the swap and comes to the queue with that one can.
