new_words.ブルーシート: blue tarp: first met p1 in his arms, 畳んだブルーシートを抱えて立っていた; spread with river stones on its corners on p3, sat on by the young woman while he is gone, brushed clear of petals, the edge the 部長 sits on at the climax, and swapped across the park
new_words.トイレが近い: having a small bladder, literally the toilet is near: first met p1 in a consequence, 僕はトイレが近いので、昨夜から水も飲んでいない; again p3 as why he will not sit by the toilet, at the climax about the 部長 (部長も、トイレが近いのだ) and in the confession (僕は、トイレが近いんです). The literal トイレの近く, three known words, runs beside it as the pun the story turns on

new_words.便箋: letter paper — framed p8 by 中から、折った便箋が一枚だけ出てきた with the blank lower half described in the next line; recurs as the son's sheet, hers, and the reply's
new_words.消印: postmark — framed p4 by position first and contents second, 切手の上の消印を読んで、日にちを数えた followed by 小さな丸の中に、遠い町の名前と三月四日が押してある; later dates the son's wait and identifies the reply's origin
new_words.表札: nameplate — framed p1 by 玄関の横の表札を確かめると、そこは松田という私の名字になっている, which is the right-address/wrong-name premise made physical. Passes check.py via the 表+札 fallback, so it must be declared to be marked

stories.title: 黄色い傘
stories._feature: Second story in the comic register, and the first comic at level 2. The engine is a ledger: the narrator's exactness is both the comedy and the evidence, and at the climax she reads her own entries 黄1 to 黄8 as a confession. The reader is meant to be a step ahead from page 2, where she complains about the bakery's yellow sign.
stories._note: NO NAMES FOR THE TWO LEADS. She is 本屋さん to him and he is パン屋の主人 to her; the feud keeps them on titles. HER VOICE is neat polite-plain わたし, comedy carried by counting; HIS is loud plain speech, and his daily 「たまにはパン、買いに来てよ！」 is planted to pay off as 「やっと来た！」. ARITHMETIC CHECKED: 10 green; 2 come back to her stand, 8 go to the bakery (the neighbourhood returns to whichever shop it passes, and the umbrellas carry no mark). 8 yellow arrive in her stand (3 by mid June, 5 by end June, 8 by late July); she lends all 8 as 黄1 to 黄8, the last on the morning of the climax. BEAT 5 is inferable: he walks to her shop under one green umbrella with a second under his arm, to return it, and she locks him out with 本日休み. 黄8 goes to the dentist's receptionist, who was the first green umbrella not to come back.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: she crosses the street in the rain with her ledger to accuse the baker, entering his shop for the first time in ten years. He shouts 「本屋さん！やっと来た！」. Behind him eight of her green umbrellas stand dried and rolled, each tagged 本屋 in his big writing. 「で、うちの黄色いのは？」 She has lent every yellow one out and her ledger says to whom; she reads 黄1 to 黄8. She closes it and says 「あんパンを、一つください」, her first purchase in ten years. He laughs the loud laugh. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: a fussy bookseller lends ten green umbrellas with a ledger; greens stop coming back and unfamiliar yellow ones arrive; she decides she is being robbed, and finally that the thief is the loud baker opposite whose yellow sign she has resented for a decade. WANT: all ten green umbrellas back, and the swapper caught. NEED: exactness is her fence against owing anyone, needing anyone, or walking into anyone's shop; she has to end up in the wrong, in debt, in public, and pay in the currency the feud refused. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2 (pp1-5), II 3-5 (pp6-13), III 6-7 (pp14-19). BEATS: 1 the ledger and the ten greens; plants: the yellow sign, his daily greeting, ten years without buying his bread; a green fails to return and a yellow appears (yes-but). 2 three missing, three yellow; she theorises a swapper with kiosk umbrellas and tapes up 緑の傘は本屋の傘です; more yellows, and a boy thanks her for one (no-and). 3 the boy shelters from the rain, only yellows left; she lends one as the thief's repayment and starts a yellow column (yes-but). 4 he shouts 傘！傘！ with his arms full; she reads mockery and shuts the door (no-and). 5 he comes under a green umbrella with a second under his arm; she locks the door and puts out 本日休み; certainty; the ledger balances on her side; she lends 黄8 (yes-but). 6 CLIMAX at the bakery (no-and). 7 home with eight greens and the あんパン; a new paper: either shop is fine; next rain she takes back a yellow without writing anything (yes-but).

new_words.傘立て: umbrella stand — first in p1 with ten green umbrellas standing in it; the story's centre, recurs as where the yellows appear, where the papers are taped, and as the bakery's own stand at the climax
new_words.商店街: shopping street — p1, as the reason she never marked the umbrellas: no other shop on it lends green ones
new_words.印: mark, tag — p1 as the mark she decided not to put on the umbrellas; paid off at the climax as his paper tags reading 本屋
new_words.雨宿り: sheltering from rain — p6, the boy standing in front of the shop, which is why she lends the first yellow

stories.title: 鍵とチェーン
stories._premise: CLIMAX: 8:50 on a Saturday; the son (about thirty, moved back home, keeps the household money and his father's pension in a notebook, with a back page dating his father's lapses) has searched every place on his list for the one house key. His father, seventy-one, cheerful, wearing the son's old high-school coat since breakfast, is at the door with one shoe on. The son says, half to himself, 「チェーンは、外からは掛けられない」. The father stops, finds the key in the coat pocket, hands it over, then sets down a damp envelope from the station-front newspaper delivery shop: three weeks' pay. 「お前の手帳に、指輪は書けんだろう」. The son looks at the mother's red circle on next Friday's calendar. He does not put the key back on its dish; he hands it to his father, 「持ってて」, and goes to work late with no key. That night he leaves the chain hanging. AFTERWORD: stories-index.md § Afterwords. PREMISE: the son reads every clue (chain off, wet paper, grey fingertips, his own old coat on his father) as the forgetfulness he dreads; the same facts describe a man getting up at four to earn money his son cannot count. WANT: find the key before nine so he can lock up and leave. NEED: stop managing his father as if he were already old; the secrecy was a reply to him. SHAPE: three-act. BEATS: Act I (1) chain off, son blames himself; wet newspaper, rain in the night; (2) father cheerful at breakfast in the son's coat, grey fingertips logged on the back page, red circle on the calendar, errand at ten; (3) 8:15, key gone from its dish [act break]. Act II (4) the list, crossed off in order; the old coat is not on it; father searching cheerfully; (5) phone to the mother: she has hers, says he is getting up early like when he was young, tells him not to fuss about next week; he cannot say 物忘れ; (6) outside to the neighbour's, nothing; father at the door to leave. Act III (7) the chain line is the turn; key, envelope, the father's one line, the calendar; (8) the key given away, the chain left hanging.

new_words.チェーン: door chain — framed p1 by its being found undone, チェーンが外れている, before the narrator says he fastens it himself every night. Recurs at the act break, at the turn as the line that can't be fastened from outside, and as the last image
new_words.年金: pension — framed p4 by the money moving through the son's notebook, 父の年金も毎月僕の手帳に入って、僕の手帳から出ていく, which is the control the father's secret answers
new_words.物忘れ: forgetfulness — framed by the word sticking in the son's throat on the phone to his mother, and next as the thing he would have to take his father to a doctor for

stories.title: 終電
stories._feature: Untagged two-person dialogue. 38 of 39 quoted lines carry no attribution and the train conversation is 100% untagged, with speakers held by register: he asks, at length and over-politely, and she answers short. The single kept attribution is the manager's remembered line on page 4, so the reader sees one tagged line before the mode changes. Longest untagged run is 10, against 1 and 2 in the stories either side. Measured 2026-09-19: her replies run 2 to 22 characters against a median of 9, so the cue is question-versus-answer and register, not a length band — an earlier version of this key claimed four to eight and was never true of either draft.

new_words.網棚: luggage rack — framed p3 by the narrator's own aborted use of it, 荷物を網棚に上げようとして、やめた, with 足元に置いておく方が、降りる時に楽だ fixing it against the floor in the next line. It is the object of the first exchange with her and the closing image of that thread
new_words.乗客: passenger — framed p3 by a count in a car already called 空いている, 今夜も車内には乗客が四人しかいなくて、皆、離れた席に座っていた; tracks the train emptying until only the two of them are left

stories.title: 煙突の煙
stories._note: The first story written through the two-gate flow: brief resolved and confirmed before drafting, premise and afterword written in English before any Japanese existed.
stories._premise: A woman returns for a week to clear her late father's apartment and goes to the neighbourhood bathhouse every evening of its last week. The owner has been keeping the water hot past closing for three months, waiting for a regular who came late from the factory. That regular was her father, and nobody told the owner he had died. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) clearing the apartment, chimney visible from the window / (2) as a child, the smoke going out meant he was on his way home / (3) first evening, closing Sunday, almost no customers / (4) the owner does not recognise her and says nothing / (5) PLANT: one 桶 kept aside, upside down, never handed out / (6) she says nothing and keeps returning to look for it / (7) the smoke keeps going up after closing, every night / (8) she asks; he says he is waiting for a regular from the factory / (9) TURN: she works out who, and that she never told him / (10) she tells him; he turns the 桶 over and fills it; from the window the smoke stops early for the first time.

new_words.湯気: steam — framed p5 by 戸を開けると、湯気が外へ流れ出した, so the word is shown doing something visible before anything is said about it, and the fogged mirrors follow in the next line. Recurs over the bath, off the filled 桶 at the turn, and under the ceiling on the last night
new_words.桶: washing bucket — framed p7 as the thing you fetch for yourself, 桶は棚から自分で取る, with the stack described bottoms-up in the next line. The one left mouth-up is the story's plant and its payoff, so it repeats without the prose reaching
new_words.番台: the raised attendant's desk — framed p6 by what crosses it rather than by what it is: the owner takes the money without a word and passes the soap up from underneath. It is where he is in every scene until he climbs down from it at the turn
new_words.煙突: chimney — framed p2 by 煙突は町のどの建物よりも高いので、この部屋からでもよく見える, which is the reason the signalling works at all. Carries that thread: the childhood memory, the smoke after closing, and the last line
new_words.湯船: the bath itself, as against washing — framed p8 by 体を洗ってから、湯船に入った and immediately by being too hot to get into. Recurs at the close, where she does not stop
new_words.廃業: going out of business — framed p4 by the notice at the door, 今度の日曜日で廃業する、と書いてあった, and by the narrator standing and reading the word. Deliberately paired against the already-known 閉店, which stays in the story for the nightly closing hour: 閉店の時間は過ぎているはずだった is what makes her look up at the smoke, and 廃業 is what the week is counting down to. Added 2026-09-19; brief.new_words raised 5 to 6 for it

stories.title: 縁台の将棋
stories._note: The first story briefed with a deliberately widened new-word budget, at 2.4x the derived rate, and the first with no death in it. Both came out of the 2026-09-19 second blind read: six evaluators named circumlocution-around-the-obligatory-noun as the corpus's clearest tell, and the reader's own ★2 on 煙突の煙 said 'another story about a dead person, derivative of the watch story'. The extra budget is spent entirely on the board, because the people could already be written — 座る, 隣, 向かい, 膝, 髪, 耳, 息, 手袋 are all known, so nothing in the relationship needed a new word.
stories._premise: Two women meet every Sunday over a shogi board on a park bench. The younger, the narrator, wins almost every week, because Hiroko resigns around the fortieth move. Hiroko is in fact much the stronger player and has been resigning from winning positions for a year: a game she wins is a game that ends, and the narrator would go home. the narrator, meanwhile, has been studying alone every night for the same reason, to make the games last. Her studying is what exposes it. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) the Sunday ritual, the bench, the pieces going down / (2) PLANT: Hiroko resigns on move forty and the narrator does not understand how she won / (3) the narrator buys a book so the next game will last longer / (4) weeks pass, the games run to seventy moves, the resignation still arrives / (5) the narrator starts watching Hiroko's fingertips instead of the board, and the pause does not look like losing / (6) a cold Sunday, gloves off, red cheeks, the closest they come to saying anything / (7) the narrator gives check for the first time and Hiroko resigns early / (8) TURN: the narrator rebuilds the abandoned position from Hiroko's side and finds mate in two / (9) a year of Sundays reorganises itself; both of them had been playing to keep the other there / (10) the next Sunday Hiroko moves first, plays it out, wins, and asks for a second game for the first time.
stories._new_words: Twelve, against a derived five. Held at twelve rather than higher because every declared word must reach min_occurrences, and 駒台 and 盤面 would have had to be reached for — the documented failure. Each of these is either the subject matter or load-bearing for the turn.

new_words.将棋: shogi — the subject; framed p1 by being played rather than described, 日曜日の午後、私はそこで将棋を指す
new_words.駒: piece — framed p2 by being set out and making a sound, never explained. The story's highest-frequency new word
new_words.盤: board — framed p2 by Hiroko sitting across it. Carries the last beat, where half of it falls into shadow
new_words.指す: to play a move — the verb the domain takes rather than する or やる, framed p1 in the opening sentence of the ritual
new_words.対局: a game, as a unit — framed p2 as the thing that begins once the pieces are out. Needed because the story counts games across a year
new_words.縁台: the wooden bench — framed p1 by being the place, and it is where every scene happens. Title word
new_words.持ち駒: pieces in hand — framed p11 by being counted during the reconstruction, which is the mechanism of the turn, and again p18 as they dwindle
new_words.王手: check — framed p10 by the narrator giving it for the first time, which is what triggers the early resignation. Returns at p20 against her
new_words.詰み: mate — framed p5 as the thing the book is teaching her, どうやって作られるのか, and it is what she finds on the abandoned board
new_words.投了: resignation — framed p3 by Hiroko doing it, and it is the story's plant. Recurs as the weekly ritual and stops recurring at the end, which is the payoff
new_words.指先: fingertips — framed p7 by the narrator watching them instead of the board. The crush made physical, and the tell that the pause is a choice
new_words.頬: cheek — framed p8 by being red in December. Returns at the end still red, when it is not the cold

stories.title: 三番の乾燥機
stories._note: The first story with every brief parameter moved off its default, at the reader's request. Two of them are attributable and the brief is the only record either way. `dialogue` 28% untagged comes from the reader's ★4 on 終電 — 'brief and aloof interaction, a quiet connection' — which is the corpus's only rating above ★3 and runs 29.8% dialogue at 97.4% untagged; it landed at 26.5% and 100%. `new_words` 12 comes from the 2026-09-19 second blind read, where six evaluators converged on circumlocution-around-the-obligatory-noun as the clearest tell and 23 of 24 obligatory nouns tested outside the known set. The domain was chosen by measurement rather than taste: have.py over ~160 words across three candidate domains put the room, the machines and the people of a coin laundry almost entirely inside the known set, so the whole widened budget goes on obligatory nouns and nothing is spent on the relationship. A bakery was rejected on the same test (窯, 生地, 粉, 小麦 all outside), which is the institutional-setting failure that second read named. Second story running with nobody dead in it and nothing anybody's keepsake.
stories._premise: A man who has just moved onto the shopping street does his laundry at the all-night coin laundry every Tuesday, and every Tuesday an older woman is in the same chair under the heater, reading, with a very small bag of washing and the one dryer that does not get warm. She washes very little and runs the cold machine through twice, which takes two hours. Annoyed after carrying his own wash home half dry, he tells the owner the machine is broken; a notice goes up; the following week she is finished and gone in thirty minutes. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) Tuesdays at the coin laundry, because the new flat has no machine / (2) PLANT: he learns the room by watching it, and the woman under the heater has a magazine, one small bag, and never leaves / (3) a cold night, only number three free, and his wash comes out cold — 乾いているはずだった / (4) 「三番は温まらない」, said to her magazine after the fact, and he does not answer / (5) weeks of not speaking, and the anomaly: she takes number three every week, on purpose, and runs it twice / (6) short exchanges accumulate over the winter — 「二番がいちばん速い」, 「あなたには、ね」 — and he cannot stop doing the arithmetic / (7) half helpfulness and half still being annoyed, he tells the owner to put a notice on it / (8) PAYOFF: she reads the notice, takes number four, and is out the door in thirty minutes; the chair under the heater is empty before nine / (9) the owner, counting him a regular now, asks him to mind the place for the repairman / (10) TURN: 「別に、悪くないです」 — the notice comes down, she puts her bag back in number three, and he puts his own wash in beside it knowing it will not dry.
stories._new_words: Nine, against a derived six and a briefed ceiling of twelve. Held there rather than filled to twelve because the ceiling is not a target and every one had to clear min_occurrences without the prose reaching for it: the shortest runs four times, the longest thirteen. Every one is an obligatory noun of the domain, and two of them — 貼り紙 and 無人 — are named in the 2026-09-19 second blind read as words this corpus had previously written around, as 「紙」 and as 「空」.

new_words.コインランドリー: coin laundry — the setting. Framed p1 by being walked to with an armful of washing, never described. Page 4 is the de-circumlocution: このコインランドリーに通うようになって rather than ここへ. Declared for the record only: Ichiran segments it into コイン + ランドリー and build.py analyses kanji words alone, so both halves ship with no n, no u and no kana — the katakana case AUTHORING.md already names for クロ, where the marker earns nothing because there is no reading to teach
new_words.乾燥機: dryer — the story's object and its highest-frequency new word at ten. Framed p2 by wet things being moved across into one, which is what a dryer is for
new_words.洗濯物: the washing, as a noun — thirteen occurrences. Framed p1 in the arms of somebody carrying it. Load-bearing for the arithmetic, because the size of hers against the size of his is the clue
new_words.温まる: to get warm, intransitive — the story's key predicate, and the sentence the whole plot turns on is 「三番は温まらない」. Framed p12 as a consequence, spoken to a magazine after his wash has already failed. 四番は温まる at p26 is the same word doing the payoff
new_words.貼り紙: a notice stuck up — framed p24 by being stuck on the machine, and it is the hinge: it goes up because he asked for it and comes down because he lies. Written as 「紙」 in 猫を探す探偵, which the second blind read caught
new_words.小銭: coins — framed p2 by being fed into a machine. Runs from not having enough on his first night to having them ready in his bag on the last page, which is the only place the story says he has changed twice
new_words.商店街: the shopping street — framed p1 as the place walked down, and it is what he goes back out into at p12 with the half-dry shirts
new_words.無人: unstaffed — framed p3 as the consequence of the owner shutting up at nine, an event rather than a definition. Carries the last movement: it is why a 留守番 is needed at all, and 無人のはずの店 at p30 is the night he is the one in it. Written as 「空」 in 終電, which the second blind read caught
new_words.生乾き: half dry — framed p11 by coming out of the machine that way after eighty minutes. The word he uses to the owner at p24, which is what makes the complaint land

stories._voice: Failure mode six, measured with voice.py after the draft. past_pct 59.8 against an authentic median of 59.3 and final3_entropy 5.74 against a median 5.45 are both the best in the corpus, and final3_top3_pct 20.5 sits on the authentic median of 20.2. run_mean is 3.90 against an authentic 2.24-3.37 and is left there on purpose. The first draft ran run_max 15 and run_mean 4.46; three changes took it to 13 and 3.90, and every one was a prose fix rather than a variety purchase — a scenic ル sentence inside the December scene, a grudge that is still live so its sentence is not past either (今でも思う), and a past event moved out of ことも覚えている into plain past. What is left driving run_mean is two long ル blocks, 11 and 13 sentences, and those are the habitual establishing passages: Japanese habitual narration is ル, and breaking them would be the documented failure of buying a number. AUTHORING.md's own test is the stretch where every sentence lands on the same ENDING, and the entropy figure says this story does not have one.
stories._mimetics: Ten, planned into the draft rather than added to it: ぐるぐる on the drum at p7, p30 and the last line, がたがた on the old machine at p8, きょろきょろ on his first night at p4, ぽかぽか and いい匂い on a load out of a dryer that works at p26, はっと at p28, そっと at p26, ばったり at p22. Measured 2026-09-19 the corpus ran 0.34 per 100 narration sentences against an authentic 4.35-33.12; the figure says where to look, not what to hit, and where to look was narration that reports motion where it could depict it. No 三点リーダー: measured Dead, the authentic median is 0.00 and this corpus's zero already is that median.

stories.title: 十五日の質札
stories._feature: First story in the ghost-story register, and the first written against the September 2026 Gate 2 — climax first, want and need on separate tracks, a declared three-act shape, every beat a yes-but or a no-and. The veiled plant is bookkeeping: the narrator spoils a ticket in the first week and voids it by number, which reads as him being tired and pays off as the only proof the story offers.
stories._note: THE GHOST IS NOT A MOURNED RELATIVE. That guard is written into the register itself because 時計の音 and 煙突の煙 are the same bereavement story twice and were rated two stars both times, the second explicitly as derivative. The woman is a stranger and the weight sits on the narrator's choice, not on her condition. THE TWIST IS NOT THAT SHE IS DEAD — a reader will suspect that by the neighbour scene, and it is meant to be suspected. The turn is the ticket number, and under it the fact that he confessed to someone who was never going to catch him. THE FATHER IS A SOURCE OF A RULE AND NOTHING ELSE: he is named three times, never mourned, and the story does not visit him. YEAR-END IS THE SUBJECT, NOT A MARKER: the 大掃除 is why the storehouse is being cleared and New Year money is why the shop is busy, which is the audit's fifth divergence answered in the premise rather than in the prose. 店を畳む rather than 廃業 or 閉店 — the audit found 閉店 used for a 銭湯 going out of business, and this is the same error class avoided with a word already in the known set.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: he voids her ticket and the number is the one he spoiled and voided himself in the first week, and that voided ticket is still in his drawer, whole. Both exist. He looks up and she is gone. Nobody explains it, including him. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: year-end at a small pawnshop; the owner is clearing the storehouse to close the business by New Year, and one customer comes every month to redeem a comb and pawn it again. WANT: empty the storehouse and close the shop by 大晦日. NEED: to admit the shop was never a business in objects — he keeps perfect records of items and none of people, and that is what lets him take the earlier date. He gets the want; it costs him the thing that would have made having it bearable. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2, II 3-6, III 7-9. BEATS: 1 counts the stock and voids a torn ticket, number 214 (yes-but, veiled plant). 2 she redeems and re-pawns; he tells her the shop closes (no-and). 3 the record runs back past this book in a third hand (yes-but). 4 next door has been shut on the third for twenty years (no-and). 5 the record says the 15th and her ticket the 16th; he takes the 15th (yes-but, the ugly choice). 6 the dealer pays less than she paid monthly (yes-but, the cost). 7 she comes on the 16th and is not angry; she asks to see the shelf (no-and). 8 her ticket is 214 and the voided one is still in the drawer (yes-but, climax). 9 he closes on schedule; the pale patch stays and he greets an empty doorway (no-and).

new_words.質屋: pawnshop — the setting and the narrator's trade. First occurrence has it doing something rather than being defined: 年末になると、うちのような質屋は忙しくなる. Recurs at the forty-year line and at the closing
new_words.質札: pawn ticket — the object the whole turn runs on. Framed p2 by the act of tearing one and voiding it by number, before the reader has any reason to care. Recurs through every counter scene and at the payoff
new_words.櫛: comb — what is pawned, redeemed and pawned again. Framed p5 by being taken out of a box and set on paper, with its three missing teeth as the only description. Recurs monthly, at the sale, and as the empty shelf
new_words.質流れ: forfeiture of a pawned item once its deadline passes — the mechanism the plot turns on. Framed p15 inside the narrator's own calculation, 十五日で質流れにすれば蔵は予定通り空になる, so it arrives as a consequence he is choosing rather than a term being explained. Recurs at the sale, the confession and the rule
new_words.蔵: storehouse — what the want is about emptying. Framed p1 by the cleaning itself, 蔵を空にするための大掃除. Recurs as where the comb lives, where the old books are, and as the empty room she asks to stand in

stories.title: 回覧板の返事
stories._feature: First story in the comic register, and the first briefed short on purpose: 15 pages against the 25 default, chosen by Rob at Gate 1. Also the first two-act shape. The comedy is dramatic irony carried by a single misreading engine: every sign of a learner (spaced hiragana, a question about a word, a kanji copied from his own note, a sincere thank-you) is read by the narrator as mockery, and the reader is meant to be one step ahead of him without being sure.
stories._note: NO DEAD RELATIVE ANYWHERE. The wife is alive and is the comic foil, and her secret (she has known グエン since summer, from the rubbish point) is the second reveal. THE NARRATOR SIGNS 班長 AND NEVER HIS NAME: plant on p2, said as officiousness, paid off on the second-last page when he writes 山本 with kana above it, which is the furigana mechanism of the reader itself turned into the story's last act. HER VOICE IS TEXTBOOK です・ます WITH COMMAS, deliberately: the corpus's named defect is neutral textbook Japanese for every speaker, and here it is the one voice where that register is the true characterisation. Her written replies are hiragana with spaces between words (分かち書き), which is how a learner writes, and kanji enter them one at a time. LOGIC CHECKED: the rule is per house, so nine or ten days round eight houses is consistent with everyone else taking a day or two; her final note arrives under 吉田's because 吉田 is house two and she is house five. 夜勤 and 介護 are both unknown and are carried instead by 施設 (a leech), the uniform, the 10am return and the curtains shut at noon. Peeked words reused on purpose: 返事, 渡す, 近所, 貼る, 黙る.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: 山本 takes the board to house five himself, with a letter clipped on top whose first word is 迷惑. A young woman in a care-home uniform opens the door, just off a night shift, and apologises for the three days before he can speak. Behind her a notebook holds every notice copied by hand, his long explanations included, with kana over each kanji. She points at the top of his letter and asks how it is read. He has no lie ready and reads it aloud: めいわく. She knows the word. She says she will not write again. He has everything he wanted and says 「三日でいい」 and walks home with the letter in his pocket. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: three years retired and group leader by rotation, 山本 takes the post far too seriously; when the board comes back late he tapes a rule to it, and the rule gets a reply. WANT: the board passed on within two days at every house. NEED: since retiring the title is the only way he knows how to speak to anyone; he needs to be answered as himself rather than obeyed as 班長. He gives up the rule to keep the replies. SHAPE: two-act, I 1-3 (pp1-8), II 4-7 (pp9-16). BEATS: 1 the festival notice comes back late, house five held it three days; he tapes up the two-day rule signed only 班長; wife: 三日くらいならいいじゃない; reply in spaced hiragana asks for three (yes-but, three veiled plants). 2 he decides the unseen tenant is a young man who sleeps all day and cannot write kanji, and refuses in heavy kanji; house five asks what you do at a drill, which he takes as mockery (no-and). 3 he writes a page-long drill explanation to shame them; the board now comes back faster because the street reads his notes and votes; house five copies 訓練 and thanks him, which he reads as sarcasm; he writes the 迷惑 letter (yes-but). 4 CLIMAX at the door (no-and: he wins and gives it back). 5 home: 「グエンさん、元気だった？」, the wife has known since summer, 聞かなかったじゃない (no-and). 6 he strikes 二日 and writes 三日 where the whole street will see, puts kana over every kanji on the next notice, and signs 山本 with やまもと above it (yes-but: she said she would not write again). 7 the board returns, three days at house five exactly, 吉田: 班長さん、負けましたね, and under it her note signed グエン.

new_words.回覧板: the neighbourhood notice board passed house to house — the object at the centre and what the story's words recur on. First occurrence p1 has it coming back late, 回覧板が戻ってきたのは、祭りが終わった次の日だった, which is the problem the want is about. Recurs on nearly every page
new_words.班長: group leader of a block of houses, held by rotation — the narrator's title and the thing he hides behind. First doing work p2, where he writes it under his rule instead of his name. Recurs as his signature, in the street's teasing, and at the payoff where 山本 replaces it
new_words.訓練: drill, in 避難訓練 — first arrives as the notice that stalls at house five, then in hiragana as her question, then copied in kanji from his own note, which is the misreading the climax pays off. Framed by his page-long account of what you do at one, which is the comedy rather than a gloss

stories.title: 狐に貸した隅
stories._feature: Second folktale, and the first told-to-you voice: every unbracketed line is the old woman talking to her grandson, so the frame is a live walk to the field in ル forms and the tale inside it runs in タ. The tale is told in the third person about 'a girl called ハル', and the teller's name is never said in the frame, so 「ハルは、わしじゃ」 is the reveal. 化ける carries the folktale magic: stolen fox rice turns to leaves, given fox rice stays rice.
stories._note: THE SAME FOUR WORDS TWICE: 「わしが刈った」 is the grandmother's lie on p21 and the teller's truth on p25, and the boy is the one who notices the repetition. VEILED PLANTS: 雀に貸しとる (p2) said as a family joke; 松吉さん's warning that fox rice turns to leaves (p10) written as envy, since he is looking at the grandmother's field while he says it; 貸すのはええ。借りるのは嫌いじゃ (p5) as plain pride; 足元を見い (p12) as a real warning about a real stone, paid off as the last line in the boy's mouth. The boy is never named and calls her ばあちゃん throughout. LOGIC: the teller's grandmother is the boy's great-great-grandmother, so he says ハルのばあさま rather than claiming kinship he has not worked out. Rent in rice to the 持ち主 (地主 and 小屋 are unknown; the rice is hung to dry 家の裏). Peeked words reused on purpose: 渡す, 黙る, 返事, 隣, 乾かす.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: the night before harvest, the boy holds the light at the corner by the woods while old ハル, stick handed off so she can stand on her own feet, says to the dark 「わしが刈った」. He says that is what ハル's grandmother said; she says 「ハルは、わしじゃ」. Nothing comes out of the woods. She tells him to cut the corner tomorrow and hang one handful behind the house by itself; if it turns to leaves she will come and say it again. Cost: sixty years of the uncut corner end under his blade, he now knows she was the thief, and there is no sign. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: an old woman makes her grandson walk her to the corner of the field she has left uncut for sixty years, telling a fox tale on the way about a girl called ハル. WANT: keep the corner from being cut tomorrow, or failing that keep the reason secret. NEED: to admit she owes; she inherited her grandmother's lend-never-borrow pride and has lived a confession as a yearly habit so as never to say it. SHAPE: three-act; frame (ル) interleaved with tale (タ), no seasonal march. BEATS: I 1 the boy will cut the corner, her sparrow joke loses; but she gets him alone and starts a tale (yes-but). 2 cold summer, the grandmother refuses 松吉さん's rice, lends the poor corner to a too-polite young man; ハル sees a tail; 狐でも、約束は約束じゃ (yes-but). II 3 the fox's corner turns gold, theirs stays thin; 松吉さん says fox rice turns to leaves; the owner's man says rent the day after harvest or the field goes (no-and). 4 frame: the boy asks how she knows ハル's thoughts; 足元を見い (yes-but). 5 rice short; 貸したもんの上に、借りはつくらん; ハル cuts the corner by moonlight and hangs it behind the house (yes-but: stolen). 6 morning, leaves; the grandmother sees ハル's muddy feet and sweeps, saying nothing (no-and). III 7 the fox brings the promised sack; 「わしが刈った」; he looks at ハル, leaves the rice, keeps the corner 刈った人が、返しに来るまで (yes-but). 8 CLIMAX. 9 cut it tomorrow; 帰ろう; the boy leads with the light: ばあちゃん、足元を見て.

new_words.狐: fox — the borrower. First occurrence p8 is ハル naming what she has just seen under the hem, 「狐だ」, an act of recognition rather than a gloss; recurs as 狐の隅, 狐の米, 狐の稲 and in the boy's last question
new_words.田んぼ: rice field — the rented land the want is about keeping. First doing work p1, 明日は田んぼを刈る; recurs as the grandmother's field, the thing 松吉さん looks at, and うちの田んぼ at the reveal
new_words.稲: the rice plant, as distinct from 米 — what grows, is cut, is hung, and turns to leaves. First p4, staying thin and green in a cold summer; recurs on most tale pages
new_words.化ける: to turn into, of a fox's doing — the mechanism the theft turns on. First p10 inside 松吉さん's warning, then p17 as the fact on the drying line
new_words.刈る: to cut (grain) — the act the whole debt is about. First p1 in the father's plan; recurs as the theft, the lie, the confession and the instruction

stories.title: 貸出中の本
stories._feature: Second ghost story, and a deliberately different mechanism from 十五日の質札: nobody visits, nothing is duplicated, no record is dug into. One object moves, a bookmark advancing overnight in a locked library, and it is reported only as page numbers, never as a shiver. The veiled plant is the narrator's rigidity: 貸出中の本は、返却されるまでお待ちください, said to an angry patron on p5 and read as her flaw, is the line she turns on the boy at the climax, where it protects a reader instead of an order.
stories._note: THE GHOST IS NEVER NAMED OR EXPLAINED. The 1981 borrower exists only as record detail: the due-date stamp 57.1.5 (Showa 57, 1982), the blank return space, and the pre-merger town name on the bookmark. Nobody speculates aloud. THE CLIMAX IS LEGIBLE WITHOUT NARRATION: the page numbers 288 and 300 are planted that morning, so 二百八十八ページと、二百五十八ページだった is the whole of her reasoning. THE OLD STAMP is planted p4 as a paperweight and pays off twice: she sets it to 57.1.5 to close the old loan on time, then to a date two weeks off for his. HIS FIRST LOAN NEVER REACHES THE COMPUTER, which still shows 0: the want is won in the one form she no longer counts. 一冊 is declared as the narrator's counting word. Peeked words reused on purpose: 渡す, 貼る, 処理, 記録, 黙る, 返事. Names: 樹 (いつき), a current boy's name, chosen because the batch already had a 湊; 小林 and 森 segment whole. 暖房 rather than ストーブ, and ハンコ for the date stamper, both inside the known set.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: December 28, the last afternoon before the New Year closure. The 1981 bookmark is 12 pages from the end; 樹, ten, is 30 behind it. After refusing every card form since spring he brings one signed by his mother. She makes the card, he asks to take the book home over the break, and she refuses: 「この本は、まだ貸出中なの」. He leaves with an empty card and waits on the entrance bench rather than at the heater. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: the return box at a small town library brings back a children's novel last borrowed in 1981, written off decades ago; its bookmark, printed with the pre-merger library name, advances every night in a building only the narrator can unlock, and the boy who waits there every afternoon starts racing it. WANT: 樹 to get a card and borrow a book. NEED: she counts reading instead of seeing it; her strict rule must be applied to a reader no system counts, at the cost of the loan she wanted. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2, II 3-5, III 6-8. BEATS: 1 the book with no barcode, card due 57.1.5, return blank; 館長 says the free shelf; she keeps it; the old stamp as paperweight (yes-but). 2 the overdue-reservation patron gets the rule; 樹 refuses the form again (no-and). 3 bookmark 41 to 58 in a locked building; she tells nobody (yes-but). 4 compressed mornings; 樹 asks what it is and starts at page one (yes-but: reading, in the one book she cannot lend). 5 he notices it moving and races it; she deflects to the heater; 小林 shelves it on the free shelf and she takes it back (no-and). 6 CLIMAX (no-and). 7 January 5, the due date: the bookmark is behind the last page; she stamps 57.1.5 into the return space; he does not come for two days (yes-but). 8 he returns; she writes his number under the 1981 line and stamps a due date by hand; the computer still says 0; his white bookmark at 258 and the old one at the back.

new_words.栞: bookmark — the wrong detail and what the story's words recur on. First occurrence p7 falls out of the book onto the desk and is picked up, never defined. Recurs as page numbers every morning, as the boy's white one beside it, and as the last image
new_words.返却: return (of a library book) — first occurrence p1 in 返却ポスト being emptied before opening, the ordinary the story holds steady. Recurs in her rule, 返却されるまでお待ちください, and as the locked door behind the return box
new_words.貸出: lending, loan — first in the rule she gives the angry mother p5, then as the count on her monthly report, the title, the climax line and the 0 on his card
new_words.挟む: to put between, slip in — first p7 as an action, she slips the fallen bookmark back in at page 41. Recurs as 挟んであった each morning and in the last sentence
new_words.一冊: one (book) — her counting word. First p1 as the one book the machine will not read, then 一冊も本を借りたことがない, the zero she keeps writing down, and 一冊の本に栞が二枚

stories.title: 号令
stories._feature: First story on a non-object anchor, which AUTHORING.md § Gate 2 names as the test of the ANCHOR line. The anchor is a ritual, the 6:30 radio exercises in a park, and no clue is reinterpreted afterwards, and the reveal is a live event in the ritual's own geometry (who stands behind whom, who copies a wrong arm). Drafted in a container with no Anki or Ichiran, then checked locally on 2026-10-24 on real Ichiran tokens (have.py, check.py, stats.py --strict, peeks.py, reviews.py, rebuild.py). What the ritual carried at 553 tokens against a minimum of 4 occurrences: 音量 x4, 苦情 x4, 号令 x5 and 蝉 x4, each first occurrence inside an action. 体操 x11 is the anchor word but is already known in Anki, so the ritual carried it without it being a new word. About ten stretch words were replaced with plainer wording before the first local run, and 端, 一行, 返ってくる and まぎれる, plus three surnames, after it. Voice figures sit inside the authentic bands: past 64.4% (56.1-66.4), longest tense run 14 (11-15), ending entropy 5.59 (5.10-5.85), top-3 endings 22.8% (18.6-28.6). Title: 「号令」 over the all-kana 「いち、に、さん、し」, whose reading the harness's title-kana checks cannot carry; the slug keeps the working title. Weakest spot: p8, where only 村上 stays on time when the volume drops, which may let a careful reader guess early.
stories._note: NOBODY DIES AND NOBODY IS MOURNED. THE PLANTS ARE VEILED AS HABIT: 村上 stands directly behind her because 風が来んでな (p3, said unasked, filed by her as the wind); his deafness is a conversational joke (おはよう answered with 今日は暑くなるな) kept apart from the exercise until p18; she stands at the front left because つまみに手が届く (p2), which is why she moves to the middle on the last page; the cicadas are masked by the radio on p4 and are the first thing she hears on p16. PAYOFFS ARE PHYSICAL, NOT EXPLAINED: 村上 copies her wrong arm exactly while 小川 tells him 逆よ and he cannot hear her. The turn is p19, 「いち、に、さん、し」 counted aloud by the one person who had made a radio the authority; her voice breaks on し. She says only the weather at the end, and so does he. FACT CHECKED: 夜の仕事 was rejected because it reads as nightlife work; 夜に働いている人 is used because 夜勤 is unknown (see 回覧板の返事). 管理人, 町内会, 列, 拍, 深呼吸, 揃う, 背伸び, 水筒, 袖 and 提げる were each replaced by plainer wording because none occurs in the shipped corpus. CHECKED LOCALLY 2026-10-24 with Ichiran and Anki: 会長 逆 大事 暑い 帽子 天気 are known; 端, 一行, 返ってくる and まぎれる were unknown and are gone (端 dropped, 一行 became 一言, 返ってくる became 返事, まぎれる became 消される); 蝉 is unknown and declared. 田中 and 木村 segment as 田+中 and 木+村 and were renamed 村上 and 小川; 石井 is unknown and became 中島. 橋本, 村上, 小川 and 中島 segment whole. SPEECH: 橋本 〜でな / 〜そうだ, 村上 おう / 〜んでな, 小川 〜ね / 〜よ, 中島 です・ます to the chairman and plain form to nobody. THE TENSE RUN was 21 in the first draft and was broken with free indirect thought in ル (うまくいくはずがない。私は、そう思っていた) rather than by changing the events. 返事 (苦手, peeked in three stories) is reused twice on purpose, in the reply to おはよう and in the silence after 橋本's proposal.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: Monday, 6:30, the first morning without the radio. Thirty-eight people have come, more than she has ever counted, and the step of the slide where the radio sits is bare. Nobody starts, so she raises her arms herself, and without the announcer's count the front drifts to different speeds while the cicadas fill the park. At the arm-circling she loses the phrase and turns her arms the wrong way. Behind her a sleeve cuts the air in the same wrong direction: 村上, who is deaf and has stood behind her every morning for ten years. Beside him 小川 whispers 逆よ, and he hears nothing. He is not wrong, he is with her. She stops, and a beat later he stops, arms still up. She does not turn around. She corrects her arms and for the first time in that park counts aloud, loud enough for a deaf man, and her voice breaks on し. After the exercises 橋本 asks whether to bring the radio back, as agreed. She says このままで. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: in an early-August park, a 当番 who runs the 6:30 radio exercise by keeping the volume at her mark gets a noise complaint from a night-shift neighbour. Her fixes make the group ragged and it agrees to try a week of silence. She is certain it will fail. ANCHOR: the ritual, ラジオ体操 at 6:30 in the park in cicada season; new words 音量, 苦情, 号令, 蝉 (体操 anchors the ritual but is already known in Anki, so it is not declared). WANT: to keep the 6:30 radio playing at the volume she has always set. NEED: to admit that someone depends on her personally. She has built the group out of a radio, a rota and a rule so that no one would, and gives up the radio and her anonymity to get it. SHAPE: three-act. BEATS: ACT I (1) the ritual at full strength, the dial, 村上 behind her, everything in time; yes, but 橋本 relays a complaint, だから (2) she lowers the volume one notch; yes, but the next morning the front is ragged and only 村上 is untouched, which she files as a body that remembers, しかし ACT II (3) she turns it back up half a notch; no, and a second, one-remark complaint arrives, だから (4) Friday on the bench 橋本 proposes a week without the radio, back if it does not hold; yes, but she gets a trial she expects to win with her own radio on trial, だから (5) Saturday she makes the front row try the first half in silence to prove it; yes, but she has her proof and 小川 says ラジオが大事なのね, しかし ACT III (6) the climax above (7) Tuesday, a hot dawn breeze, the radio left at home, she stands in the middle, says 今日は、風が強いですね, 村上 says ああ、そうだな, and the story ends on the count under the cicadas.

new_words.音量: the volume of the radio, her one decision. First occurrence p1 in her hands, つまみを回して、音量を四のところに合わせる. Recurs as the dial lowered to three, the knob she looks at afterwards, and the half step back up
new_words.蝉: cicada, the sound the radio hides. First occurrence p4 as what she cannot hear, 蝉が鳴いているはずだが、ラジオの音に消されて、私には聞こえない, a consequence and not a gloss. Recurs p16 as the first thing she hears, p20 coming back loud, and as the closing image, 蝉の声の下で
new_words.苦情: complaint, from the night-shift neighbour. First occurrence p6 inside 橋本's message as a consequence, 苦情が出たそうだ. Recurs as the second complaint and as her own thought about long and one-remark complaints
new_words.号令: the count the radio instructor calls, いち、に、さん、し, and then hers. First occurrence p4 as an action, 先生が号令をかける. Recurs as the thing the children cannot keep up with, the thing she says is needed, and the thing she finally supplies herself

stories.title: 墨の量
stories._feature: First story with a real historical narrator: 紀貫之 on the voyage home from Tosa in 934-935, the voyage 土佐日記 records. He is never named in the text, as the corpus's narrators are not; the afterword names him. First first-person story set before the modern era, so the speech is held apart rather than made period-heavy: the boatman is rough (出せねえ, 通り抜けるぜ), the servant fawning (多うございまして), the wife ですます throughout as a woman answering her husband with distance, the narrator plain.
stories._note: THE INK IS THE CLUE AND THE WIFE'S OWN GRIEF. Planted as a wife's habit and a husband's non-thanks (p2, p6: she finishes grinding before he writes, it never runs short, 墨は高い物だから無駄にしない人なのだ), kept up through the dark pirate night when she grinds with no light to write by (p8), the sleeve and the bare feet (p9), the night the woman on the paper first cries while the wife sleeps and the ink is more than usual (p10), and the storm when she saves the bundle and he saves the paper (p13). The bundle is the child's sandals, planted p3 as 'a charm for a sea journey' in the narrator's own wrong guess and paid off p22. The real 土佐日記 ends with the narrator saying he will tear the diary up; here that line is p25 and the wife is why it survives. HISTORY, CHECKED AGAINST THE 土佐日記 TEXT (國文大觀) ON 2026-10-24: boarding on the 21st of the 12th month of 承平4 at the hour of the dog, and arrival at night on the 16th of the 2nd month of 承平5; the ship did not leave the shore until the 27th, the days between being farewell drinking, so the first draft's night departure on the 21st was wrong; the pirate fear, the prayers and the night crossings all fall late in the first month (23rd to 30th), not at the end of the 12th month as the first draft had it, and the narrator's own dread there is retaliation for his term as governor, so the subordinate's rumour of an attack last year is invented; the house kept by a neighbour who had asked to keep it (望みて預れる) and found ruined (家を預けたりつる人の心も荒れたるなりけり), the narrator sending a thank-you gift anyway (志をばせむ); the hollow like a pond with a pine at its edge, some of the pines gone and new ones among them, so the story's two pines and one small one are a reading of that; the poem 生まれしも帰らぬものを我がやどに小松のあるを見るがかなしさ, which the text says he said quietly to someone who knew his heart (密に心知れる人); and the last line 疾くやりてむ, where やる means to tear up or throw away. The wife is unnamed in the source and so is the child; the sandals, the sleeve, the ink and the whole climax conversation are invented. Fifty-five days by the diary's own count, so the text says only 何十日.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: night of the 16th of the 2nd month, the ruined Kyoto house, moonlight. His wife unwraps the bundle she carried the whole voyage and sets a child's red-threaded sandals at the foot of the small new pine. He sits down to write the pine poem as the woman, as he has every night. She opens a small inkstone with that morning's ink still wet and asks whether he will have that woman weep for him again. She says that she knew before he wrote a word, because on the nights he wept more ink was needed, and that the woman wept more than she did, and that while she wept for her, the wife slept well. He cannot answer; then says aloud, for the first time since the child died, that she was born here. He writes the poem without the word 女 and without a woman's voice, and his hand shakes. He says he will tear the diary up, and she takes it from his hand and puts it away in the opened bundle: tear it tomorrow. COST: the mask that let him grieve in private and be admired for it (the young subordinate wept at the reading), and the cheerful diary he sailed to write, which never gets finished. AFTERWORD: stories-index.md. PREMISE: a courtier writes his voyage diary as a woman, for fun; his wife grinds the ink every night and carries a bundle he never asks about. ANCHOR: the inkstone and the nightly grinding of ink, an object and a ritual together, carrying 墨 and 硯 through every scene, 海賊 and 草履 in the dark and the bare feet, and 荒れる in the ruined house. WANT: to reach the capital with a light, witty diary in kana, nothing in it about the daughter he lost in Tosa. NEED: to say aloud that she died, to the one person who has been grieving beside him in silence, instead of letting an invented woman do the crying. SHAPE: three-act. BEATS: (I) 1 the man's diary against the kana one, p1-2: he announces the joke diary, she grinds the ink and says only 'as you wish'; yes-but, he gets his diary and she watches the harbour until the waving hands are out of sight / 2 the bundle and the first jokes, p3-6: the young subordinate calls it a woman's diary and he is pleased, the boatman is mocked, the ink is always enough; yes-but, the diary is fun, and the wind will not let them leave | (II) 3 pirates, p7-8: no fire, no writing; no-and, she grinds ink in the dark anyway / 4 the boy's bare feet, p9-10: she binds them with her own sleeve in a steady voice, and that night the paper woman weeps while she sleeps; yes-but, the best page he has written, and ink more than usual / 5 the reading aloud, p11-12: the subordinate and the boatman weep, the narrator is proud, the wife at the rail says the wind has changed; no-and, he is praised and she leaves the room / 6 the storm, p13-15: he saves the paper, she saves the bundle; the funny pages are ruined and the weeping ones survive; he cannot write the laughing woman again, and she pours the unused ink into the sea; no-and, the want is breaking | (III) 7 the white blossoms and the river, p16-17: he starts to say he is looking forward to it and stops; yes-but, they arrive / 8 the house, p18-21: ruined, the neighbour's man full of excuses, the narrator handing over thanks in silence and not shouting, the hollow like a pond, one pine and a small one / 9 the climax, p22-24 / 10 p25: tear it tomorrow; the shadow of the pine on the sandals and the ink still wet.

new_words.墨: ink — the story's title and its clue. First occurrence p2 in the wife's hand, grinding it; recurs every night she grinds, in the dark on the pirate night, after the storm, as the unused ink poured into the sea, and as the last image, still wet.
new_words.硯: inkstone — the object at the centre. First occurrence p2 in her hand setting it down and starting to grind; recurs in the dark, in the storm, washed, tipped into the sea, and as the last image, ink still wet.
new_words.海賊: pirate — the danger that forces night sailing and the dark scene. First occurrence p7 in the boatman's plan, 昼に出れば見つかるから; recurs as the prayer in the sound of ink, p8.
new_words.草履: sandals — the bundle and the bare feet. First occurrence p9 in a child running without them; recurs p22 as what is in the bundle, laid at the foot of the pine.
new_words.荒れる: to go to ruin, run wild — first occurrence p19 as the consequence of neglect, the garden gone completely wild; recurs as the keeper's heart gone to ruin too, p19.

stories.title: 舌切り雀
stories._adaptation: Retelling of the traditional tale, after 楠山正雄 「舌切りすずめ」 (Aozora card 18378, author died 1950; text not copied, wording is ours). Plot, cast and ending kept as in the tale: the starch, the cut tongue, the walk to the bamboo thicket, the two boxes, the old woman's heavy box and the monsters. Replacements: 井戸ばた to 川; しば刈り to 木を切りに山へ; 座敷 to 家; ごちそう to plain 料理; さんご and 宝珠 to 金, 銀 and 宝; 入道 and 一つ目小僧 to 化け物 shown as a one-eyed thing and a snake; つづら to 箱; 睨む to the monsters speaking. Cut: the 一つ目小僧 names. Additions that are ours: the 糊-checking habit (plant), the cage door left open, the empty cage as the closing image.
stories._premise: CULTURE: PRACTICE: the お土産 at the end of a visit, in order. The host feeds the guest (もてなし), the guest rises to leave (おいとま), the host presses a stay (引き止める), then brings out gifts and lets the guest choose; the guest takes the lighter one (辞退, 遠慮), thanks the host (お礼), and the host sees the guest off at the gate (見送り). The old woman breaks every step: she will not sit, she asks for the gift before it is offered, she takes the heavy box, she leaves without お礼. Beside it runs her own work, the 洗濯 and the 糊, in a 台所 that is hers. PRESSURE: 遠慮, the old man's. He will not cross his wife in her own kitchen or over her own dish, so pity is all he lets himself say, and the empty cage is where it ends up. Her want is the opposite, 欲: a person with no 遠慮 at all, which is what the sparrow's politeness shows up. VOICES: the old man says わし, calls his wife ばあさん, speaks plain (だ, な, だろう, か) and is called おじいさん. The old woman says わたし, calls him おじいさん (never by a name), speaks ですます to him (ですよ, んです) and plain imperatives to the sparrow (おくれ, 決まっていますよ). The sparrow says わたし, is politeness itself to both of them (いらっしゃいました, お持ちください, 〜いらっしゃいな), and in the refrain 〜よ, the one place she is not formal. Nobody has a name; the tale has none and the sheet gives none. Era: むかし, a village, no 苗字. SEASON: none. The tale names no month and the retelling keeps it so on purpose, because adding one would be ours and not the tale's. This is a known cost under the SEASON test, since the story could move to any month without changing a beat, and the sheet critic should say whether it is acceptable for a traditional tale. ABSENT: kept: the refrain 舌切り雀、お宿はどこだ, the two boxes, the gate seeing-off, the bamboo thicket. Cut on purpose: つづら, which is a woven trunk, to 箱 because つづら is not in the known set and 箱 keeps the choice; the 恩返し frame of the oldest version (宇治拾遺物語 「腰折れ雀」), where a kind act is repaid, because the tale as told in 楠山 has no word for it and 恩返し is unknown; さんご and 宝珠 to 金, 銀 and 宝; 入道 and 一つ目小僧 to 化け物. Not added: a shrine, a New Year or any named festival. CARRIED: behaviour inside the known set carries all of it, namely もてなし, 引き止める, 選ぶ, 背負う, 見送る, 送る and the gate. New words: 糊 (the dish and the offence), 籠 (the cage), 欲 (the engine), 藪 and 野 (the walk). Brief ceiling 7, planned 5. Looked up: 洗い張り and the use of 飯糊 or ふのり for 糊 are real, but the exact boiling steps were not found, so nothing on the sheet depends on them. CLIMAX: night, the old woman on a roadside stone with the heavy box, lifts the lid a finger's width to look before home. The first thing out is a tongue, which licks her face; then monsters, one-eyed, snake-long, one all tongue; 「欲ばりばばあ」. She drops stick and box and runs; at the door she opens her mouth and no voice comes out. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: an old woman cuts out the tongue of her husband's sparrow over a dish of starch. He walks through fields and mountains to the sparrow's house and is sent home with a light box of treasure; his wife goes for the heavy one. ANCHOR: the walk and the call, 野を越え、山を越え / 舌切り雀、お宿はどこだ, said once by each of them, plus the two objects the tale hangs on, the 籠 and the dish of 糊; carries 糊, 籠, 欲, 藪 and 野. Chosen after the climax, since the tongues in the box answer the starch and the cage is what the old man comes home to. WANT: the old man wants to find the sparrow; the old woman wants the bigger box. NEED: the old man cannot cross his wife in her own kitchen, and has always called that kindness; the old woman has no need she faces, the tale gives her the want and its price. SHAPE: three-act, climax in the last quarter. BEATS: I 1 cage and the 糊 checked every morning (veiled plant) (yes-but: the dish is hers and watched, in her 台所). 2 the cage door left open, the sparrow licks the dish empty (no-and: she returns to the empty dish). 3 the tongue cut; the old man returns to the empty cage and only pities, and does not cross her (遠慮) (no-and). II 4 he walks out calling the rhyme and a voice answers from the thicket (yes-but: she speaks badly). 5 feast (もてなし) and dance, he rises to leave (おいとま) and is pressed to stay (引き止める), then two boxes: he takes the light one because he is old (辞退) (yes-but). 6 at home gold and silver; his wife is furious he left the heavy one, and 欲 is the word he uses (yes-but). III 7 she walks all night and asks for the gift before she has sat down, takes the heavy box and leaves without お礼 (no-and: the sparrow stays polite). 8 CLIMAX. 9 she runs home without a voice; he says only 「だから、言ったろう」 and shuts the empty cage (遠慮 broken at last, and too late to help).
stories._gate: No panel was run. Rob approved the English sheet in chat under the old Gate 2, before PANEL.md existed on main, and chose not to read the story, so the guesser, locator, transplanter and sheet critic have not read this sheet. The CULTURE block was written afterwards, from the draft, and not before it, which is the order the rule forbids; it records what the draft already does rather than shaping it. Open for the critic: the SEASON line, which is none on purpose, and whether the old woman breaking every step of the お土産 is enough Japan in the causes for the locator. The 洗い張り outline and the 飯糊 or ふのり starch were checked on secondary sources only.

new_words.糊: starch for washing, the dish she checks each morning and the whole offence. First occurrence p2 as an action, she tests it with her finger; recurs in the quarrel, the empty dish and the sparrow's apology
new_words.籠: cage, where the sparrow lives and what the old man comes home to. First occurrence p1 as where he puts the bird; recurs as the open door, the empty cage and the last image
new_words.欲: greed, from 欲を出す and 欲ばり, the tale's own engine. First occurrence p13 in the old man's mouth as a reproach; recurs as the monsters' word
new_words.藪: bamboo thicket, where the sparrow's house is hidden. First occurrence p8 as a voice answering from inside it; recurs on both journeys
new_words.野: open fields, the first half of the refrain 野を越え、山を越え. First occurrence p7 as the walk itself; recurs each time anyone walks to the thicket
