stories._brief: Batch 2026-11-13, story s4. Gate 1 settled by the pipeline, not Rob. pages 18 with page_slack 2 (16 to 20) because Rob asked for 15 to 20 pages. register comic overrides a quiet-realism draw, which s1 had already drawn; comic is the highest-rated register (回覧板の返事 ★5, 黄色い傘 ★4) and its 役割語 and dry dialogue answer the standing note that characters are generic. new_words 4 and leech_seeds 5 derived at ~360 tokens. Gate 2 sheet passed the panel on round 2; the critic's fact flags F1 to F5 (price of the beer, 年賀状, how the box is shipped, who gets the reunion photograph, the お中元/御中元 surface) were applied to the sheet before drafting.
stories._premise:
Level 3 (N3 voice), register comic, 18 pages (16 to 20; Rob asked for 15 to 20), new_words 4, leech seeds 5. Batch 2026-11-13, story s4; every Gate 1 parameter but length settled by the pipeline. Gate 2 passed on round 2 of the sheet panel; the round-2 critic's fact flags F1 to F5 (beer price, 年賀状, how the box is shipped, who gets the photograph, the お中元/御中元 surface) were applied below before drafting.

TITLE: 素麺とビール (そうめんとビール) · slug `soumen-to-biiru` · level 3 (N3 voice) · register comic · pages 18 ±2 (16 to 20; Rob asked for 15 to 20)

## CULTURE

**PRACTICE: お中元, run as a household procedure, in the order a Kanto household runs it.**

1. The last days of June. The wife opens the 贈答帳 (here the known word 手帳: a notebook that lists, per year, 誰に何を送ったか and 誰から何が来たか, with the price of each). Eleven names. She orders at the 百貨店's お中元ギフトセンター on a printed order form (申込用紙): the recipient's 住所 and 電話番号, the item, the 熨斗 wording. Delivery is booked for the first half of July.
2. The 百貨店 wraps and labels: printed 熨斗紙, red-and-white 蝶結び, 「御中元」 above the knot and the sender's surname below, 内のし for anything delivered. A 百貨店 order can carry a short message card. (Carried in the story as 紙, 字, カード: 熨斗 is not a new word.)
3. Delivery by 宅配便 (carried as 配達のトラック / 運転手) to arrive between early July and 15 July in the 首都圏 and 静岡, both 新盆 regions; most of the rest of the country runs to 15 August. Every 宅配便 label carries the sender's (ご依頼主) name, address and telephone number as well as the recipient's. 望月's beer does not come through a 百貨店: it is a 四千円 gift set from a shop in 静岡, and the 奥さん carries it to the コンビニ and fills in the 宅配便 slip by hand (F3), so the sender's number is on the box in the same hand as the postcard, and 大野 has seen that hand forty-four times. The number is not in the 手帳, which has a column for the item and a column for the price and no column for a number, and the box goes out with the Tuesday 資源ごみ. (F1) The gift set has been 四千円 every year; what has changed is the number of cans in it, twenty-four in 1979 and twelve now, which 大野 reads as 望月 being careful with money, the same reading he gives the empty December.
4. After the 15th the label changes: 「暑中御見舞」 until 立秋 (7 or 8 August), 「残暑御見舞」 after it. A gift that lands late is relabelled, not refused. (Carried on the page as the clerk's 十五日を過ぎていますので、紙の字が変わります; 暑中 is not bought.)
5. The recipient answers with an お礼状 (a postcard or letter within about three days, or a phone call). A return gift is not required. Between friends, siblings or colleagues, a gift of like value (同程度) may go back, also labelled 御中元; between unequal parties only the お礼状 goes. Two rules of the return gift, both quoted by the narrator as law: a return worth more than the gift received is rude (もらった物より高い物は失礼), and the same item is not sent back (同じ物は返さない).
6. Once begun, it continues every year. The polite ways to stop are to lower the value gradually or to replace the gift with a 暑中見舞い postcard saying 今後はお気遣いなく. A sudden stop with nothing in its place has no polite reading. It is a message.
7. Sources: SMBC Card ギフトカード column 「お中元のマナー」 (timing 関東 1 to 15 July; 暑中御見舞 after the 15th, 残暑御見舞 after 立秋; 目上 answers with 礼状 only, 友人や同僚、兄弟 return 同程度の品物); hugkum.sho.jp 617780 (arrive 7月初めから15日まで; 新盆 regions include the 首都圏 and 静岡; 熨斗紙 with 蝶結び, purpose above, full name below, 内熨斗 for shipped gifts; 「お中元をもらったら必ずお礼状を送ろう」); event.rakuten.co.jp/ochugen/howto/return (the return gift is 同程度 or less, 高価すぎるお返しは失礼, and 同じものをお返しに送らない); allabout.co.jp 456061 and moneypost.jp 805163 (stopping by switching to 暑中・残暑見舞い postcards, 今後はお気遣いなく); takashimaya.co.jp help guide99 (the 百貨店 gift order slip carries a field for the recipient's telephone number); Yamato Transport 送り状 layout (ご依頼主 name, address and telephone on every label).

**PRESSURE: 恩 and お返し.** 望月's beer is 4,000 yen; 大野's 素麺 was 1,500 and is now 1,800. By the only arithmetic 大野 knows, he is the debtor, and has been for forty-four years of 手帳 lines and three before the 手帳. A debtor does not ask after the next instalment: asking why the beer stopped is asking for beer, and a man who asks for a gift is a man who was counting on it. So the want (find out) cannot take the one road that would settle it in a minute, and the need underneath it (he wants 望月, not the beer; to be spoken to by him) cannot be said at all, because under 恩 what he owes is a thing and what he can send back is a thing, and the ledger has no column for a phone call. Test: take the pressure away. An American who has had a case of beer from a college roommate every July for forty-seven years rings him on the 12th and says "No beer this year? You dead, or just cheap?" and the story is over on page 3. Here the silence is held by the debt, and the moment the debt is shown to be a joke, he speaks.

**VOICES.**

- 大野, narrator, 71, born 1955, a Saitama suburb; joined a parts maker (部品メーカー) at 本社 in April 1977, two years in the 独身寮 beside 本社, then 本社 for the rest of it, retired as 課長. Married 1982. Narration 私, plain past, with the manners sites quoted as law (「〜のが決まりだ」; 決まり is known, 礼儀 is not and is not used) and every gift given with its price. To his wife: 俺, terse, 「いい」「分かってる」「〜だろう」, addresses her 「おい」 and never by name. To 望月 at the door: 望月さん and です・ます, because forty-seven years of 熨斗 have made the man formal; after the hat comes off, 望月, お前, 俺. Habit: describes his own head as 横にはまだある and his hat as 日のためだ.
- 大野の妻, 68, born 1958, unnamed in the text (私の妻, 家内 in his mouth). Married him in 1982 and started the 手帳 that year. Calls him あなた. 〜じゃない, 〜のよ, 〜でしょ. Answers a statement with a question, and quotes his own rules back at him (「あなたが言ったのよ」). Keeps the 手帳 and the prices in it. Her lines are short and she is always already doing something else while she says them.
- 望月, 71, born 1955, 静岡; the same 寮 room from 1977 to 1979, then the 工場 in 静岡 for forty years, 現場. Bald by twenty-four. Married 1983. お前, 俺, 〜だろ, 〜ぞ, 〜な, loud, laughs 「は」 in one syllable, calls his wife 母さん, calls 大野 bare 大野. His one written word for forty-seven years is 「まだまだ」. Answers the door in a ランニング. Says what he thinks the moment he thinks it, which is why the one thing he does not say (why he kept paying) is audible.
- 望月の奥さん, 69, unnamed (望月の奥さん). です・ます to a guest, 「この人」 for her husband, 〜ですよ, 〜ますから. Has written 「まだまだ」 at his dictation every July since 1983 and has her own opinion of it. Three lines and a plate of 素麺.
- 乾物屋の主人 (carried as 駅前の古い店の主人), seventies, has sold 大野 the same 素麺 since 1982. 〜だよ, 〜だね, 悪いね; remembers the destination before the customer does (「毎年、静岡だったね」). One scene, beat 1.
- 配達の運転手, thirties. です・ます, 「今日はないですね」「また明日来ますから」. One scene, beat 2; he does not return in beat 8.
- 百貨店の店員, twenties, woman. 「〜になりますね」「お届け先のお電話番号を」「なくても大丈夫ですよ」.

Names checked with Ichiran on this machine, in the forms the sheet uses (bare, さん, 様, の, before 、 and は): 大野 and 望月 survive whole in every form. 久保 was the round-1 name and splits as 久 + 保さん; 坂本 and 中村, suggested by the critic, split into single characters on this Ichiran (坂 + 本, 中 + 村) and were rejected. 望月 is the most common surname specific to 静岡 prefecture, which is where its bearer is from, and it is not used in the batch (s1, s2, s3, s5 names checked) or the corpus. Every 〜子 name tried for the wives (良子, 和子, 恵子, 文子, 敏子, 久美子) splits, which is why the two wives are 妻 and 奥さん, as a man of 71 narrates them anyway. 静岡 is whole in Ichiran and is carried in marker form (｜静岡《しずおか》) like a personal name.

**SEASON: July, as the thing the story is made of.** The 15th is the deadline that makes the silence legible, and the end of the 梅雨 around the 20th is when the queue at the 百貨店 stands in the first real heat. 素麺 is the July food and beer is the July drink; both gifts are chosen by the month. The sun on a bald head is July's own joke: the wife's クリーム, the hat 大野 will not take off, the 熱中症 she warns him about on known words (倒れるわよ), the twenty minutes uphill from 静岡 station with twenty-four cans. Test: move it to December and お歳暮. A hat in December hides nothing, 素麺 is not a winter gift, there is no 15th that flips a label, and nobody carries beer uphill in the cold for comedy. The story does not move.

**ABSENT.**

- In: お礼状, two postcards a July, both in wives' handwriting since 1983. From 静岡: the 奥さん's postcard of thanks for the 素麺, arriving around the 11th, and 望月's card with the beer (「まだまだ」, in his own hand 1979 to 1982, in hers since). From Saitama: the wife's postcard of thanks for the beer, within three days of the 10th. The narrator reads the whole channel as how things are done; the reader may read it as how little the two men have ever said. **This year** the 奥さん's postcard for the 素麺 comes on the 11th as always, in her hand, thanks for the noodles, nothing about beer. So 大野 knows by the 11th that the house is alive, that the 素麺 arrived, and that the silence is not an accident. The postcard is on the table in beat 2.
- In: 同窓会 (the 寮's January reunion; 望月 absent; the group photograph mailed in February by the man who ran it, carried as 同窓会を開いた男, to everyone on the 寮 list whether they came or not (F4), which is how 望月 has seen it; that man has every number in the room). In: the 百貨店 order form and its telephone field. In: the 宅配便 label's sender field, as the place the number has been forty-seven times. In: 熱中症 and 日焼け止め, carried on 倒れる and クリーム. In: 暑中御見舞 as the label after the 15th, carried on the clerk's 紙の字が変わります and the manners site's 夏の見舞いの葉書.
- Out, on purpose: お歳暮. Nothing comes from 望月 in December, and the narrator has always read that as 望月's economy. A true 中元 relationship between households would usually run both ends of the year; a bet about July beer runs one. The absence is a plant, named once in beat 1, and 大野 pays it himself on the step (「だから十二月には何も来なかったのか」). In: 年賀状 (F2), one each January between the two wives since 1983, printed, with the address under the names and no telephone number, as the wives print them; so the number has still never been anywhere but a 宅配便 label, and the 年賀状 give 大野 nothing on the 20th but the address he already has. Out: 半返し (belongs to 内祝い, not 中元). Out: 仲人 and 上司 (the equals rule is the point). Out: お盆 and 帰省 (the story ends on 31 July). Out: 蝉 (not in the known set; the heat is carried by 暑さ, 汗, 日).

**CARRIED.** On known words: ビール, 帽子, 髪, 寮, 同窓会, 百貨店, 売り場, 葉書, 見舞い, お返し, 恩, 義理, 負け, 勝ち, まだまだ, 脱ぐ, 箱, 紙, 住所, 電話番号, 番号, 運転手, 玄関, 値段, 冷蔵庫, 冷やす, 汗, 暑さ, 塗る, 決まり, 失礼, 捨てる, 母さん, ランニング, 扇風機, 坂, 駅前, 用紙. Leech seeds available where they fall: 贈る, 送る, 配達, 遠慮, 計算, 手帳, 工場, 合計, 過ぎる, 遅れる (ten; the brief wants five). New words, four, at the cap: お中元, 素麺, 賭け, 禿げる (have.py: all four ✗; 中元, そうめん, 賭ける, 禿げ also ✗). Not bought, with what carries each: 熨斗 (紙), 伝票 and 申込用紙 (用紙), 宅配便 (配達のトラック), 同期 (同じ年に入った), 贈答帳 (手帳), 幹事 (同窓会を開いた男), 定年 (会社を辞めてから), 万円 (〜円), 礼儀 (決まり), 手ぶら (ビールなしで来い), 乾物屋 (駅前の古い店), 梅雨明け (梅雨が終わった日; 明ける is unknown), 暑中 (紙の字が変わる; 夏の見舞いの葉書), 担ぐ (持つ), 返済 (返す). Place name: 静岡, marker form, whole in Ichiran. Every quoted line in CLIMAX and BEATS was run through check.py on this machine: the only unknowns are the four new words and the two names.

## CLIMAX

31 July, two in the afternoon, 35 degrees, the step of 望月's house on a hill above 静岡 station. 大野 has carried a 百貨店 box of twenty-four cans two hours by train and twenty minutes uphill, in the hat, the shirt gone dark down the back, the 手帳 page with the address in his pocket. He has a sentence ready and has said it to the train window eleven times: 「四十七年、お返しが足りませんでした」. He rings. 望月 opens the door in a ランニング, bald to the ears, looks at the box, looks at the hat, and says nothing about the beer. 「脱いでみろ」. 「は？」 「帽子だ」. 大野 takes it off. 望月 looks at the top of his head for one long second and laughs the 寮 laugh, one syllable. 「やっぱりな。写真の通りだ」.

Then he says it, plainly, and this is the reveal. 「寮で賭けをしただろう。先に禿げた方が、禿げてない方に、毎年七月、ビールを一箱。両方禿げたら、終わりだ」. 大野 has not thought of it in forty years, and it comes back whole as 望月 says it: the 寮 room, the summer of 1978, the cans on the floor, 望月's hairline already going and 望月 proposing it loud, and himself at twenty-three with all his hair taking a bet he could not lose. 望月 goes on: 「一月の写真を見た。お前も禿げてる。だから、終わりだ」. 大野 has begun his sentence anyway, 「四十七年、お返しが…」, and 望月 looks at the box on the step: 「お返し？は。で、お前が持ってきたのか。じゃあ今年はお前の負けだな」. 大野: 「忘れてたんだ」. 望月: 「知ってる。素麺が来るたびに、こいつ忘れてるな、と思ってた。だから止めれば、電話ぐらいしてくると思ったんだ。お前、ビールを持って来たのか」. From the hall behind him, the 奥さん: 「この人、賭けに負けたって、毎年『まだまだ』って私に書かせるんですよ」.

Then 大野 does the arithmetic he is good at, on the step, aloud, and this is the protagonist paying the plants (Rob's 鍵とチェーン note). 「だから十二月には何も来なかったのか」. 望月: 「十二月に何を送るんだ」. 「まだまだ、は、髪か」. 「他に何がある」. And in thought, in a run of four short sentences: 望月 lost his hair at twenty-four and that was the bet, not the 工場; the photograph was not a bad photograph, it was the end of the bet; and the 素麺, by the book, every July since his wife opened the 手帳, was the thing that told 望月 he had forgotten. 望月 does not say why he kept sending after he knew. He is asked nothing, and the sheet keeps it that way.

What 大野 pays, in order: the hat, in the sun, in front of a man he has not seen in forty-seven years; the apology, which is half out of his mouth when it becomes ridiculous; the arithmetic, which was the whole of his standing in the friendship (the gracious under-returner who owed and knew it) and which has just been shown to have no debt in it, only a joke he lost; and the want itself, since he is standing on the step asking. The turn is in his register. He arrived at 望月さん and ご無沙汰しております. What he says next is 「望月。重いんだ、これ。中に入れろ」.

TWIST: the beer was never お中元. It is the stake of a bet made in the 寮 in the summer of 1978 about who would go bald first, paid by 望月 every July since 1979, labelled 御中元 only because a July parcel from a Japanese household goes out that way, and kept up though 望月 had known for decades, from the 素麺 that came back by the book, that 大野 had forgotten the bet. It stopped this year because the February photograph showed both of them bald and the bet ends when both are; 望月 expected the missing beer to produce a phone call, not a man with a box. 望月 states it, in speech, at the door, and understands it completely; 大野 remembers it as it is said and then works the plants out aloud.

## AFTERWORD

See stories/stories-index.md, ## Afterwords, where it lives. Written at Gate 2 and revised to the final text at drafting: the narrator is unnamed there because he is unnamed in the story, and the page reference for the cream follows the draft.

## PREMISE

Every July for forty-seven years a case of beer has come to 大野 from 望月, who shared his company dormitory room in 1977, and every July 大野 has had a box of 素麺 sent back. This year the fifteenth passes and no beer comes. 大野 has never once telephoned 望月, and he does not intend to start over beer.

## ANCHOR

The July box, and the one line it occupies each year in his wife's 手帳: a 四千円 beer set one way (「望月様よりビール 四千円」, twenty-four cans in 1979 and twelve now, F1), a box of 素麺 the other (「望月様へ素麺 千五百円」, and this year 千八百円), a label that says 御中元, a card that says 「まだまだ」. The box 大野 carries uphill is twenty-four cans from the 百貨店 beer aisle, 五千八百円 (F1), which breaks his own rule about value as well as the rule about the same item, and is twice what 望月 has been sending. Everything in the story is done to, with, or about that box: ordered, waited for, computed, relabelled, carried uphill, set on a step, eaten under a fan. It carries the four new words. お中元 (the label on every box and the name of the season, ten or more occurrences; declared once as お中元 and written on two surfaces on purpose, お中元 in narration and speech, 御中元 on the paper, with the occurrence floor counted across both, F5). 素麺 (every reply, the 5 July order, the 奥さん's postcard, the plate at the end, eight or more). 賭け (five uses, every one after the reveal: 望月 「寮で賭けをしただろう」 at the door; the 奥さん 「賭けに負けたって」 from the hall; 大野 in thought on the step, 賭けだったのか; 望月 at the table 「賭けは終わりだ」; 大野 at home 「寮の賭けだ」; against a floor of three at ~400 tokens). 禿げる (望月 at twenty-four in beat 1, the bet's wording at the door, 先に禿げた方 / 禿げてない方 / 両方禿げたら, 「お前も禿げてる」: five or six). Nothing else is new. The 手帳 is a leech word and rides for free.

## WANT

To find out why 望月's beer has stopped, without asking 望月.

## NEED

He has taken forty-four years of correctly answered gifts for forty-seven years of friendship, and he has no way to reach 望月 that is not a box with a label on it.

## SHAPE

Three-act, eight beats. Act I, beats 1 and 2 (about pages 1 to 4): the exchange and its deadline, the plants laid as a wife nagging and a man being gracious. Act II, beats 3 to 6 (about pages 5 to 13): the want pursued by the book, and the book convicting him at every step, the need surfacing at the 百貨店 counter as a blank on a form. Act III, beats 7 and 8 (about pages 14 to 18): the step, and the table. Chosen over two-act because the comedy needs the long middle in which a man does everything correctly and nothing right; chosen over five-act because what happens after the climax is a plate of noodles and a train, one beat, and five acts would make it two.

Connectives written honestly: 1→2 しかし; 2→3 だから; 3→4 だから; 4→5 だから; 5→6 しかし; 6→7 だから; 7→8 しかし. The だから run through the middle is the straight line of a man following instructions; beats 5 and 7 are where it breaks.

## BEATS

**Act I**

1. The last days of June. 大野's wife opens the 手帳 (the household 贈答帳) at the kitchen table and fills the 百貨店's お中元 order form (申込用紙) for eleven names, 住所 and item and price. 大野's one job in this, every year since 1982, is 望月's 素麺, which he buys at the old shop by the station (乾物屋, carried as 駅前の古い店) and not at the 百貨店, because the 百貨店's is dear (planted as thrift; it is the price gap). The 素麺 goes out on the 5th, before the beer it answers, because the beer has never once failed to come by the 10th and the wife moved the お返し forward years ago so it would reach 静岡 by the 15th (planted as a wife's efficiency; it is an お返し paid in advance on forty-seven years of credit, and it is why this year he has already paid for a gift that did not come). Four lines of history, as a column and not a sequence: the 独身寮 beside 本社 in 1977, the same room; 望月 to the 工場 in 静岡 in the spring of 1979, 大野 to 本社; the beer every July since 1979, 御中元 on the paper, 四千円 in the 手帳, and a card that has said 「まだまだ」 for forty-seven years, in 望月's hand at first and in the 奥さん's since he married, which 大野 reads as a factory man saying he is still standing. 望月 lost his hair before he was twenty-five (禿げる, first occurrence, inside the narrator's pity: それは工場のせいだと思っている). Nothing comes in December (お歳暮), which 大野 puts down to 望月's economy. On the shelf, the January 同窓会 photograph, posted in February by the man who ran it to everyone on the 寮 list: 望月 did not come, 遠いから; 大野 is in it without his hat because the man said 帽子は取って, and he thinks it a bad photograph. One line, as scenery. His wife hands him the hat and the クリーム on his way to the shop: 「頭に塗ってよ。倒れるわよ」. 「日のためだ」. At the shop the old man has the box ready before 大野 speaks (「毎年、静岡だったね」) and tells him, 「悪いね、今年から千八百円だよ」. **Yes, but:** the 素麺 goes out on the 5th with 御中元 and 大野 on the paper, as always, and 大野, who knows the other figure to the yen, does the subtraction on the walk home for the first time in his life.

2. The 10th, the day the beer has come for forty-seven years: nothing. The 11th: the 奥さん's postcard (お礼状) for the 素麺, in her hand, as every year, thanks for the noodles, nothing else. So the house is alive and the noodles arrived. The 12th. The 配達 truck stops at the neighbours' and 大野 waits by the 玄関 and asks the 運転手, the one man he can ask: 「うちには？」 「今日はないですね。また明日来ますから」. His wife, from the sink, with the postcard: 「元気じゃない。電話すれば？」 「ビールのことで電話できるか」 (asking after a gift is asking for a gift: 恩, said as a man's dignity). The 15th passes, and with it the Kanto date. He reads on his telephone that a gift after the 15th goes out under a different word (暑中御見舞, carried as 紙の字が変わる) and that switching to a summer postcard (暑中見舞い, carried as 夏の見舞いの葉書) is how people end an exchange politely (辞退, 今後はお気遣いなく). **No, and:** no beer has come, and now even beer would come under the wrong paper, and no postcard has come either, so whatever 望月 is doing he is not doing it politely, and he is doing it on purpose.

**Act II**

1. He takes the 手帳 to the table and does what he knows how to do. Forty-four lines of 望月様よりビール 四千円 and forty-four of 望月様へ素麺 千五百円, 1982 to 2025, every line the same, and three Julys before the 手帳 that he counts from memory, beer with nothing against it. He computes it (計算, 合計): 二千五百円 × 四十四 = 十一万円, plus 四千円 × 三 = 一万二千円, 十二万二千円 in 望月's favour. He has his answer and it is him: forty-four years of お返し at less than half (同程度 is the rule between friends, and he has read the rule), and 望月, who said 「まだまだ」 for forty-seven years, has finally said enough. **Yes, but:** he has a cause for the silence, and the cause convicts him.

2. The cure by the book. The debt is cleared in kind: a 百貨店 gift, ham, 五千円, the classic, labelled for after the 15th, and no card, because a card would explain and explaining admits the count. His wife: 「ハム？望月さん、ハム好きなの？」 「知らん」. Then, drying her hands: 「五千円？もらった物より高いのは失礼なんでしょ。あなたが言ったのよ」. He has said it. He says the ham is 四千円 with the tax off, which it is not. **No, and:** he now needs the 百貨店, and the 百貨店 needs the 手帳, and the 手帳 is where the forty-four lines are.

3. The 20th, the day the 梅雨 ends, the 百貨店's お中元 corner in the first real heat, a queue of forty under the lights with the hat on, cream under it. At the counter the 店員 fills the order form (用紙) from the 手帳 page: 住所, 静岡, the ham, and the label (「十五日を過ぎていますので、紙の字が変わります」). Then: 「お届け先のお電話番号を」. He has none. He has had it forty-seven times: it is printed on the sender's half of every 宅配便 label, under 望月's name, and every one of those labels went out on a Tuesday with the box it was stuck to, because the 手帳 has a column for the price and none for a number. He thinks of the man who ran the 同窓会 (幹事), who posted the photograph and has every number in the room, and does not ring him either, because that man would ask what for, and the answer is beer. 「なくても大丈夫ですよ」, the clerk says, and he says he will come back tomorrow, and does not. **No, and:** he leaves without the ham, and what he carries home is the blank on the form, which he does not name, to his wife or to himself.

4. His wife, who has watched him not go back for three days: 「じゃあ、持っていけばいいじゃない。住所、ここにあるんだから」. A man does not turn up at a door in July with a box (he says this; it is in fact exactly what a summer 見舞い visit is). She puts the hat on his head, the cream in his pocket and the 手帳 page in his shirt. He does not buy ham. He stands in the 百貨店's beer aisle with the rules in his head and none of them usable: more than 四千円 is rude, the same item is not sent back (同じ物は返さないのが決まりだ), and a card would explain. He keeps away from the お中元 counter where the clerk is, and buys twenty-four cans of the brand 望月 has sent, 五千八百円 (F1: more than 四千円, and twice the twelve cans 望月 now sends), against both rules and knowing it, for the one reason the book does not cover: ham was a guess, and the only thing he knows about 望月 after forty-seven years is what he drinks (望月について私が知っているのは、このビールだけだった). **Yes, but:** he is going, which is what he swore not to do, with the one gift the rules forbid, for a debt that is about to turn out not to exist, on the hottest day of the month, uphill.

**Act III**

1. CLIMAX, as above: the step, the hat, 「脱いでみろ」, the bet (賭け) stated by 望月 in two sentences, 「両方禿げたら、終わりだ」 as written there, the photograph, 「今年はお前の負けだな」, 「電話ぐらいしてくると思ったんだ」, the 奥さん's 「賭けに負けたって、毎年『まだまだ』って」, and 大野 paying the plants aloud: 十二月, まだまだ, the hair at twenty-four, the photograph, the 素麺. 大野's apology dies in his mouth at 四十七年、お返しが. The turn is his next line and its register: 「望月。重いんだ、これ。中に入れろ」. **No, and:** he has his answer, and with it he has lost the bet, the hat, the arithmetic and the standing it gave him, and is standing bareheaded in the sun on a step in 静岡 holding the loser's beer.

2. Inside, under the fan (扇風機): the 奥さん puts out 素麺, his own, from the 5th, cold, and two cans from the box, and says the 素麺 is to keep coming, please, 「あれだけは、毎年楽しみにしてますから」 (resolves her, and keeps the one honest gift in the story alive with nothing left to return). 望月, eating: 「賭けは終わりだ。来年はビールなしで来い。飲むのはうちのだ」. 大野 asks why he never rang, and 望月 pays the number from his side: 「番号？箱に書いてあっただろう。母さんが箱ごと捨てる」. 大野 says 「分かった」 to the first and nothing to the second, and the hat stays on the floor by the box. On the train home, hatless, the sun through the window on his head, he does what he does: 素麺 千八百円, ビール 五千八百円, both lines his. (The walk with the truck is cut; the driver was resolved on the 12th with 「また明日来ますから」, and the train goes straight to the kitchen.) At home his wife asks 「で、まだまだって何だったの？」 and he says 「髪だ。寮の賭けだ」 and she laughs in the kitchen for a long time. Last line, a plain fact: 今年は、両方、私が払った。 **Yes, but:** the ordinary resumes, and he is still counting, and now the count is of his own money.

## DRAFTING NOTES

Where the draft (20 pages after draft-panel round 1) departs from the sheet above, recorded so the readers can check against the text and not the plan:
- 大野 is never named in the story. 望月 calls him お前 and the wife calls him nothing; the name stays on the sheet only. At the door the narrator opens with 「望月さん、お久しぶりです」 and 「はい？」; after the hat comes off he says 「忘れてたんだ。俺は、すっかり」, bare 望月 with 中に入れろ, and お前 at the table (「お前こそ、なぜ電話してこなかった」). To his wife he uses 俺 once (「ビールのことで、俺が電話できるか」). ご無沙汰しております is not used (無沙汰 is not known).
- The wife's 「おい」 is not used. The hat habit line 日のためだ became 「いい。帽子があるだろう」 after both Japanese-only readers read it as English. 望月 has 俺, 〜ぞ, 〜な, one Shizuoka 〜だら (「寮で賭けをしただら」), and narration marks his voice as loud.
- 賭け occurs seven times, not five; お中元 six times across both surfaces (お中元 three, 御中元 three), not ten or more, which clears the floor of five.
- In thought on the step the narrator says 賭けだ, not 賭けだったのか.
- Beat 6: the rules counted in the beer aisle are もらった物より高い物は失礼 and 同じ物は返さない; the card rule is not repeated there. He stands where the clerk cannot see him, which takes the round-2 critic's optional note on closing the clerk.
- Beat 8: the 奥さん's line is 「素麺だけは、毎年楽しみにしてますから。あれは、やめないでくださいね」. The walk with the truck is cut as the critic asked; the driver closes on the 12th with 「また明日来ますから」.
- The phone number is on the delivery slip pasted on the box (箱に貼ってある配達の紙), in 望月's hand at first and his wife's after he married; 箱の紙 is kept for 御中元 and the name. At the table the narrator asks why 望月 never rang, 望月 answers that he has only ever seen the number on the 素麺 box's delivery slip and 母さん throws the box out, and the narrator says nothing because his own house does the same.
- Beat 2: the phone lookup covers only what a sudden stop means and the polite stop by postcard (見舞いの葉書); the 15th label change is left to the clerk, who says 「紙は御中元ではなく、お見舞いになりますね」. The ham line no longer names the label.
- Beat 6: the narrator objects to the wife that turning up after forty-seven years is the same as going to ask where the beer is, not that hand delivery is wrong.
- At the door 望月's second 「お前、ビールを持って来たのか」 is replaced by 「それが、ビールを持って坂を上ってくるとはな」, so it no longer repeats 「で、お前が持ってきたのか」.
- The narration line 日の中に立っている became 頭に、七月の日がまっすぐ当たっている; 自分にできることをした became 一ページ目から開いた; 私のすることをした on the train became writing both prices on the back of the 手帳 page.
- Years are written 一九七八年 and 一九七九年 (furigana せんきゅうひゃく...), not 千九百....
stories._gate: Gate 2 passed on round 2 of 3. Round 1 sent the sheet back for the climax and the afterword timeline under withhold, never confuse (the climax's two accounts of what 望月 expected did not agree, and the marriages, the 寮 and the start of the 素麺 did not add up), for Plants under the 鍵とチェーン note (the narrator had to work the plants out aloud after the reveal), for Characters, for PRACTICE and inside the culture at the level of fact (a same-item return rule stated backwards, and a phone number that was on every delivery label), for ABSENT (the 素麺's thank-you postcard this year), for VOICES (the first surname split in Ichiran and was renamed) and for CARRIED (賭け planned four times and written once). The guesser reported no leak in either round and no guess reached the bet as a mechanism; the locator placed it in present-day Kanto from the gift calendar, the cutoff on the 15th and the relabelling; the transplanter broke every beat, the climax and the need-beat included, named 恩 and お返し as the pressure lost, and found the need would be said aloud on the phone once the pressure was gone. Round 2 passed with fact flags on the beer's price, the 年賀状, how the box is shipped, who receives the reunion photograph and the お中元 and 御中元 surfaces, all applied before drafting. Draft stage: two Japanese-only readers and one English-only reader. Draft round 1 was sent back by the reconciler for a split turn on the phone-number exchange (speaker attribution), a duplicated line, three fact objections both Japanese-only readers raised (carrying a gift in person, the phone number on the wrong paper, the label rule looked up on a phone), the two men's voices under VOICES and Rob's standing note on generic characters (both readers found the narrator and 望月 hard to tell apart), translation-shaped lines, a present-tense slip in the English and afterword sentences. Draft round 2 passed, and its ship fixes were mechanical: the summer-greeting label, the 手帳 years against the three remembered ones, the shop holding the 素麺's price, translation-shaped lines, the laugh, speaker tags in the English and afterword sentences. Endings: in both rounds all three readers chose the last line, the fact that this year he paid for both, where intended; the English-only reader would have stopped one line earlier, on the prices written on the back of the 手帳 page. Twist: all three found the bet stated at the reveal by 望月 at the door and nowhere earlier; the English-only reader saw the hair and the photograph coming, which the afterword intends. Both Japanese-only readers named the お中元 procedure and 恩 and お返し, and found the communication natural. Naturalness rose by a step between rounds, the two Japanese-only readers agreeing each time, with the remaining loss put down to known-word paraphrases (紙 for the のし, 配達の紙 for the slip) and a few English-shaped lines. Left as flagged: one reader's objection that お中元 needs no return gift and that the dearer-is-rude rule belongs to お祝い (the narrator is meant to misread rules), the queue at the counter, and the English-only reader's view that the coda restates the reveal, declined by the author. 暑中 is not a known word, so the late label is 夏のお見舞い.

new_words.お中元: the midsummer gift, and the name of the season it is sent in — the label on every box in the story. Written お中元 in narration and speech and 御中元 on the paper, both surfaces on purpose, one entry. First occurrence p1 inside the wife filling in the order form, an act and not a gloss; recurs as the label, the deadline, the counter and the thing the beer was never
new_words.素麺: the thin summer noodles the narrator sends back every July — the other half of the exchange and the one honest gift in it. First occurrence p1 in the act of buying it at the old shop by the station; recurs as the 手帳 line, the postcard of thanks, and the plate at the end
new_words.賭け: a bet — what the beer was all along. Every occurrence comes after the reveal: first in 望月's mouth at the door, then the 奥さん's, then the narrator's, at the table and at home
new_words.禿げる: to go bald — the bet's whole subject. First occurrence p3 inside the narrator's pity for a friend who lost his hair at twenty-four; recurs in the bet's wording at the door and in 望月's verdict on the photograph

stories.title: 吉田さんの順番
stories._premise: CULTURE: PRACTICE: 有給休暇の申請と年5日の取得義務, as a procedure (proposed AXES value LEAVE_AND_COVER). Every employee with ten or more days of annual leave must take five within a year of the grant date, and it is the employer who is in breach if not (労働基準法第39条第7項, in force April 2019; managers covered). Days are granted each April 1, carry over a year and lapse after two, so March 31 is when the oldest days vanish and head office counts the five. A day is taken on a paper 休暇届 (name, kind of leave, dates, reason written 私用, seal in the first box); the 課長 stamps the second, the clerk carries it to the 支店長 for the third and records the days on the leave register (管理簿, the 有休の表), kept three years. Cover notes (引き継ぎ) are written before a day off. A superior may fix the dates himself (時季指定) after hearing the employee's wishes (意見聴取); the chief's pre-filled form is his own way of asking them, and the draft does not call it the legal procedure. Until last year this company met the five by planned leave (計画年休: three New Year days and two at Obon, branches shuttered); an inspection at another branch found staff working on those days and a correction notice followed, so from this April the shutter days became company holidays that do not count, the work rules were amended to allow 時季指定, and this March is the first list of names at zero, and the first time in thirty-six years 吉田 has been on any list. The fine is up to 300,000 yen per employee (第120条, secondary sources only). Attendance is on a system but leave is still paper, though head office has twice announced the end of seals. PRESSURE: 遠慮, sealed by 察し. A head-office chief does not ask the floor to carry his private want at year end; he hands it to the clerk as 余裕があったら, and the clerk is expected to read it correctly, and has, for thirty-six years. VOICES: 柴田剛, 46, 課長, narrator, Tokyo head-office man two Aprils into a three-year rotation, wife and daughter (中学三年) in Tokyo, alone in a 会社のアパート; 私; です・ます up, plain down; gives every instruction by handing over paper; never once spoken to in dialect. 吉田明美, 57, 一般職 clerk, thirty-six years at this branch, local; わたし; complete short です・ます to the chief, the city's speech (〜け, 〜ちゃ) with 村田 and the branch manager; answers a question with a fact about paper or a date; keeps the register, the stamps and the floor's one key; never apologises. 高木修, 64, 支店長, retires the March after this one, the last local 課長 before head office began posting the job from Tokyo twenty-one years ago; わし, blunt, calls head office 東京 and the clerk 吉田くん; reads head-office mail aloud and hands it over as the instruction; holds that a head-office man settles his own line with Tokyo. 村田翔, 28, 営業, local, slack polite (〜っすね) to the chief, dialect with 吉田; wants his Friday for a school friend's wedding. All eight names survive Ichiran whole. SEASON: March as the subject: the year-end count, the lapse, his transfer season, the daughter's high-school results and junior-high graduation; snow in the car park corners when the list comes, gone on the 31st. CALENDAR: March 2027 (the 1st a Monday, the 22nd the substitute holiday for 春分の日, the 31st a Wednesday); Friday is head-office paper day, the bank is crowded on the 10th, 15th, 25th and month end; list and results Tuesday the 2nd, wedding Friday the 5th, sweets Monday the 8th; his first form the 10th, 12th, 15th, 17th, 19th; climax the 9th or 10th; his five the 15th to 19th, graduation the 19th; back Tuesday the 23rd; hers the last five working days. ABSENT: 計画年休 kept as the reason this is the first list (会社が決めた正月の休み); 高校受験 and results kept as the wife's message; the transfer notice background only; 送別会 out; 決算 present as the March figures; 単身赴任 present in behaviour; 意見聴取 kept as beat 3; 労働基準監督署 kept as 国の検査が入った; tea-serving cut on purpose; her sick days named once in 村田's mouth. CARRIED: 休暇 + 届, ハンコ, 押す, 本社, 課長, 引き継ぎ, 引き出し, 鍵, 決める, 渡す, 順番に, 黙る, 法律, 余裕, 挨拶, 正月, 新幹線, 卒業, 式, 理由のところ (私用 rendered いつもの言葉); 判 to ハンコ, 朝礼 to 最初の朝の挨拶, クレーム to お客からの電話, 社宅 to 会社のアパート, 時季指定 to 課長が決める. New words, four, all in the anchor: 有休, 支店, 支店長, 出勤. Leech seeds: 書類, 表, 手帳, 遠慮, 営業. CLIMAX: an evening in the second week of March, after seven, the floor dark but the chief's lamp. Having fixed her five as the month's last five working days and told her he will lock up, he goes to her desk for the register and cover notes. The register is not in the drawer; the third drawer holds a stack of leave forms in order, each stamped once by its writer and never by the branch manager: his own August form on top, his predecessor's Golden Week under it, seven chiefs before him, the oldest dated twenty-one years back; 村田's wedding form is not among them. Her key turns in the door: there is one key, it is hers. He does not put the forms down; his voice is louder than he means. She does not apologise: his stamp is on them, only the branch manager's is missing, she threw nothing away. TWIST, stated by 吉田: 出さなかったのは、わたしです。課長は、来ますから. Every head-office chief said 休みは遠慮なく on his first morning, wrote himself a form for his first long holiday, handed it over with 余裕があったら, and came in on its first morning; she holds such a form until then, and if he is at his desk it goes in the drawer. A day off on her register for a day the person came in is a lie, and her own five are the same: fix them and she will come in. What would make it true is someone in her chair; if he sits there she will come in to stop the nuisance. He crosses out August on his own form, writes the 15th to the 19th, says 私が先に休む。五日。東京に帰る。娘が中学を卒業する, and hands it over as 明日、支店長に出してくれ, not 余裕があったら. She reads the dates, names Friday as paper day, says she will teach 村田 the bank-day work, and sets her five after he is back: she still decides the order. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: two years into a posting at a provincial branch, a head-office section chief is handed a list: the clerk who has run his floor for thirty-six years has taken no paid leave this year, and the law wants five days on the register by March 31; the branch manager wants no call from Tokyo, and every date he proposes comes back with a reason from the calendar. ANCHOR: the leave form and 吉田's desk, where the forms go and where nobody but her has ever sat; handed across a desk on the first morning, written for her in beat 3, remembered in beat 4, found in a stack of eight in beat 6, re-dated at the climax, its figure written into the register on the last page; carries 有休, 支店, 支店長, 出勤. WANT: five days of paid leave on 吉田's line of the register before March 31. NEED: he can give any order about work and cannot ask for anything for himself, and in two years away from his family has stopped noticing that he wants anything. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2, II 3-6, III 7-8. BEATS: I 1 高木 reads the head-office notice and the planned-leave paragraph aloud; two names from the section, 吉田 and 柴田; 君はいい … 吉田くんを何とかしろ; leave still on paper; 村田's wedding form stamped unread and carried by her; the wife's 合格 answered in two characters (yes-but). 2 he asks her in passing; the bank is crowded; 課長は、いつ取られますか / 私はいい / そうですか; she goes quiet (no-and). II 3 he fills in a form in her name, five mid-March dates; it comes back with a reason for each, none refused; 高木 asks every morning (no-and). 4 the wedding sweets, his desk last; 村田 on six years without a day, the fever winter, the last chief's spring request; that night he remembers his own first-morning promise and the August form handed over 余裕があったら, and the customer who made him come in all five days (yes-but). 5 he asks 高木 to say it; わしが言って休む女なら…; seven chiefs before him tried; fix the days, sit at her desk yourself, 法律だ, you're the eighth (no-and). 6 the last five working days on a fresh form; he sends her home to lock up himself, and finds the drawer; the key in the door (yes-but). III 7 the climax (yes-but: she sets the order). 8 his five days in two strokes, the graduation, a floor that ran without him; her five: the key to 村田 with 頼んだちゃ, he sits at her desk, does the Friday paper wrong and again, she does not come in or call; on the 31st he writes a five on her line and a five on his own, and leaves the eight forms in the drawer.

TITLE: 湯あたり

## CULTURE

**PRACTICE: 自炊湯治 at 農民の家, 鳴子温泉, autumn 1993.** Written as a procedure, from sources (named at the end of this block).

1. After the rice is cut (稲刈り, carried as 稲を刈る), farming households of Miyagi go to 鳴子 for the off-season cure (湯治; the kitchen's word for it is 骨休め, carried as 体を休める). The stay is counted in rounds of seven days (一廻り, carried as 一週間 / 七日; the second round is 次の週); two rounds is the usual stay. The inn's season runs November to March; its busiest nights run to 750 to 800 guests against a capacity of 1,061.
2. The family drives the elder up in the light truck (軽トラ), unloads the rice sack and the bags, and goes home the same day; weeks later someone drives back to collect them. In other years the truck bed carried the household's own eating rice (飯米) for two people's two rounds, plus daikon and white cabbage from the field for the kitchen. In 1993 it carries one sack of last year's rice (古米, carried as 去年の米) and nothing from the field: the cold summer (冷害, carried as 冷たい夏) left the 及川 paddies' ササニシキ standing green and sterile and the household's crop came to nothing. Miyagi's crop index for the year was 37, about a third of a crop, and the kitchen's talk is in those numbers (「うちは三割」「うちはゼロ」). The members' side of the inn is thin, and in a thin year it is men who come: a household that cannot spare two people sends the member alone, or nobody. The serviced side is full of leaf-season (紅葉) tourists.
3. At the front desk (帳場) the member shows the cooperative's member card (組合員証, carried as 組合の紙). Membership is by household, in the head of the house's name; his wife is not a member in her own name. The clerk enters name, address and dates in the ledger by hand, takes the money for the first round, and hands over the room key. The serviced wing (旅籠部, carried as 食事の付く方) is open to the public, books by the night rather than the round, and carries meals to the room on a tray three times a day at about double the price. The self-catering side has two grades: rooms with their own burner, in the south building, and the cheapest rooms, on the shared-kitchen corridors (共同の台所, carried as みんなの台所) of the north building. The second round is paid at the desk on its first morning.
4. Self-catering guests bring from home: rice (米), miso, soy sauce, vegetables, pickles. The inn supplies pots, dishes and a refrigerator. The gas ring runs on ten-yen coins (十円玉, carried as 十円) fed into a coin meter that keeps them; the desk changes notes into tens. (Revised at draft round 1: the draft first had the coin returned, after the 2005 source, and both Japanese readers rejected that as fact for a coin gas meter.) Futon are in the closet. The shop on the ground floor sells fresh food, padded coats (どてら / 丹前, carried as 厚い上着) and sundries; this autumn it has a sign up saying it will sell rice to members, which is this story's inference from the failed harvest (flagged below).
5. Guests bathe three times a day, morning, after noon and evening, in the inn's four springs. The baths are mostly mixed (混浴); one is divided, and the big bath has a women-only slot (女性の時間) each evening, which this story puts at seven to eight. Around the end of the first round comes bath-sickness (湯あたり): fatigue, chills, no appetite, a day or two of it; the regulars read it as the cure taking hold (効いてる証拠) and the rule is no bath that day, rest, drink water.
6. The inn keeps a clinic (診療所, carried as 帳場の横の医者の部屋) beside the main office with a resident nurse (看護婦) and a doctor on Saturdays, because the guests are old.
7. Kitchen order among long-stayers: regulars take the same room every year and ask each other in advance whether they are coming; the kitchen's bench by the window is where tea is drunk together at the end of the day (お茶っこ, carried as 茶); what is cooked is shared out among the neighbours on the corridor (お裾分け), and the share is taken, not refused, and not paid for. Some guests stay the whole winter on their pensions and are collected in March.

**PRESSURE: 遠慮, with 察し behind it.** 遠慮 is what stops 茂 saying to キク "I cannot cook; feed me and tell me what I owe": a share taken from a stranger's pot has to be answered, and he has nothing in the sack but rice he cannot cook, so he puts money on her lid instead and cannot say why. 察し is what has kept forty years of 春江's cooking from ever being spoken of as a thing done for him, and it is why neither of them would say "come and let me cook for you" or "I want one week where nobody's dinner is mine to make". Take the pressure away and an American husband at a spa says "Honey, I can't boil rice, and the lady next door keeps feeding me" on the phone on night one, and his wife says "I'm not coming to cook for you, I booked myself the full-service wing".

**VOICES.**

- 及川茂, the writer, born 1927, rice farmer, 登米郡 (northern Miyagi). The diary is a farmer's working diary: an entry usually opens with the date, the weather and the number of baths, and most entries record what he ate and who it came from; he never writes a feeling, and the one time he writes something like one it is a fact about 春江. The entries are uneven: the arrival and the climax are long, the sick day is one line with no weather and no count, five days (28, 30, 31 October, 5 and 6 November) have no entry, and the 4 November entry says in its header that it also covers the 2nd and the 3rd. First person 俺 in speech; in writing the subject is mostly omitted. Speech is Miyagi farmer's plain form: 〜だ, 〜だべ, 〜ねえ, bare plain questions (〜け was weighed and not used in the draft, being less sure for 仙台・県北 speech), 〜しとけ for orders; 「んだ」 for yes. He calls his wife 母ちゃん aloud and 春江 on the page, calls キク キクさん, calls the clerk 帳場の人 and then 由美さん after キク's 由美ちゃん, calls his son 正一 and his son's wife 美代子. To 由美 he uses no です; he says 「頼む」. He counts: coins, bowls, days, and the counts are right.
- キク, born 1915, farm widow from 加美郡, first brought to 鳴子 as a bride (嫁) of twenty, in 1935, behind her husband's mother (姑, carried as 夫の母), to an old inn in the village; at the farmers' inn since the year it opened, and the last ten years November to March on her pension ("冬はここの人だ"). Every one of those years was in the south building, in a room with its own burner. This is her first autumn on the north building's shared-kitchen corridor, because the cold summer took her son's crop too and she will not take money from his house this winter: 「南は高い。今年は」. She has never met 春江. First person おら. Endings 〜だべ, 〜んだ (no 〜け in the draft); bare imperatives 「食え」「入るな」「寝てろ」. Calls him あんた, later 登米の. Habits: every offer starts with 「ほれ」; she never says ありがとう or すまない and does not expect them; she answers questions about herself with a count or a refusal to count (「数えてねえ」); she keeps a row of ten-yen coins on the window sill for the ring; she comes back from the women's hour with everyone's stories and tells them to the kitchen bench whether anyone asked.
- 由美, born 1961, front-desk clerk, employee of the cooperative. です・ます throughout, 「及川さん」, reads the ledger aloud as she writes, doubles her yes (「はい、はい」), and when she will not do something says 「お教えできないんです」 and nothing more. Her politeness is the cooperative's rule (建前), and it is what protects 春江.
- 美代子, born 1955, 正一's wife, on the inn's pink public phone (ピンク電話) at the front desk. 「お父さん」, polite with hesitation: 「ええと」, 「今、ちょっと」, and one fixed phrase, 「手が離せなくて」. At the entrance on the last day: 「お父さん、お疲れさまでした」.
- 正一, born 1954, the son, drives the truck. Calls his father 親父, speaks in short plain sentences with 〜よ, says nothing about the paddies. On the phone once: 「母さんは、行ってるよ」. At the bus stop in 登米 on the last day, with the truck: 「親父、風呂、沸かしといたよ」.
- 春江, born 1930, the wife, speaks twice, at the entrance on the last day: 「ご飯、硬かった」 and 「鍋、返した?」. Calls him お父さん. No apology and no explanation, in either direction.
- The nurse (看護婦), unnamed, born about 1965: brisk です・ます with ね, 「及川さん、今日はお風呂お休みです」「お水、飲んでくださいね」. Seen twice: on the sick day, and at the clinic door beside the desk on checkout morning, 「及川さん、お水、ちゃんと飲んでましたか」.

**SEASON: late October into November, 1993, as a subject.** The cure comes after the rice is cut, and this year the 及川 paddies were cut green for nothing: the entries open with the empty truck bed, the kitchen's talk of crop indices (「うちは三割」「うちはゼロ」), the shop's sign about rice, and a thin members' corridor of men on their own against a serviced wing full of tourists for the 鳴子峡 leaves. 紅葉 is why the serviced wing is full and why one more farm wife in it is invisible; the thin year is why the corridor women who would know 春江 by sight are at home this autumn. 大根干し is the real November work that is 春江's cover. The first frost (霜, carried as 朝、草が白く凍っていた) falls at the start of the second week and the kitchen's window is where everyone stands. Move the story to another month and the serviced wing empties, 春江 has a harvest to be at, and the cure has no reason to happen.

**ABSENT.**

- In: 一廻り counting, as weeks; 自炊 with rice from home; 古米 / 飯米, the sack being last year's eating rice kept back for the house, said once in the kitchen (「去年の米だ」); the 帳場 ledger and member card; the ten-yen token for the gas; お裾分け along the corridor; 湯あたり at the end of the first week; the women-only hour; the clinic and its 看護婦; the 1993 冷害 and the shop's rice sign; 骨休め as the kitchen's word for the cure; お茶っこ, the bench by the window where キク pours tea for whoever sits, carried as 茶 (the っこ is cut to protect the known set); キク's first autumn as a 嫁 behind her 姑, one line; the padded coat (丹前 / どてら) from the shop, worn to the desk on the sick day; 大根干し.
- Cut, on purpose: 混浴 as a scene (the baths are mostly mixed and the story never enters one; what the plot needs is the women's hour, which is sourced). 減反 (the acreage policy was a decade old by 1993 and the kitchen's numbers this year are about the cold, not the policy; one mention would need the word itself, which is not in the set). 出稼ぎ (the winter work the men of the kitchen will go to is mentioned once and not followed). The rice imports and the 1994 米騒動 (they came after this autumn). 共済金 crop insurance (春江's money is her own, thirty years of egg and vegetable money, and the story says so). こけし and the 外湯 滝の湯 (tourists' 鳴子, not farmers'). Karaoke and the 農民の家音頭 (real, and not this story). The inn's rule of not supplying knives or chopsticks (not confirmed for 1993). 新米 for the inn's shop (under the 食糧管理法 a household did not sell rice to an inn; the truck bed in other years carried the household's own eating rice and vegetables for the stay, and the sheet now says so).

**CARRIED.** On known words: 自炊, 温泉, 風呂, 布団, 鍋, 米, 炊く, 研ぐ, 焦げる, 台所, 茶碗, 杯, 蓋, 紅葉, 稲, 刈る, 田んぼ, 組合, 旅館, 宿, 廊下, 階段, 建物, 南, 北, 電話, 看護婦, 医者, 大根, 白菜, 味噌, 嫁, 夫, 妻, 奥さん, 母ちゃん, 親父, 息子, 孫, トラック, バス, 七日, 週, 次, 回, 割, 円, 十, 卵, 札, 財布, 沸かす, ぬるい, 証拠, 効く, 休める, 体, 凍る, 冷たい, 厚い, 上着, 茶, 最後, 紙, 空, 通る (the last five are the brief's peek words, and 紙 is the member card, never the diary's page). On behaviour: the coin put on the lid and found on the sack next morning (遠慮 refused by action); the pot pushed across without a word (お裾分け); the clerk's 「お教えできないんです」 (建前). Needing new_words, 4 of the budget of 4: 湯治, 帳場, お裾分け, 湯あたり. Carried by paraphrase, each declared: 一廻り (一週間, 七日; 二廻り目 as 次の週), 骨休め (体を休める), 姑 (夫の母), 冷害 (冷たい夏), 診療所 (医者の部屋), 霜 (草が白く凍る), 新米 (今年の米), 古米 (去年の米), 稲刈り (稲を刈る), お粥 (柔らかく炊いたご飯: the circumlocution is deliberate, because it is what キク would say to a farmer and the budget is spent), 丹前 (厚い上着), お茶っこ (茶), 混浴 (never named), 共同 (みんなの台所), 浸かる (入る), 湯船 (風呂), 手拭い (タオル), 漬物 (キク's pot is 大根と豚の汁 and her side dish is 白菜; 漬ける is unknown and not used), 農協 (組合), 組合員証 (組合の紙), 旅籠部 (食事の付く方), 軽トラ (トラック). Compositional on known parts, which have.py marks ✗ as compounds: 十円, 二杯, 三回, 三割 (十, 円, 二, 杯, 三, 回, 割 all ✓).

**Sources.** 鳴子温泉 article, Japanese Wikipedia (湯治 culture at 鳴子: 7日間を一廻り, two or three rounds, all guests self-catering, 農民の家 founded 1949 by the 宮城県農民の家農業協同組合). 『水の文化』22号「農民の家 鳴子温泉に今も残る湯治の場」, ミツカン水の文化センター, about 2005 (the inn's two wings, 274 self-catering rooms and 48 serviced, capacity 1,061, the serviced side limited to 150 a day; kitchen-sharing rooms as the cheapest grade; rice, miso, soy sauce and vegetables brought from home; the gas ring that takes a coin and returns it, 「コインを入れて稼働させるが、コインは後から戻ってくる仕組みだ」, denomination not given; the ground-floor shop selling fresh food, clothing, sundries and どてら; families driving the elder up and collecting them weeks later; the baths mostly mixed with one divided and a women-only slot in the big bath; the clinic beside the office with a resident nurse and a Saturday doctor; guests who stay all winter on pensions; peak year 1989; most income earned November to March). 西川雅樹, 農民の家 stay reports 2015 and 2016 (manual front desk, member card or ID at check-in, the ten-yen ring, a coin rice cooker in 2015, futon in the closet, four baths and the women's slots). 国土交通省 多言語解説 database, 黒湯温泉 (regulars sharing their cooking with other guests as the self-catering custom; another spa, and the 水の文化 article does not mention sharing at 農民の家, so お裾分け on the corridor is this story's transfer of a general 湯治場 custom). 湯あたり article, Japanese Wikipedia (symptoms, onset around a week in, skip the bath and rest). 宮城県農業センター 1993 冷害 report and 気象庁仙台 climate notes (crop index 37, 187 kg per 10a, ササニシキ sterility above 80%, the 7月 to 8月 cold). Unconfirmed for 1993 and flagged: the women's slot and its hour; the resident nurse; the coin ring and its denomination; the coin being returned (sourced for 2005 only, and not used: the story's meter keeps the coin); a coin rice cooker in the shared kitchens (sourced for 2015 only; the story gives the kitchen a ring and a pot and no cooker, so the burnt pot in beat 2 stands, and if a cooker was there in 1993 the beat changes to 茂 not knowing how much water it takes); the shop selling rice to members under the 食糧管理法 (the shop sells food; a cooperative is a legal 食管 channel, but the sign is this story's inference from the failed harvest and it carries nothing in the plot beyond キク's remark); the wing name 旅籠部 for 農民の家's serviced side (carried only as 食事の付く方, so it never reaches the text); membership by household in the head's name with the wife not a member (plausible for a 1990s 農協 and leaned on by 由美's ledger question, but not in the named sources).

**AXES.** DOMAIN is proposed as a new value, `LODGING_AND_CURE_STAY`: an inn, lodge or cure house where guests live for days or weeks alongside other guests, often cooking and keeping house themselves; the tie is the shared stay, not a repeated service visit (SERVICE_PREMISES) and not distance and weather (REMOTE_TERRAIN). The self-catering side receives no service: guests cook, fetch their own bedding, and pay by the round. PRACTICE `LONG_STAY_CURE`, PRESSURE 遠慮. OBJECT FOOD_OR_VESSEL. RELATIONSHIP SPOUSES_OR_PARTNERS. CLIMAX HIDDEN_FACT_SAID. ENDING SENSORY_MOMENT.

## CLIMAX

Monday 8 November, the sixth night of the second week, a little after eight, at the shared kitchen on the second floor of the north building. 茂 is measuring rice into the rented pot with a rice bowl (茶碗), because that is the measure he has, and has got as far as two bowls when キク comes back along the corridor from the women's hour (女性の時間) with her towel round her neck and sits on the bench to tell the kitchen what she heard, as she has every night since the first. Tonight it is a woman from 登米 in the serviced wing (食事の付く方), who laughed in the bath because a tray had been carried to her room three times a day for twelve days and nobody had ever carried her one before; who said she had paid for it with thirty years of her own egg money; who said her husband was in this building, on the self-catering side, and could not wash rice. キク laughs, and 茂 laughs, and then キク looks at the bowl in his hand and stops laughing and says it plainly: 「……あんたの母ちゃんだべ」. Then, because she has already asked the woman: 「あんたの次の日から、あっちにいるんだと。自分の金で」.

What he does is not what the kitchen expects. He puts the bowl down, walks to the front desk and asks 由美 for the room. 由美 looks at the ledger she has had both names in for twelve days and says 「お部屋の番号は、お教えできないんです」, and then, because she is also a person: 「奥さんも、水曜までです」. The stairs to the serviced wing are beside the desk, and at that hour the dinner trays are coming down them; a girl passes him with a stack of them, and he could ask her for a woman from 登米 and does not. He goes back up to the kitchen. キク pushes the pot of daikon and pork across to him as she has every night, and he says the one cruel thing in the story, 「余計なこと言うな」, and she answers 「んだ。おらは口が軽い。ほれ、食え」. He eats it. He does not put money on the lid. The entry ends on the only sentence in the diary about 春江 that is not a count: he has never once seen her eat a meal someone else made.

**TWIST:** 春江 has been in the same inn since the day after he arrived, in the serviced wing, on her own first cure, paid with her own money, and 美代子 drove her up and has been lying on the phone for twelve days. キク states it, in speech, in the kitchen, the moment she understands it: 「あんたの母ちゃんだべ」. 茂 confirms it in the entry and adds the fact that makes it his: he has never seen 春江 fed.

## AFTERWORD

The twist is that the wife who "stayed home with the daikon" was in the same building the whole time. ｜春江《はるえ》 checked into the inn's serviced wing the day after ｜茂《しげる》 was dropped on the self-catering side, booked through the same Wednesday, paid with egg money she had been putting by for thirty years, and for twelve days ate meals brought to her room. The family covered for her on every call, and ｜正一《しょういち》's 「｜行《い》ってるよ」, his answer when his father asks whether she is at the co-op, was simply true. For ten years she had come with ｜茂《しげる》 to the room beside the same kitchen; this year, with nothing from the field to carry up, she took the other side of the building. What hides her is the building and the year. The wings have their own corridors and stairs, hers is full of people up for the autumn leaves, and she eats in her room and bathes in the women's hour. In a lost harvest a household sends one person or none, so the members' corridor is half empty and all men, and the women who would know her face are at home. The one woman there is キク, new to that corridor because 「｜南《みなみ》は｜高《たか》い。｜今年《ことし》は」, who crosses between the two sides by bringing everyone's stories back from the women's hour. On the 8th her story is a funny one: a woman in the serviced wing who does not know what to do with her hands while her meals are carried in. キク has asked that woman more than she tells the kitchen, and when she sees ｜茂《しげる》 measuring rice with a bowl she says it: 「……あんたの｜母《かあ》ちゃんだべ」. ｜登米《とめ》, the egg money and the husband who cannot wash rice come after that line. The diary does not keep the reader as blind as ｜茂《しげる》. A reader who noticed the single sack, ｜正一《しょういち》 gone before the bags were upstairs, ｜由美《ゆみ》 asking whether he is the only one in the co-op, and a son saying his mother is "away" may suspect first; ｜茂《しげる》 writes each of these down and reads none of them, and キク's line is the first place it is said. The title names the day the cure makes you worse, which the kitchen calls proof the water is working (「｜湯治《とうじ》が｜効《き》いてる｜証拠《しょうこ》だ」). ｜茂《しげる》 has soaked in ｜春江《はるえ》's care all their married life without feeling it, the way you stop feeling the water, and has never once seen her eat a meal someone else made. Care that was never noticed was still care taken, and the one return he can make for it is not to fetch her out of the one stay she took for herself. He could go: ｜由美《ゆみ》 refuses only the room number and then says his wife is booked through Wednesday too, and a girl comes down the stairs to her wing whom he could ask and does not. Instead he eats キク's food and leaves nothing on her lid: he lets himself be fed without paying for it, which in his first week at the kitchen he could not do. The coins taught him that キク would not be paid in money, so only a share answers a share. From the first night キク fed the gas from the row of tens on her window sill, so the tens he changed at the desk to pay his way did not go down, and the hundred yen he left on her lid came back on his rice sack. When he can cook, he lights the gas with a ten of his own, and on the 9th he leaves a bowl of his rice on her lid as a share, not a payment. キク carries it to the women's hour unasked and comes back with 「｜食《く》った。｜硬《かた》いと」, while he stays in the kitchen through the hour her wing's women come out. That is the rice ｜春江《はるえ》 means when she says at the entrance that it was hard. What keeps all of this unsaid is 遠慮, with 察し behind it. 遠慮 is why ｜茂《しげる》 cannot tell キク that he cannot cook and ask what he owes: a share taken from a stranger's pot has to be answered, and he has nothing to share but rice he cannot cook, so he puts money on her lid and cannot say why. 察し is why a married life of ｜春江《はるえ》's cooking was never once spoken of as something done for him, and why neither of them would say "come and cook for me" or "I want one week where nobody's dinner is mine to make". The diary is a farmer's working diary of date, weather and bath count, irregular as such diaries are. 1993 is the cold summer that left the house nothing in the field and only last year's rice, so ｜春江《はるえ》 could be spared; it is also before mobile phones, so the pink phone at the desk is the only line home, and ｜美代子《みよこ》 can stand in front of it. The inn is modelled on the real farmers' cooperative inn at ｜鳴子《なるこ》, ｜農民《のうみん》の｜家《いえ》. Assumed for 1993 rather than sourced: the women's hour and its time, the nurse, the ten-yen gas, the shop's rice sign, the name ｜旅館部《りょかんぶ》, and membership by household in the husband's name, which ｜由美《ゆみ》's question leans on. At home ｜春江《はるえ》 cooks supper as she always did and he washes the rice, the one thing changed. The bath ｜正一《しょういち》 ran is lukewarm, and it is the last thing the diary records.

## PREMISE

Autumn 1993, after the cold summer left the paddies of northern Miyagi standing green and empty. 及川茂, 66, a rice farmer from 登米, is driven up to the farmers' cooperative inn at 鳴子 for his two weeks of the cure as he is every year, and put in the self-catering wing with a sack of last year's rice; his wife 春江, who has cooked in that corridor's kitchen every autumn for thirty years, has stayed behind with the daikon and is to come for the second week. The old woman at the window burner is new to the corridor and feeds whoever sits down.

## ANCHOR

The shared kitchen of the self-catering corridor: the window burner that runs on ten-yen coins and keeps them, the rented pot, the rice sack on the floor, the rice bowl he measures with, the bench where キク pours tea, and the pot of daikon and pork that comes across the table every night. Every phone call and every settling of accounts runs through the front desk, so the desk is the kitchen's second pole. New words, 4 of 4: 湯治 (the cure itself, in the entries' counting of weeks), 帳場 (the desk: check-in, the token, the pink phone, the refusal, checkout), お裾分け (キク's pot, and the one bowl that goes the other way), 湯あたり (the title, the end of the first week, and the kitchen's reading of it).

## WANT

To have 春江 arrive for the second week, and until she does, to eat his own rice and not another bowl of the old woman's.

## NEED

He cannot take a bowl from a hand that is not 春江's without putting money on the lid, and 春江's hands he has never counted as hands: forty years of being fed by her never registered as being fed, so being fed by anyone else registers only as debt.

## SHAPE

Three-act, eight beats. Act I is beats 1 and 2, Act II is beats 3 to 6, Act III is beats 7 and 8. The twist is in the third act; its seeds (キク's gossip habit and the trays at six in beat 1, the ledger question and the coin returned to the sack in beat 2) are in the first.

## BEATS

**Act I**

1. **Wednesday 27 October, clear. Baths: one. (Long entry.)** 正一 drives him up in the light truck (軽トラ) with the bed empty but for one sack; other years it carried two people's eating rice (飯米) and daikon and white cabbage from the field, and neither of them says so. At the front desk (帳場) 由美 takes the cooperative's member card (組合員証), writes his name and address in the ledger aloud, takes the first week's money (一廻り), and gives him the key to the cheap room on the shared-kitchen corridor, the one he and 春江 have had for ten years. 正一 says 「母さんは次の週から」 at the entrance and is gone before the bags are up the stairs. The corridor is half empty and all men this year; the one woman is at the window burner, and he has never seen her: キク, who hands him a bowl of daikon and pork before his coat is off: 「ほれ」. He eats it standing and says he will bring something tomorrow. The gas ring wants a ten-yen coin (十円玉) to start, and he has notes and hundreds and no ten; キク takes one off the row on the sill without a word. At six the trays go along the far corridor to the serviced wing (食事の付く方), tourists' dinners for the leaves (紅葉). After the evening bath キク comes back from the women's hour (女性の時間) with her towel round her neck and sits on the bench with the teapot (お茶っこ) and tells the kitchen what she heard: a woman from 石巻 whose son sold the boat. He writes it down because it was said. _Yes, but:_ he is in, and fed, and already owes on night one, and the sack is a thing he has never opened himself.

2. **Friday 29 October, cloudy. Baths: three.** He opens the sack (「去年の米だ」, to the kitchen, which nods). He measures rice with a rice bowl (茶碗) because that is the measure there is, washes it (研ぐ) the way he has watched it done, and burns the bottom of the rented pot. キク takes the pot off him, scrapes the burnt rice into her own bowl (「おらはこれが好きだ」), and gives him hers. He puts money on her pot lid when she is at the bath. Down at the desk to change a note into tens of his own, 由美 asks over the ledger 「組合員は、及川さん、お一人ですね」 and he says 「んだ。母ちゃんは組合員でねえ」, and she writes. He phones home on the pink phone (ピンク電話) and 美代子 answers: 「お母さんは今、大根を干しに出てて」. _No, and:_ the rice is a failure, the money is back on his rice sack in the morning, his tens do not go down because キク's coins light the gas, and 春江 is "out".

**Act II**

1. **Monday 1 November, clear, the grass white and frozen in the morning (霜). Baths: three.** The serviced wing is full for the 鳴子峡 leaves and the members' corridor is half empty, which 由美 says is the year. The kitchen's men compare crop indices (作況) over キク's tea: 「うちは三割」「うちはゼロ」; 茂 says nothing. He asks キク how many autumns, and she says 「数えてねえ」, then that her first was behind her husband's mother (姑) as a bride (嫁), at an inn in the village that is gone, that every year since has been in the south building, and that this year 「南は高い」. She is here until March. She asks when his wife comes; he says next week; she says 「んだら、それまでおらの鍋だ」. _Yes, but:_ he belongs to the kitchen now, and he has eaten her pot five nights running, and the sack is still full of rice he cannot cook.

2. **Tuesday 2 November. (One line, no weather, no bath count.)** 「二日。寝てた。キクさんの飯。」 Seventh day, the end of the first week, and the bath-sickness (湯あたり) the kitchen told him would come: chills, no appetite, the stairs too long. The line is all the entry holds; the day is told in the next one. _No, and:_ he is in bed being fed by a stranger, and the diary itself has stopped counting.

3. **Thursday 4 November, clear. Baths: three. (Written for the 2nd, the 3rd and today.)** On the 2nd キク said 「効いてる証拠だ。今日は入るな。寝てろ」 and brought rice cooked soft (柔らかく炊いたご飯) to the room; the nurse (看護婦) from the clinic (診療所) beside the office took his temperature and said 「及川さん、今日はお風呂お休みです。お水、飲んでくださいね」. On the 3rd, the first morning of the second week, he got himself down to the desk in a padded coat (丹前) from the shop and paid the second week himself; 由美 said 「はい、はい」 and wrote, and asked nothing; the shop had a sign up about rice, and キク, who came down with him, said she had never seen that before. He phoned; 美代子: 「お母さんは、組合に行ってて」. He said 「次の週から来いって言っとけ」, which is the want said aloud, to the wrong person, a day late. Today, recovered: he cooks rice that is hard but rice, and carries the first bowl to キク as a return (お返し). She eats it, says 「硬い」, and hands him her white cabbage (白菜) anyway: the return is taken and the account does not close, because the kitchen does not keep one. _Yes, but:_ the rice is done, the giving does not balance the way he needs it to, and 春江 has not rung back.

4. **Sunday 7 November, cloudy. Baths: three. (Short.)** Twelfth day. He phones and 正一 answers for once: 「母さんは、行ってるよ」, and then 美代子 has the receiver, 「今、ちょっと手が離せなくて」. He decides at the desk that he will not phone again; she is needed at the house and he will finish the week and go home alone, and he tells 由美 nothing. Back in the kitchen キク puts the pot across without asking anything, which is worse than asking. _No, and:_ he gives up the want on his own terms, and he now owes the old woman twelve nights.

**Act III**

1. **Monday 8 November, clear. Baths: three. (The climax, as above; the longest entry.)** キク's story from the women's hour: the laughing woman from 登米 in the serviced wing, twelve days of trays, her own egg money, a husband on the self-catering side who cannot wash rice. 「……あんたの母ちゃんだべ」. The desk: 「お部屋の番号は、お教えできないんです」, and 「奥さんも、水曜までです」. The stairs beside the desk, the trays coming down, the girl he does not ask. The kitchen: 「余計なこと言うな」, 「ほれ、食え」. He eats, and puts nothing on the lid. The entry's last line: he has never once seen 春江 eat a meal someone else made. _Yes, but:_ the want is won in the form he no longer wants, she came and not to him, and the only return he can make is to stay on his side of the building.

2. **Wednesday 10 November, written at home. (Covers the 9th too.)** Yesterday, before the evening bath, he cooked two bowls' worth and left one on キク's lid, as a share (お裾分け), not a payment; at seven she took it to the women's hour without being asked and without saying she would, and at eight, when the bath let out and he knew which door, he was in the kitchen; she came back and said 「食った。硬いと」, and the diary writes that the bowl went to 春江. This morning: pot, dishes and key back to the desk (帳場); 由美 settles the ledger and says 「お二人とも、お気をつけて」; at the clinic door beside her the nurse says 「及川さん、お水、ちゃんと飲んでましたか」. At the entrance 美代子 is at the wheel of the two-seat truck and 春江 is beside the bags with her own. 春江 says 「ご飯、硬かった」, and then 「鍋、返した?」, and he says 「返した」. 美代子 says 「お父さん、お疲れさまでした」 and puts 春江 in the passenger seat; the truck seats two, and he takes the bus. キク stays; her ride comes in March. At the bus stop in 登米 正一 is waiting with the truck: 「親父、風呂、沸かしといたよ」. At home 春江 cooks as she always did, and he washes the rice. The bath 正一 ran was lukewarm. _No, and:_ the house is exactly as he left it and he is not, and the last thing the diary can find to say about that is the temperature of the water.

## DRAFTING NOTES

- Afterword (critic condition 1): the unwritten days are stated as they fall (eight entries; 28, 30, 31 Oct and 5, 6 Nov have none; the 4th covers the 2nd and 3rd; the 9th is written on the 10th), the bowl on the 9th is left before the bath and carried off at seven, and one sentence says why 春江 chose the same inn.
- Last-day vehicle (condition 2): the truck seats two, so he takes the bus; the truck is faster than the bus, and 正一 meets him at the 登米 stop with the same truck.
- CARRIED (condition 3): the tray is carried as 食事を部屋に運ぶ throughout; 「お二人とも、お気をつけて」 passes check.py as 気 + 付ける.
- 〜け (condition 4): not used; 茂 and キク ask with bare plain questions, 〜だべ and 〜んだ.
- Flags (condition 5): 旅籠部 never reaches the text (always 食事の付く方), and the household-membership assumption is added to the unconfirmed flags; the draft says only 「母ちゃんは入ってねえ」.
- Beat 1 (condition 6): the entry records the 石巻 woman as a fact of the evening; no entry remarks on the diary or its writing.
- Departures from the beats forced by the known set: 由美 asks 「会員は、及川さん、お一人ですね」 (組合員 unknown); the nurse says 熱があると言った (測る unknown); the second rice is 今度は焦げなかった (焦がす unknown); no county names (郡 unknown). The bath report 「初めての湯治で」 is 春江's own word for it, her first cure as a guest after years at the burner; a reader may set it against 十年この部屋. 茂's age (66) and the thirty-year figure appear only in the premise and blurb, not in the text.

The guesser reported no leak in either round and no guess reached the wife's presence in the same inn as a mechanism; the nearest had her arranging the feeding from home. The locator placed it in a Japanese 湯治 inn in rice country in the leaf season, from the week-based cure, the bath sickness after the first week, the two wings under one roof, the co-op card, the ten-yen gas and the segregated bath hours, and noted that a mobile phone would break the phone mechanism; it had no year input, so the year it gave is not a finding. The transplanter broke the climax and the need-beat, named 遠慮 with 察し behind it as the pressure lost, and found the need would be said aloud on the phone once the pressure was gone. Round 2 passed with conditions applied before drafting: the last day's vehicles made legible, the meal trays carried as a known-word phrase, the dialect checked, the unconfirmed flags extended, and the diary kept from remarking on its own writing. Draft stage: two Japanese-only readers and one English-only reader. Draft round 1 was sent back by the reconciler under reveal, not puzzle: all three readers found the twist all but stated in the women's-hour report a paragraph before キク's line, and two heard the son's answer on the phone as saying where his mother was. With it went a plant both Japanese-only readers rejected as fact (a gas meter that gave its coin back), two more facts (the call rate to 登米 and a first-name badge), the membership word, two split turns (speaker attribution), the first evening's outsider glosses and other translation-shaped lines, the truck and the bus on the last day, and afterword sentences (pipeline vocabulary, a plants checklist, and a claim that the reader is as blind as the diarist, which the readers contradicted). The new-word budget was raised by one at that round so that the serviced wing could be named rather than paraphrased. Draft round 2 passed, and its ship fixes were mechanical: afterword sentences naming the pressure and saying outright what the coins taught, a stock phrase cut, translation-shaped lines (the thousand-yen note, the gas ring, the stairs, the half-empty corridor, the catch-up entry's header) and the English truck sentence split in two. Endings: in both rounds all three readers chose the last line, the lukewarm bath at home, where intended; the Japanese-only readers put the emotional close a line or two earlier and read the bath as the coda. Twist: in round 2 all three found it stated at the reveal by キク, in speech, and no earlier line stating it; two called it heavily seeded, which the afterword now owns as dramatic irony. Both Japanese-only readers named the practice in both rounds, and in round 2 named the 遠慮 half of the pressure by its mechanism, the share that has to be answered, and the 察し half by its effect, the bowl doing the talking, without using either word. Both found the speech, the pink phone, キク's relay from the women's bath and the bowl natural for this couple and this year. Naturalness rose by a step between rounds, the two Japanese-only readers agreeing each time. Left as flagged: 霜 is not a known word, so the frost stays as grass frozen white; 春江 and 正一 speak without dialect; the nurse's repeated water question; the run of plain-past sentences in the last scene; and one reader's view that the diary's long dialogue scenes read as a novel in diary costume, which is a note on the corpus's epistolary convention.
