stories.title: 拍子木
stories._brief_reason: page_slack 2 because Rob asked for 15 to 20 pages; every other parameter is the default. Batch 2026-11-13, story s2.
stories._premise:
Level 3 (N3 voice), register ghost-story, 18 pages (16 to 20), new_words 4, leech seeds 5. Rob asked for 15 to 20 pages, and the page slack of 2 records that; every other Gate 1 parameter was settled by the pipeline. Gate 2 passed on round 3 of 3; the round-3 critic's drafting conditions C1 to C6 (the 1963 bridge shut, the father leaving in 1967, three strikes every night of the watch, a quoted last line, the cut-off snow story played as old-man irritation, the senior-most walker) are applied below. Three characters were renamed at drafting so that every name segments whole (佐藤 to 小林, 鈴木 to 森, 誠 to 実), and again before the panel to clear name collisions with the corpus and the batch (小林 to 丸山, 森 to 本間, 実 to 和夫; see the note under VOICES). Of the four planned new words, check.py counts two as unknown (消防団, 詰所); Ichiran splits 拍子木 into 拍子 + 木 and 火の用心 into 火 + の + 用心. 拍子木 stays declared as the anchor; 火の用心 is called twice in the draft, against the ×8 planned below, and is not declared. In draft revision round 1 懐中電灯 was declared as the fourth new word, replacing bare 電灯, because both Japanese-only readers flagged 電灯 for a flashlight; the four declared words now match brief.new_words 4. At ship the reconciler's mechanical fixes were applied to the draft: among them 本間's 九年ぶりじゃ on the 28th became 十年ぶりじゃ, because the last newest man to strike the year's last round did so the winter before 丸山 came across (item 5 below says nine); the counters 軒 and 棟 and the words 大工, 法被 and ストーブ were checked and are not known, so the draft keeps 三十二, 十一の家, 家を建てる仕事, 上着 and 火.

TITLE: 拍子木 (hyoushigi). Level 3, N3 voice. Register: ghost-story (怪談). Pages 18 ±2 (16 to 20; Rob asked for 15 to 20). First person, 俺, past tense, close narration. December 1974 into 1 January 1975, a small town in snow country with a river through it and a bridge; the prefecture is never named.

## CULTURE

**PRACTICE: 消防団の年末夜警 (the volunteer fire brigade's year-end night watch), the procedure as this town's 第三分団 runs it.**

1. The town's 消防団 is made of residents with day jobs, part-time local public servants appointed through the town office, organised in 分団 under a 分団長. Terms run with the fiscal year, April to March, so a man who leaves leaves at the end of March (年度末), which is why 和夫's sentence is 三月で辞めます. Rank inside the 分団 runs by years of service, and the newest member is 後輩 to everyone. The story never leaves 第三分団, so inside it the unit is simply うちの消防団 and 本間 is 一番上; the town's brigade head (団長) is a different man, mentioned once (item 7). Until 1965 the 分団 had two sections (班): the town's, thirty-two houses, and the far bank's, eleven houses up the far road across the bridge, with its own pair on the round and its own senior. Since 1965 it has had one.
2. On the last nights of the year (this 分団: 28 to 31 December, 8 pm to midnight) the brigade staffs its hut (詰所), the room beside the pump truck (消防車), in pairs by shift. The pair on duty keeps the stove going, the kettle on, and waits. 本間 reads the shift list (名簿) aloud on the 28th; 和夫 and 丸山 are paired on the 28th and the 31st, which is why the 29th and 30th are not in the story.
3. Each pair walks the district (見回り, carried as 町を回る) in the brigade coat (法被, carried as 上着). The senior of the pair carries and strikes the wooden clappers (拍子木); the junior walks one step behind with the hand lamp (懐中電灯, carried as 電灯) and carries nothing that makes a sound. At each house the senior calls 火の用心 and strikes twice: カチ、カチ. The route is fixed and the houses are counted: thirty-two on this side of the river, the last of them 丸山's own, nearest the water, and the round turns back at the bridge (橋), which is where the district ends. From the bridge, the far road goes up, and the eleven roofs of the far bank stand on the slope (坂) above it, in sight in snow-light. On the 31st every door on the round has its 門松 up.
4. On returning, the pair strikes the clappers twice at the hut door and calls 異常なし; 本間 inside answers 「おう」. That is how the hut knows who is back without anyone opening the door. (This door convention is the 分団's own, not a general custom; the sheet says so and the story presents it as the hut's habit. Until 1965 the far bank's section had its own hut and its own count, three, which the story withholds until 本間 says it on the 1st; see item 8.)
5. The last round of the 31st ends before the temple bell (除夜の鐘, carried as 寺の鐘) at midnight; the watch ends with the bell, and the pair on the last shift cleans the hut on the morning of the 1st. This 分団's own custom, stated by 本間 on the 28th: the newest member strikes the last round of the year, as far as the bridge (大晦日の最後は、一番下が打つ。橋までじゃ). The bridge itself stays the senior's. The custom has not been used since the far bank left, because the 分団 has taken in nobody since; 和夫, who joined in April, is its first newest member in nine years, and one of the seniors says so on the 28th (久しぶりだな、一番下が打つのは).
6. A member who means to quit tells the senior who brought him in, or if that man is gone, the senior he walks behind on the round, who tells 本間; the junior does not go to 本間 himself. This is the 分団's own order of telling, not a general rule, and the story shows it as such: 和夫's father went the same way when he left in 1967, and told 丸山, the senior he had walked behind for two winters since the far bank came over.
7. The morning of the 1st, with the last shift's kettle, 本間 writes the turnout list (名簿) for the 出初め式 on the 6th: who stands, in what order, the newest at the back of the line (列の後ろ). It is a list for one ceremony, not a year's appointment; the year's appointments follow the town office and the fiscal year (item 1). The town's brigade head (団長) makes his year-end round of the huts (激励, carried as 団長が来た) on the 30th, which the story skips; 本間 reports it on the 31st in one line, and the sake the pair drinks that night, one cup each, is what he left. It is the only cup in the story: on the 28th the pair goes out on tea.
8. The snow year (三八豪雪, January 1963, carried as あの雪の年 and 雪がたくさん降った年). The far road was buried for eight days and the far bank's eleven houses were cut off, and the bridge was shut as well: the river wind had drifted the snow across it higher than a man, with the rails buried, so that a man who went onto it could not tell the bridge from the river, and the town closed it like the road. Each pair could reach only its own end, by the path it dug from its own side. The telephone line to the far bank was down under the snow, and a voice does not carry across a river in falling snow, but the clappers do, which is the physical fact the whole exchange rests on. On each of the eight nights the far bank's pair dug its way down to its end of the bridge and struck three, and the town's pair at this end answered two: that is how the hut knew the eleven were alive, since nobody could cross and nothing else carried. The counts are the two sections' own door strikes: the far bank's hut answered 異常なし with three, the town's with two (item 4), so what crossed the river each night was each hut's own all-clear. The three-and-two at the bridge is this 分団's own invention for that week, and the story presents it as such, told by 本間 as a thing that happened.

Sources: Otsu and Hiroshima city notices for the period and hours of the 年末警戒 (27 to 30 December, 20:30 to midnight; brigades assemble at the 詰所 and patrol with the truck's red light); the Kochi Ino town press release for 法被, 拍子木 carried and the 火の用心 call on the round; Oita city's brigade history for the 拍子木 as the 夜警's traditional tool; Machida city for the 出初め式 held in the first half of January; the 消防団令 of 1947 for the brigade's founding year (the 警防団 before it is why 丸山's service is counted from 1947 and 本間's from before the war); the JMA's 1963 report for the snow (a month of snowfall centred on Hokuriku, roads unshovelled, many hamlets cut off). For the far bank's leaving: the Shimane University study of 石見 mountain villages for whole-household departure (挙家離村) as the documented pattern of 1960 to 1965, and the 1965 山村振興法 for the year the state took up the mountain-village problem. No source was found for a whole hamlet leaving together in 1965 on the strength of the 1963 snow; the eleven households leaving in one spring, with the town office's help with the move, is the story's own case and is stated as such, and the draft keeps it as an old man's story (みんなで町を出た) rather than a policy. The far bank is a hamlet (carried as 向こうの家, 向こうの班) on the slope above the far road: eleven roofs visible from the bridge, eight fallen under nine winters of snow, three still standing, none shovelled. The two-strike door answer, the three-and-two across the river, the junior's last round and the order of telling are this 分団's own, and the story presents them as such.

**PRESSURE: 先輩・後輩.** A first-year walks behind, carries the lamp and nothing that makes a sound, speaks when spoken to, and does not correct a senior's round. What it forbids 和夫 to say is one sentence, and it is both his need and a correction of 丸山's round: 橋の向こうには、誰もいない. To say it is to tell a man who has been in the brigade since before 和夫 was born that his round ends in front of nobody, and to say it to the one man in the town who was born over there; a 後輩 cannot say that to a 先輩 any more than he can take the clappers out of his hand. It also forbids the plain quit on its own: a 後輩 does not open a conversation on a senior's round, and when he does open his mouth, the senior answers with an instruction before the sentence has landed. The same order binds the other way: a senior cannot ask a junior for anything, only instruct him, which is why what 丸山 wants at the bridge can only come out as 二つ打て. Test: take the pressure away and a nineteen-year-old in Iowa says "Walt, there's nobody over there, you're clapping at a hillside, and I'm gone in March" in one breath, and Walt says "I know. Do me a favour and clap twice."

**VOICES.**

- 和夫 (かずお), 19, born 1955, narrator. 俺 in narration; to 丸山 and 本間 です・ます, 丸山さん and 本間さん; never opens a conversation with either until the story makes him; answers 「はい」 and 「いえ」. Works at the town's small factory (工場), the same one as his father, which has cut its shifts. Habits: hands in the coat pockets; counts the dark windows on the round and not the lit ones; counts anything in front of him (windows, roofs, strikes); speaks in the hut only when asked. His one long speech in the story is at the bridge, and it comes out in the wrong order.
- 丸山 (まるやま), 58, born 1916 on the far bank, builds houses (大工, carried as 家を建てる仕事). Called up in 1941, back in 1946, in the 分団 from the spring of 1947 when the 消防団 was made: twenty-seven years, eighteen of them on the far bank's round and nine on the town's. Everyone in the town knows he is 向こうの生まれ, that he came across the year the eleven left, and that the house at the end of the round is his own far-bank house, taken down and carried over the bridge and built again by his own hands (自分で運んで、こっちで建てた); the narration says so plainly on the 28th, as a thing everyone knows. 俺; calls 和夫 お前, calls 本間 本間さん. Plain imperatives (打て, 来い, 持て), 〜ぞ, 〜な, 〜か; answers a question with an instruction and an opening with an instruction, and answers what pleases him with a correction; never says 寒い; counts the houses aloud (三十二) at the bridge on every round; wipes the clappers with his sleeve (袖) before they go back in his coat. Says 「そうか」 to news. Wants: the round walked as it has always been walked, the boy not to be made to feel the watch is his, and one thing he cannot ask for, because a senior does not ask a junior. He hands over the houses for one night because the hut's custom says so, and keeps the bridge. He is the senior-most of the men who walk: 本間 is above him and never leaves the hut, so on every round 丸山 is on, the clappers are his, and the narration says so on the 28th.
- 本間 (ほんま), 64, born 1910, 分団長, addressed as 本間さん by both and described in narration as うちの消防団の一番上. わし, 〜じゃ, 〜かい, 〜だな, 〜とる, which is old-man 役割語 and marks no region; the story's region shows in the snow and nowhere in the speech. Calls 和夫 和夫 (has known his father since his father's own years in the 分団), calls 丸山 丸山. Keeps the list and the kettle, pours on the 31st, tells the story of the snow year every year and is stopped at the same place every year, and answers the door strikes with 「おう」 without looking up. He is never seen outside the hut; his knees have kept him off the round for years, which is said once (わしはもう橋まで行けん). Era: a man who was thirty-five when the war ended and already walking this round, and says so once (戦争が終わった年、わしは三十五じゃった。もうこの町を回っとった).
- 父 (和夫's father), 52, born 1922, alive, works at the factory. A former member of the 分団 who left it in 1967, at forty-five, when his knees went, after two winters walking behind 丸山 once the far bank's men had come over, and told 丸山, his own 先輩 on the round, before 本間 heard. 俺, few words, 〜だ, 〜な; calls 和夫 和夫 and 丸山 丸山さん. In April he is the one 丸山 asks for the boy, and he says 「預けます」. His one line on the 31st is 「丸山さんによろしく」, said from the gate with the 門松 in his hands, which is a man who went through 丸山 once telling his son which way the telling goes.
- 母 (和夫's mother), 48. 〜なさい, 〜だよ, 〜でしょ; calls him 和夫. Has mended the brigade coat's sleeve, torn on the 28th, and packed 餅 for the hut (差し入れ). Her agenda: that the telling be done properly and by him. Her one scene is the afternoon of the 31st.
- The other pair at the hut, two seniors, unnamed: one says 〜だってな and has the gossip line on the 31st; the other says 久しぶりだな on the 28th.

Names checked against each other, and changed twice. At drafting, for segmentation: the sheet had 佐藤, 鈴木 and 誠, but check.py on the first draft split 佐藤 into 佐 + 藤 and 鈴木 into 鈴 + 木, with 佐, 藤 and 鈴 unknown, and 誠 is a single unknown kanji, so they became 小林, 森 and 実. Before the panel, for collisions: 森 and 小林 are both in 貸出中の本 (also level 3, also ghost-story), 小林 is also in スープを残す客, and 実 is in this batch's 一人半. So the senior is 丸山 (まるやま, a common snow-country surname, known and whole), the 分団長 is 本間 (ほんま, an old Niigata and Sado surname, known and whole), and the narrator is 和夫 (かずお, known and whole, a common boy's name through the early 1950s); each was checked with check.py on the story and appears nowhere else in stories/ or in the batch. 高橋 was rejected because the story's bridge (橋) would sit inside the senior's name.

**SEASON: late December into 正月, as the subject.** The watch exists because the year's end is when houses burn: stoves run all night, the dry cold air, people up late. Snow has fallen and stopped; the sky over the town on the 31st is clear and full of stars (星), and the cold air carries the clappers farther than in any other month, which is the physical fact the bridge scene stands on; the river is frozen at its edges and silent. Between the 28th and the 31st the 門松 go up on every door of the round, lit houses and dark ones alike, which 和夫 walks past and does not count. The hut eats the 餅 the junior's mother sent; the radio plays the year-end singing; the temple bell at midnight is what the last round races. On the 1st the turnout list for the 出初め式 on the 6th is written. Snow is also the story's memory: the snow year is what emptied the far bank, and snow is the one wrong thing on the last night. Test: moved to July there is no watch, no bell, no snow silence to hear across, no 門松 and no 出初め式; nothing survives.

**ABSENT.** In: 出初め式 (as 六日の式, what the list on the 1st is for); 除夜の鐘 (as 寺の鐘, the clock the last round runs against); 差し入れ by name, twice (the mother's 餅, and the sake the town's 団長 left at the hut on the 30th); the 団長's visit to the hut on the 30th (激励, carried as 団長が来た), reported in one line by 本間 on the 31st, because the story skips the 30th and because it fixes for the reader that 団長 is somebody other than 本間; 門松 on the doors of the round on the 31st and in the father's hands at the gate; the year-end radio singing, as an era marker; the factory's cut shifts and young men leaving, in one line; the far bank's leaving in 1965, told as an old man's story; the carrying of a house across a river and its rebuilding (移築, carried as 自分で運んで、こっちで建てた), as the ordinary thing a carpenter from a leaving hamlet does. Cut on purpose: しめ飾り, because the word is not known and 門松 does the same work on the page; 半鐘 (the fire bell on its tower), because the story has one bell and it belongs to the temple; 纏 and 法被 by name, carried as 上着; 年越しそば, because the hut eats 餅 and the word is not known; 初詣 and お年玉, because the story ends at the hut on the morning of the 1st and never reaches the family; 雪下ろし, because the roofs are not this story's work, except as the reason the far bank's roofs have fallen; the old men's match-line call (マッチ一本火事の元), because the story's call is 火の用心 and nothing else, so that the strikes and not the words carry the code.

**CARRIED.** On known words: the round itself (町を回る, 火, 窓, 明かり, 暗い, 橋, 川, 向こう, 岸, 坂, 雪, 星, 空, 雲, 寒い, 息, 袖, 上着, 電灯, 足元, 門松), the count (数える, 三十二, 十一, 八日, 家, 屋根), the door answer and the river answer (異常なし, 叩く, 打つ, 返す, 答える, 聞こえる, 遅い), the list (名簿, 名前, 書く, 列, 後ろ), the hut's life (火, 湯, 茶, 酒, 餅, ラジオ, 差し入れ), the brigade's order (一番上 and 一番下 as 一番 + 上 and 一番 + 下, 番, 順番, 先輩 and 後輩 as words, 辞める, 入れる, 預ける, 久しぶり), the far bank (班, 向こうの生まれ, みんなで町を出た, 引っ越す, 残る, 屋根, 倒れる, 運ぶ, 建てる), the bell (寺, 鐘, 鳴る), the clappers' care (拭く, 濡れる, しまう in kana, 音が変わる), the snow on the last night (降る, 止む, 晴れる). Needing new words, four, at the budget's cap: 消防団 (the institution, said by everyone, ×10 or more), 拍子木 (the anchor, struck in every scene, ×15 or more), 火の用心 (the call, ×8), 詰所 (the hut, where every act begins and ends, ×8). ## CLIMAX

Thirty-first of December, the last round, half past eleven. For the first time 和夫 has the clappers (拍子木): the hut's custom gave him the year's last round as far as the bridge, 丸山 put them in his hand at the hut with 「今夜はお前が打て。橋までだ」 before he could finish a sentence and took the lamp (電灯) out of his hand in exchange, and has walked a step behind him all the way, the lamp on the boy's feet, counting under his breath. 和夫 has struck twice at thirty-two doors with 門松 on them and called 火の用心 in a voice the cold cracked at the ninth; the thirty-second door was 丸山's own, with his wife's light in the window. At the bridge (橋) he stops where the round turns, and before he turns he sees the wrong thing: snow is falling on the far bank. On the far road and on the eleven roofs above it, thick and straight, and over the bridge and the town the sky is clear to the stars (星), and the rail under his glove is dry. There is no cloud; he looks for one. He turns to hand the clappers back, because the bridge is 丸山's. 丸山 takes them, says 「三十二」, and strikes three toward the far bank as he does every night, and then does not put them in his coat. He holds them back out. 「二つ打て」. Two strikes are the hut's all-clear; they are struck at a door, with 異常なし, and answered from inside; there is no door here and nothing to answer. What refuses it is the one sentence a 後輩 cannot say, and he has now had it in his mouth for four nights. He says it. 「向こうには、誰もいないでしょう」. To the man who was born over there. And because the quit is the same sentence from the other side, it comes out behind it, badly, all of it in the wrong order: that he is quitting in March (三月で辞めます), that the town is finished, that his brother has found him a company in Tokyo, that he meant to say it on the 28th, that he is sorry. It is the first time all year he has said a sentence to 丸山 that 丸山 did not ask for. 丸山 does not argue 誰もいない. He says 「そうか」. Then, as if the only thing said had been a question about the clappers: 「二つだ」. He is not facing the far bank. He has his back to it, and the snow is coming down behind his shoulders and not on him, and the lamp hangs at his side pointed at the boards. 和夫 takes the clappers and strikes two, カチ、カチ, and his hands are so cold the second is late. 丸山 says 「遅い」. That is all he says to it. He takes the clappers out of 和夫's hand, wipes them with his sleeve the way he always does, and for longer, puts them in his coat, and says 「帰るぞ。鐘が鳴る」, and starts walking. 和夫 gets out 「雪が…」 and 丸山 says 「三十二だ。全部回った」, which is what he says at the bridge every night, and nothing else. The cost 和夫 pays: to get the quit out he had to say the one thing a 後輩 does not say to a 先輩, to the one man it could wound, and the old man answered it not with a word but with an instruction, and the instruction was to strike the all-clear at him, with the empty bank at his back and snow falling on it out of a clear sky; so his quit was accepted without a word of argument or of release, the reason he gave for it was neither denied nor granted, and he cannot ask what the two were for, or what the snow is, because a 後輩 does not ask a 先輩 about his round. He walks behind him back to the hut, carrying the lamp.

TWIST: what the story keeps back is that the three strikes at the bridge were never a salute to the empty houses. They are the far bank's half of the snow-year exchange, item 8: for eight nights in 1963 the far bank's senior came down to the bridge and struck three to say the eleven were alive, and the town's senior answered two from this end. The man who struck the three was 丸山, then the far bank's senior; the man who answered was 本間. 丸山 has struck his three at the bridge on every night of the year-end watch since he came across, which 本間 knows from every man who has walked behind him, and for nine years nobody has answered them, because the bridge is the senior's and the senior holds the clappers, there has been no junior to hold them, and the one man who ever answered cannot walk that far. On the last night of 1974 a first-year with the clappers in his hand, having just said there was nobody over there and that he was leaving, was told to strike two, and did. 本間 states the exchange and the names on the morning of the 1st, in speech, as the end of the story he is stopped from telling every year, understanding exactly what he says about 丸山 and not knowing what 和夫 struck; 和夫 states the rest in thought, that the two he struck were the first in nine years. The wrong detail the story never explains, the 怪談 exemption (AUTHORING § Craft, one turn): the snow that fell on the far bank alone, out of a sky of stars, on the night the three were answered. Nobody names it; 丸山 does not turn round to look at it; the afterword says it.

## PREMISE

On the last nights of 1974 a snow-country town's volunteer fire brigade keeps the year-end night watch: two men to a shift, a hut beside the pump truck, and a round of the district with wooden clappers and the call of 火の用心. 和夫, nineteen and in his first year, walks a step behind 丸山, who has been in the brigade since before 和夫 was born and has never once handed him the clappers. In the inside pocket of the brigade coat 和夫 carries a letter from his brother in Tokyo.

## ANCHOR

The clappers (拍子木) and their counts: two strikes at every house after 火の用心, two strikes at the hut door with 異常なし, three strikes at the bridge toward the far bank, and on the last night two struck at the bridge on an instruction. A ritual object, handled in every scene, never stored wet. The new words it carries: 拍子木 (×15 or more), 火の用心 (×8, the call that precedes every pair of strikes), 消防団 (×10, everyone's word for what they are), 詰所 (×8, where every round begins and ends). Four, at the brief's cap. have.py on the anchor's vocabulary: of 橋, 向こう, 岸, 坂, 打つ, 叩く, 返す, 鳴る, 鐘, 異常, 数える, 袖, 上着, 電灯, 足元, 火, 窓, 明かり, 暗い, 雪, 星, 空, 雲, 降る, 止む, 晴れる, 川, 寺, 名簿, 列, 班, 番, 順番, 一番, 久しぶり, 遅い, 晩, 八日, 餅, 酒, 差し入れ, 門松, ラジオ, 辞める, 残る, 答える, 聞こえる, 真っ暗, 息, 凍る, 拭く, 濡れる, しまう, 預ける, 屋根, 倒れる, 運ぶ, 建てる, 生まれ, 工場, 膝, all known; 消防団, 拍子木, 火の用心, 詰所 not known and declared; 夜警, 見回り, 当番, 団員, 分団, 分団長, 班長, 法被, 懐中電灯, ストーブ, 軒, 昭和, 合図, 対岸, 向こう岸, 移築, 大雪, 豪雪, 出ていく, 警防団, しめ飾り not known and carried by substitution or avoided as listed under CARRIED.

## WANT

To tell 丸山, before the year ends, that he is quitting the brigade in March and going to Tokyo.

## NEED

He has decided the town is finished and that the round is walked for nobody, and he has let that verdict stand untested because it makes his leaving cost nothing and need nobody's leave. The one man it could be put to is the man whose round it is, and a first-year does not correct a senior's round, so he has never said it to anyone, and he cannot get the quit out without it.

## SHAPE

Three-act. Act I is beats 1 to 3 (the 28th: the hut, the round, the stove). Act II is beats 4 to 6 (the walk home on the 28th with April inside it, the afternoon of the 31st at home, the hut before the last round). Act III is beats 7 and 8 (the bridge, and the morning of the 1st). The story covers two nights and one remembered afternoon, not a run of dates: 和夫 and 丸山 are paired on the 28th and the 31st, and the 29th and 30th do not appear.

## BEATS

**Act I**

1. The 28th, eight in the evening, the hut (詰所) beside the pump truck (消防車). 和夫 puts on the brigade coat (上着) and is handed the lamp (電灯); 丸山 takes the clappers (拍子木) from the shelf and wipes them with his sleeve (袖) before they go in his coat. 本間, the top of the brigade (分団長, as 一番上), reads the shift list (名簿) aloud, 和夫 and 丸山 on the 28th and the 31st, pours tea, and says the hut's rule for the year's last night as a thing everyone but 和夫 knows: 「大晦日の最後は、一番下が打つ。橋までじゃ」. One of the other pair, pulling on his boots: 「久しぶりだな、一番下が打つのは」, and 本間: 「九年ぶりじゃ」, and nobody says more about it. 和夫 has his brother's letter from Tokyo in the inside pocket and has decided to tell 丸山 by the 31st, because it was 丸山 who brought him in and the junior tells the senior (先輩), not 本間, and because he will not walk the year's last round in front as a man who is leaving and has not said so. Yes, but: the deadline is now three nights, and the man he must tell is the one man a first-year (後輩) does not speak to first.
2. The round (町を回る). 丸山 calls 火の用心 at every house and strikes twice, カチ、カチ; 和夫 walks one step behind with the lamp and counts (数える) the dark windows, not the lit ones. Thirty-two houses, and the thirty-second, nearest the river, is 丸山's own, which the narration tells plainly as the thing the whole town knows: 丸山 is 向こうの生まれ, came over the bridge the year the far bank left, and the house is his far-bank house, taken down and carried across and built again by his own hands (自分で運んで、こっちで建てた). The round turns at the bridge (橋); across the river the far road goes up, and on the slope (坂) above it, in snow-light, the eleven roofs (屋根): 和夫 counts them, eight fallen under nine winters and three standing, none shovelled. 丸山 says 「三十二」 and then strikes three times toward them before turning back, and 和夫 files it as a far-bank man's full stop, said to his own roofs. The narration has said, at the hut, that 本間 does not walk and that of the men who do, 丸山 is the top, so the clappers on any round he is on are his (C6). Back at the hut, 丸山 strikes twice on the door and calls 異常なし, and 本間 answers 「おう」 from inside without opening it. No, and: 和夫 said nothing the whole round, because a 後輩 does not open a conversation on a senior's round, and he has learned that the round ends not at the hut but at the bridge, in front of a man's own empty hillside, where the sentence he has to say is a worse one than he thought.
3. The stove. 本間 tells the story of the snow year (三八豪雪, as あの雪の年, 雪がたくさん降った年): the far road buried for eight days, the eleven houses up it cut off with their own section (班) of the brigade, the bridge drifted shut and closed like the road, the telephone line down. He gets as far as 「晩になるとな」 and 丸山 says 「本間さん、その話は去年も聞いたぞ」 and gets up to see to the fire, and the story stops where, 和夫 gathers, it stops every year: an old man's story cut off by a man tired of it, and nothing more (C5). 本間 tells 和夫 the end instead of the middle: two springs later all eleven left for the city together (集団離村, as みんなで町を出た), and the far section ended; 丸山 walked their last round with them, and came across. 和夫 asks nothing. Yes, but: 和夫 now has his verdict, the round ends in front of eleven fallen roofs and the thirty-two are going the same way, and he cannot ask about the three strikes, because asking is correcting a senior's round (先輩・後輩), and the senior is the man the roofs belong to. Walking home at midnight he counts the dark windows again.

**Act II**

1. The walk home, the 28th, after midnight, the same road, 丸山 a step ahead with the clappers in his coat. 和夫 tries. 「丸山さん」, the first time he has opened a sentence to him all year. Without turning: 「電灯、下げるな。足元だ」. The lamp jerks up, the sentence does not, and the coat's sleeve (袖) catches on the cut bamboo of a 門松 already up at a gate and tears. Inside the silence, April: rain, 丸山 at the family door asking 和夫's father (父) for him, the brigade (消防団) down to twelve men and 和夫 the only one who would be under thirty, the factory (工場) cutting shifts and the young ones going; the father, who went through 丸山 once himself when his knees went, saying 「預けます」; and to 和夫, 丸山 said only 「後ろを歩くだけだ」. No, and: a 後輩's opening is answered with an instruction before it is a sentence, and he has found out what the quit needs to stand up: a reason, and the reason is the one sentence a 後輩 cannot say to a 先輩, that the round is for nobody. Bare, 三月で辞めます has nowhere to land. And the coat is torn.
2. The 31st, afternoon, home. The torn sleeve put the brigade coat (上着) in his mother's (母) hands on the morning of the 29th, and she has mended it, and packed rice cakes (餅) for the hut (差し入れ), and the coat is what she hands him when she asks 「丸山さんに、言ったの？」 and he says 「いえ」. She knows about Tokyo and does not argue it; the neighbourhood (近所) already says the young ones are going. What she says is 「丸山さんには、ちゃんと言いなさい。あの人が、お前を入れたんだから」, and that it is his telling, not hers, because that is the order things go in (先輩 first, then 本間). At the gate his father is setting the 門松 and says only 「丸山さんによろしく」, which from a man who went through 丸山 once is the same instruction. Yes, but: the sleeve is mended for a year he will not serve, the telling is now his job by both parents' word as well as the brigade's, the house knows from a torn sleeve that nothing was said, and none of them can walk it for him.
3. The 31st, eleven at night, the hut. The radio plays the year-end singing; 本間 says the town's brigade head (団長) came round on the 30th (激励, as 団長が来た) and left the sake, and pours one cup each; another pair comes back, two strikes on the door, 異常なし, 本間's 「おう」 without looking up. The other pair's senior, taking his cup: 「和夫、兄さん東京だってな」. 和夫 puts the 餅 by the fire and goes to 丸山 before the round, with the sentence ready this time: 「丸山さん、あの、俺…」. 丸山 takes the clappers (拍子木) from the shelf, wipes them, and instead of putting them in his coat puts them in 和夫's hand, the hut's rule for the last night: 「今夜はお前が打て。橋までだ」, and takes the lamp (電灯) out of 和夫's other hand. The sentence dies a second time. No, and: the town already knows, so the telling will be late as well as bad; the clappers are in his hand, which he never asked for; and now he walks in front and 丸山 behind, so the thing he has to say must be said to a man at his back, on the last round, before the bell (寺の鐘), with nothing to answer him with but an instruction.

**Act III**

1. The bridge (橋). See CLIMAX. 和夫 has called 火の用心 and struck twice at thirty-two doors with 門松 on them, the last one 丸山's; at the bridge, before he turns, snow (雪) is falling on the far bank and the far road and the eleven roofs, out of a sky of stars (星), and none on the bridge. He turns to hand the clappers back, because the bridge is 丸山's. 丸山 says 「三十二」, strikes three toward the far bank as always, and holds the clappers back out: 「二つ打て」. 和夫 says the sentence a 後輩 does not say, 「向こうには、誰もいないでしょう」, to the man born over there, and behind it, in the wrong order, the quit: 三月で辞めます, the town is finished, Tokyo, his brother, that he meant to say it on the 28th. 丸山: 「そうか」, then 「二つだ」, with his back to the far bank and the snow behind him. 和夫 strikes two, the second late. 丸山: 「遅い」. He takes the clappers, wipes them with his sleeve (袖), says 「帰るぞ。鐘が鳴る」 and the count, 「三十二だ。全部回った」, and nothing else; 和夫's 「雪が…」 gets the count. No, and: he got the quit out only by saying the verdict to the man's face, the verdict was answered with an instruction to strike the all-clear at the man himself, the quit was taken without argument or release, snow is falling where there is nobody and nowhere else, and a 後輩 cannot ask a 先輩 about his round. He walks behind him with the lamp, and looks back once.
2. The hut door: 和夫 strikes twice, calls 異常なし, 本間 answers 「おう」, and the temple bell (寺の鐘) begins. Morning of the 1st, the hut: 和夫 on the last shift cleans the stove; 本間 writes the turnout list (名簿) for the ceremony (出初め式) on the 6th and says 「三月までか」, because 丸山 has already told him, which is the proper order, and writes 和夫's name at the end of the line (列の後ろ): 「三月までは消防団じゃ。六日は来い」. Then, to the list and not to 和夫, the night that 丸山 stops him from telling: in the snow year, every night for eight (八日), three strikes came down from the far end of the shut bridge, the far hut's own door count, and the hut knew the eleven were alive; 「打っとったのは丸山じゃ。向こうの一番上じゃった。わしが、こっちで二つ返した」; and that 丸山 still strikes three there every night of the watch, which every man who has walked behind him has told 本間, and 「わしはもう橋まで行けん」. 和夫 says nothing. In thought he has the rest: the two he struck were the first in nine years, and he struck them as a man leaving. He picks up the clappers (拍子木) from the table to put them on the shelf and wipes them first with the sleeve his mother mended, as he has seen it done. 丸山, in the doorway, holds out his hand: 「貸せ」, and puts them in his own coat, dry, where they spend 正月 every year; the shelf stays empty. Then the last line of the story: 「六日は後ろを歩け」. Yes, but: his want is granted in exactly the brigade's form, passed up without him and written down at the back of the line for the months he has left, the two strikes he gave go home in the old man's coat with the three, nobody in the room but the two of them knows they were struck, and the ordinary resumes with him told where to walk.

Twist: in both rounds all three named it in full and quoted the head's morning speech and the narrator's thought, the two places the TWIST line puts it, and all three said it was all but stated before; the reconciler ruled that planted setup, not a leak, since no earlier line names the signal, who struck it or who answered, and both Japanese-only readers said it confirms more than it surprises, which they found fitting for the register. All three readers took the snow as unexplained, as the register requires. Both Japanese-only readers named the practice, the year-end watch with its door count, and the 先輩・後輩 order of telling, and found the sparse speech natural, with the clapper code as the real channel. Naturalness middling, rising by a step for one reader between rounds. Left as flagged, non-gating: in both draft rounds both Japanese-only readers noted that only the hut head speaks western dialect while the senior and the parents, born in the same valley, speak standard Japanese, so the head's じゃ reads as stock old-man 役割語; it is a voice choice and gates nothing, but it sits near Rob's standing note about generic characters. Also flagged: the empty-shelf sentence echoes the September audit's arrived-at ending, though it is not the ending; the town's brigade chief stays as a rank device; the two unnamed seniors are hard to tell apart.

new_words.消防団: the volunteer fire brigade, what they all are. First occurrence p1 on the brigade coats on the top shelf; recurs as the brigade 丸山 brought the narrator into, the twelve men it is down to, the brigade his father left, the far bank's own section in 本間's snow story, and 本間's 三月までは消防団じゃ on the 1st
new_words.拍子木: the wooden clappers, the anchor. First occurrence p1 taken off the shelf and wiped with a sleeve before they go into a coat; struck twice at every door, twice at the hut, three times at the bridge, and on the last night two at the bridge on an instruction
new_words.詰所: the brigade hut beside the pump truck, where every round begins and ends. First occurrence p1 as the room the narrator walks into at eight; recurs as the place 本間 no longer leaves, the door struck twice with 異常なし, the radio on the 31st, the mother's 差し入れ, and the far bank's own hut (向こうの詰所) in 本間's story on the 1st
new_words.懐中電灯: the hand lamp the junior carries on the round, pointed at the senior's feet. Declared in revision r1 because both Japanese-only readers flagged bare 電灯 for a flashlight as unnatural; the junior's one job object, it recurs on every round. First occurrence p1 as the narrator is handed it; recurs at the senior's feet on the round, in 丸山's 懐中電灯、上げるな on the walk home, taken from the narrator's hand in exchange for the clappers on the 31st, hanging at 丸山's side at the bridge, and carried back behind him

stories.title: 猫を探す探偵
stories._feature: A plot held across 30 pages: the boxes clue is planted on page 8 and not recalled until page 21, and the reader is expected to reach the answer from facts already on the page. The second plant is the detective's own: a book borrowed at twelve and never returned, p22, which makes his decision about the boy a fact about him rather than a position he argues. The story now ends on that book, the cold office and a fee that does not cover the rent. THE NO-THESIS EXCEPTION WAS RETIRED 2026-09-19. This key used to read 'the one exception to the no-thesis rule; it is allowed to state its closing claim outright', which licensed the last two lines, 探偵の仕事は真実を見つけることじゃない。見つけた真実をどうするかだ。 Four evaluators independently named that pair as the clearest proof of an English short-story pattern in the corpus. The afterword mechanism now says it in English on the last page, which is where it belongs, so the lines are cut and the exception does not survive them.
stories._new_words: This story's four teaching words predate the per-story mechanism and still live in approved-words.json, where they are marked correctly. Left there rather than moved, to avoid churn; new stories should declare theirs here instead.

stories.title: スープを残す客
stories._feature: Second story in the comic register and the first at level 4 since 猫を探す探偵. Three-act, eight beats. The misreading engine is new: every sign of a salt ration (water first, a white medicine packet, a notebook, a hospital sighting) is read by the owner as a verdict on his broth, so each fix he makes aims at the wrong problem and lands on another customer. The climax is three dry lines from a man who almost never speaks, and the owner's turn is shown only in action: he pours the half away and does not look at the line.
stories._note: 半分さん IS THE OWNER'S PRIVATE NICKNAME, said only in his head from p2 (小林にも言ったことはない); he lets it slip on p13 and 小林 grins, which is the setup for 小林 writing it on the wall in the last act. FOUR VOICES: 松田 俺 / 〜ぞ / ねえ; 小林 〜っす; 高橋 loud, 〜な / 〜ぞ / あんのか; 半分さん わし / 〜とる / 〜ん, three lines at the climax and one at the close. The health plants are meant to read as health to the reader from first sight while 松田's verdict stays confidently wrong. NO WEEKLY MARCH: visits are undated, the only time markers are その日, ある朝, その週のうちに, 次に. Side characters close on the page: the student gets the お湯 on the wall, 高橋's wife orders it for her health, 小林 gets the nickname. Peeked words reused on purpose: 渡す, 黙る, 隣, 決める, 近所, 返事. Names chosen to survive segmentation whole: 健太, 田中, 大野 and 佐藤 all split or failed check.py in drafting.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: 半分さん drinks the owner's near-saltless private pot to the bottom; 高橋 starts clapping. He takes out the white packet, opens his 手帳 on the counter and orders a regular bowl. Three dry lines: 医者に、一日の塩を決められとる / わしの分は、ここで使うことにしとる / これは、お湯だ。数に入らん. The page logs 松田　半分 against salt on every date. He drinks exactly half of the real bowl, pays for two and leaves; 松田 pours the half away without looking at the line. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: 松田 has run a ten-seat ramen shop for thirty years and measures himself by the soup left in the bowl; one quiet regular always drinks exactly half, and 松田 sets out to fix the broth. WANT: 半分さん drinks the bowl to the bottom. NEED: he cannot trust his broth without an empty bowl to tell him so; he has to take the half as the compliment it is. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2 (pp1-5), II 3-6 (pp6-16), III 7-8 (pp17-23). BEATS: 1 the ritual, pill read as stomach medicine, notebook as a score (no-and). 2 高橋 saw him at the hospital, read as my soup put him there; the want stated (yes-but). 3 double bones; 高橋 loves it, the student sweats, 小林 admits it was always salty, 半分さん drinks less (no-and). 4 the steam theory, a cooled bowl, 小林 serves it to 高橋 (no-and: the rumour of a special bowl). 5 a private small pot with less salt each visit; the line drops; the nickname slips; the student orders it (yes-but). 6 the pot becomes hot water, the big pot burns (no-and). 7 CLIMAX (yes-but: won and worthless). 8 the card 半分さんの on the wall; 半分さん orders regular, わしは、そっちは頼まんぞ / 頼まんでいい.

new_words.麺: noodles. First occurrence p1 is the regular eating them down to the last strand, part of the ritual the whole story watches; recurs in every repetition of that ritual and in 麺の湯を切った
new_words.丼: the ramen bowl, and the scoreboard of the whole story: the line of soup left in it is what the owner reads. First occurrence p1, arriving and then lifted in both hands
new_words.暖簾: the shop curtain. First occurrence is the owner hanging it out at eleven, the opening action of the story; the regular ducks under it to leave and arrive, and the last line is spoken through it
new_words.湯気: steam off the bowl. First occurrence fogs the regular's glasses, which is the red herring the owner chases in the second fix (the cooled bowl)

stories.title: 父の鋏
stories._premise: CLIMAX: 佐野's monthly cut. The father's scissors drag instead of cutting above the ear, 佐野 hisses (the same っ as p5), the open scissors shake. 修 steps in with his own scissors; 佐野 speaks past him to the father in the mirror: 先月も、その前の月も痛かったぞ。黙ってりゃ、勝が自分で気づくと思ったんだがな. 修 remembers the silent Sunday nights and the thumb on the blade. TURN: 私は自分の鋏を台に置いて、父の手から鋏を取った。 He sharpens on the dry 砥石 in the back while the two old men talk baseball through the curtain, hands the scissors back, and the father tests one hair and says 寝かせすぎだ. 修 never cuts 佐野. AFTERWORD: stories-index.md. PREMISE: 修, 34, works beside his father in their two-chair 床屋. The father's hands shake; he still cuts his oldest regulars with his own scissors and will not discuss stopping. WANTS: 修, to cut 佐野, which would make the shop his. 父 (勝, わし), to keep cutting his regulars with his own scissors and never be seen failing. 佐野 (下町, 〜ぞ/〜な), いつもの from 勝 and nothing else; his secret is that he has known about the dull blades for months. NEED (修): he has never asked or offered anything, and waits to be handed the chair as proof, which is his father's pride in him. He must offer the thing he resents rather than claim the thing he wants. SHAPE: three-act, across the month between two visits, childhood recalled inside it. BEATS: I-1 佐野's っ, covered by a joke; the scissors sound dull; 修 blames the hands (yes-but: cut done, 修 resolves the father must stop). I-2 childhood Sundays made to sharpen (研がされた), 寝かせすぎだ / もう少し立てろ; he has not touched a stone since school; this Sunday the back room is silent and he reads it as tiredness (no-and). II-3 来月から俺がやる; わしの客だ; next morning the case is locked (no-and). II-4 修 asks 佐野 directly; the wedding haircut; 勝の鋏でいい (no-and). II-5 岡田 defects to the station chain; at night the father, case open, thumb on the blade, unexplained (yes-but). III-6 climax. III-7 the dry stone, the sharpening, the talk through the curtain (yes-but: blade fixed, and so he is not the one cutting). III-8 寝かせすぎだ; 佐野 to 修, 来月も頼むぞ, the first time he has looked him in the eye. III-9 Sunday night, the father behind him with an unturned newspaper: もう少し立てろ; everything laid out on a towel.

new_words.研ぐ: to sharpen, on a stone — the chore the son was made to do as a boy and refused ever since, and the act after the turn. First doing work p8 as something paid for and handed off, 駅前の店に持っていって研いでもらう. Recurs through the childhood Sundays, the climax and the last page
new_words.刃: blade — first in the same habit, 刃が鈍くなる前に, then on the stone, under the father's thumb at night, and turned to the lamp at the payoff
new_words.砥石: whetstone — first wet and worked by the father's hands, 砥石を水で濡らして刃を当て. Recurs as the thing the boy was sat in front of, the thing the man swore off, and dry on the shelf at the climax
new_words.鈍い: dull, of a blade and of its sound — planted p2 as a sound the son blames on shaking hands, then as the son's own sharpening habit, then as the sound of the climax and the sound that stops
new_words.剃刀: razor — first used rather than named: the father shaves 佐野's neck with his right hand gripped in his left. Recurs on the mirror shelf, in the same gesture after the turn, and on the last page's stone

stories.title: 白い番号
stories._feature: Procedural register, level 4, the second mystery in the corpus after 猫を探す探偵 and written against its review: the boy is the centre and gets the last move, nobody is paid half for a trope, and nobody is dead. The plant does visible work of its own: the white paint number under every 防犯登録 sticker is introduced recovering a stolen bike for the police on page 1, which also misdirects the reader toward theft. The reader can reach the buyer from three facts before the ledger opens: 木 begun and struck out on the repair slip, 雄 shared by 雄太 and 雄一, and the saddle set for someone ten centimetres taller.
stories._note: Topic changed at Gate 1 by the orchestrating session: option 1 (an old man who pushes rather than rides) overlapped another level 4 story in the same batch. Responds to reviews.py: 猫を探す探偵 ★4 (boy disappears, unexplained half pay), 城の鐘 ★4 (monotonic day-by-day time, generic voices), 煙突の煙 ★2 (another dead person). Time moves morning, evening, night, ten days, one evening; no sequence of days. Voices: narrator 俺/〜ぞ/〜な to the boy, 道子 〜わよ/あんた, 雄太 です・ます slipping, 木村 polite and brief. CONTACT HISTORY, made consistent at Gate 2: father and son met once, in March at the station, after six years; the father bought the bike here that morning, guessing the height; the boy told him the new surname then and refused his address, so the bike is registered to the father; no contact since; the father came back in summer fishing for any sign; the mother does not know the meeting happened.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: after closing, 木村 signs the transfer as previous owner and writes 中村雄太 as new owner without asking, sees the saddle three fingers below the height he chose in March, asks only about the brakes; the boy folds the signed paper into his pocket and tells the narrator not to register it: if stopped again he will say it is 木村's bicycle. The narrator tapes the old sticker back over his white number and corrects 170 to 160 in the ledger, the first correction in thirty years. AFTERWORD: stories-index.md. PREMISE: a high-schooler wants a nearly new bike registered to himself, says it is secondhand with no paper; under the scratched sticker is the shop's own white number, and the ledger says the narrator sold it in March to a man buying it for his son. WANT (雄太): the bike in his own name so it cannot lead back to his father. NEED: to admit he wants his father. Narrator's cost: phoning a customer out of the ledger, against his rule, against the boy's wish, in front of his wife. SHAPE: three-act. BEATS: ACT I (1) police bring a stolen bike, identified by the white number; second stop means a call home / (2) the boy, the saddle, the lie, 木 crossed out, no home number. ACT II (3) the number under the sticker, the ledger, 170; registration refused / (4) 道子 remembers the father's summer visit, the rule holds / (5) the forged paper, 雄 stroke for stroke / (6) 'we sold this bike in March'; the meeting, the mother, the police. ACT III (7) the call, the rule broken aloud / (8) climax / (9) tape, ledger, 160.

new_words.防犯: crime prevention, met only inside 防犯登録, the bicycle registration sticker every bike in Japan carries; declared as 防犯 because Ichiran segments the compound as 防犯 + 登録 and 登録 is known, the sticker every bike in Japan carries. First doing work p1, peeled off a stolen bike so its owner cannot be found; the engine of the plot, since a name mismatch on it is what gets the boy stopped
new_words.台帳: the shop's sales ledger. First carried out of the back and searched with a finger p3, then shelved as the thing shown only to police
new_words.剥ぐ: to peel off, written throughout as 剥がす; keyed 剥ぐ because Ichiran lemmatises every 剥がす form in this story (剥がして, 剥がした, 剥がせて, 剥がし) to 剥ぐ, so a 剥がす key matches nothing. First as what a thief did to the sticker p1, then what the boy half did and the narrator finished
new_words.ペンキ: paint. First wiped clear of grime to reveal the number p2; the hidden number of the title
new_words.中古: secondhand. The boy's lie, first said in answer to where he got it, and repeated as what he told his mother
new_words.サドル: saddle. First as the job the boy asks for; its height is the clue that the buyer guessed a son he had not seen

stories.title: 一人半
stories._brief: Level 4 (N3 solid), retrospective, 18 pages with page_slack 2 (16 to 20): Rob asked for 15 to 20 pages, and the slack records that request. Every other parameter was settled by the pipeline, not Rob.
stories._premise:
Level 4 (N3 solid), register retrospective, 18 pages (16 to 20), new_words 7 (raised from 4 at draft round 1), leech seeds 5, min occurrences 2. Rob asked for 15 to 20 pages, and the page slack of 2 records that; every other Gate 1 parameter was settled by the pipeline. Gate 2 passed on round 2; the round-2 critic's fixes F1 to F8 are applied below, and five characters were renamed at drafting so that every name segments into known parts (see the note under VOICES). Refreshed from the sheet at ship (2026-11-14): the WANT and TWIST lines, the book and the new-word counts in CULTURE, CARRIED and ANCHOR, and the seedling baskets in PRACTICE now match the final text. CLIMAX and BEATS are the plan of record and differ from the story in small particulars.

TITLE: 一人半 (ひとりはん). Slug `hitori-han`. Level 4 (N3 solid). Register retrospective (述懐). Pages 18 ±2 (16 to 20; Rob asked for 15 to 20 pages, and the slack records that). About 360 tokens, new_words 4 (raised to 7 at draft round 1: 苗代, 帳面, 一人前), leech_seeds 5, min occurrences 2.

## CULTURE

**PRACTICE: 結 (ゆい) at 田植え, the hamlet's labour exchange, as it ran in a one-crop hill hamlet of 安曇野 (Nagano) in 1955, before the planting machine.**

Written as a procedure:

1. **The group and the book.** A 結 group (結の組) is five houses on one lane. The count is kept in a book (帳面, declared at draft round 1; it replaces the postwar ノート) at 金蔵's house: for each house, days received on one side and days given on the other, in person-days (一人役, carried as 一人前, declared at draft round 1: one grown man or woman for one day). The hamlet's own rules, stated once by 糸 in the text and not confirmed by any source below: a grown hand who comes to the host's seedbed before dawn for the 苗取り (step 3) and then plants the day is written as one and a half (一人半); a child's 苗運び is not written at all ("the book writes hands"). A day received is returned the same season as the same work (the Minpaku principle, exchange rate 1); what cannot be returned at planting is carried on the book to the first weeding (一番草, carried as 草取り) after the 農休み, or to the harvest. Nobody speaks of a house's balance and everybody knows it.
2. **The calendar.** When the snow shape of the monk (常念坊) shows on 常念岳 in late April, the men plaster the paddy banks with mud (畦塗り, carried as 畦に泥を塗る) and turn the paddies. The seedbed (苗代, declared at draft round 1) is sown after the 花まつり of 卯月八日, which is 8 May in Shinshū's month-late calendar (安曇野 source). The paddies are flooded and harrowed with the horse (代掻き, carried as 馬で田んぼをならす) in the last days of May. The 苗 are ready about forty days after sowing, mid June, and the 梅雨 arrives at about the same time (around 9 June in 1955 in this story). The five heads meet at 金蔵's house in late May and set the order of the five days. The deadline is the 苗 and the rest, not a date: 苗 left in the seedbed past forty days grow too tall and their roots mat (伸びすぎる), and the lane takes its 農休み on 1 to 3 July (豊科, 安曇野 source), by which everything must be in. These hill paddies grow one crop (一毛作); the plain's barley-then-rice (あと田) and its 18 June rule are not this hamlet's and are out (see ABSENT).
3. **The host's day, before dawn.** The host's men, and whoever comes early, pull the 苗 from the seedbed (苗取り), tie them in bundles with straw, and carry them to the paddy bank (畦) in baskets (苗かご; boxes and trays belong to the machine era, so the story carries the 苗 by the armful and keeps 苗の箱 for the coda).
4. **The rope and the line.** The men stretch the planting rope (田植え縄, carried as 印のついたひも) across the paddy from a spike driven into the 畦 on each side. The rope carries a mark (印) at every hill, about a hand's span apart (株間; 摂津 source: the rope is the baseline of the 正条植え). The leader of the women's line, here 糸, counts the marks aloud and divides them by the women present: each woman gets her stretch of hills (持ち場, carried as 自分の六株, 自分の分), and 糸 says each stretch aloud from the near spike outward. The women stand in one line (列) in the water facing the rope and each plants her hills in the row; the men on the 畦 lift the rope one step back; the line steps back and plants the next row. Fewer women means more hills each and a longer day; more women means fewer hills each. The division is made once, at the first row, and 糸 does not remake it mid-morning. A crooked row cannot be weeded with the push weeder in July (摂津 source), so the rope is the law of the paddy and nobody plants off it.
5. **Carrying and throwing.** Children and half-hands carry 苗 from the baskets (苗運び) and throw bundles to the women from the 畦 (苗打ち) so nobody leaves the line. The terms, and the saying that if you can throw 苗 right you are a full hand, are from 摂津 (Osaka), not Nagano; they are used here as a plausible practice, and 糸 says the saying in her own Shinshū words, not the Settsu formula.
6. **Food.** The host house feeds the hands on the 畦: the ten o'clock 小昼 (carried unnamed as 十時のおにぎり; 安曇野 gives きなこむすび), the noon meal, the three o'clock tea. The host's women cook; a house with a mother, a bride and a daughter sends the bride to plant and keeps the mother and the daughter in the kitchen, because the bride is the house's labour and the mother is its kitchen.
7. **The evening.** When the host's last paddy is planted, three bundles of 苗 are set on the household shelf (神棚, carried as 神様の棚) with a bowl of rice (安曇野 source), and the house feeds everyone who planted, with sake (マンガレー, 馬鍬洗い; carried unnamed as 田植えがすんだ夜の飯). The day's count is spoken aloud by 糸 and written by 金蔵.
8. **This house's arithmetic in 1955,** which is what the story counts. The lane's standard is three hands a house on each of the other four days: twelve given, twelve received, balanced. Before a 苗 was in the water this house had already taken three days from the lane: 金蔵 and his horse two days at the 代掻き, and 金蔵 one day finishing the 畦 the father had left half plastered. Nothing stood against them. On the given side the house could send 実, ナツ and 雪子, three a day, twelve: against twelve on 17 June plus the three of May, fifteen. Three short. With 雪子 written one and a half on all four days, fourteen: one short, to be paid at the 一番草 after the 農休み. And the father's back did not come back: every spring after, the house took a man's days from the lane for the horse work, and 雪子's half was the house's standing return for them, nineteen Junes.

**PRESSURE: 恩 and お返し.** A day taken is a day owed. The house went into the season three days in the lane's debt, and the lane knows to the day. That is what forbids the thing the family has decided: a house that is asking the lane to carry it cannot, in the same breath, be seen spending on a luxury, and a daughter at a town high school is a luxury, three years of fees and board and three years in which the hand the house would have had at fifteen is in a classroom. So the plan stays unsaid until the return is arranged in a form the lane will accept, which is the bride's hands, written in the book. It stays unsaid inside the house too, because telling 文子 that 雪子 is paying for her would put the sister in the bride's debt, and a 嫁 two months in the house cannot be owed by anyone in it. Take the pressure away and the family says the whole thing at the table in one line: you're going to high school next year, your sister-in-law will cover your share.

**VOICES** (Shinshū dialect, kept to four forms the reader can carry: 〜ずら (だろう), 〜だに (だよ), 〜しな (しなさい), 〜だで (だから)):

- **文子** (ふみこ), the narrator. Fourteen in June 1955, eighty-five in June 2026. Narration: 私, long subordinated sentences, タ and ル moving inside a scene, no dialect; she left the hamlet in 1956 and the dialect left her. In 1955 speech: あたし, 〜だに, 〜ずら, blunt questions. Addresses her mother おかあちゃん, her brother 兄ちゃん, her father おとうちゃん, and the bride 雪子さん, never 姉さん though her mother has told her twice to say it. Habit: she counts things, hills, marks, bundles, days, and says the number.
- **雪子** (ゆきこ), the bride. Twenty-two, from a rice hamlet in the next valley (池田 side), married into the house in early April; six years of school, the old 国民学校, and no more. です・ます to everyone in the house, including 文子, whom she calls 文子さん; わたし; short sentences; answers an emotional question with a task (「お味噌汁、冷めます」, 「ひも、動かしてください」). Habit: wipes her hands on the cloth at her waist before she touches anything in the house, is up and out before the hens every morning from mid-May (the paddies' water round in May, the 苗取り on the planting days), and reads at night by the lamp (明かり). Plants deep, to the wrist, and never leaves a floating 苗.
- **実** (みのる), the brother. Twenty-four. おれ, 〜だ, 〜ずら, 〜しろ, 〜だで; calls 文子 おまえ or 文子, 雪子 by name with no さん, his mother おかあ, his father 親父. Speaks in one breath and goes back to work. Holds the rope's end on the 畦. Ninety-five now, alive, in the hill house.
- **ナツ**, the mother. Forty-seven. 〜しな, 〜だで, 〜だに; calls 文子 文, 実 実, and the bride 雪子さん with the さん a 姑 keeps for the first year. Dry; jokes with numbers, and her jokes have a 姑's edge. Her 「雪子さんは一人半だに」 at the late-May table is the story's phrase.
- **庄吉** (しょうきち), the father. Fifty. わし, 〜だ, 〜な. Lying on the 布団 in the back room since the last week of April with his back gone; speaks once in the story, at the evening meal, to the bride: 「雪子、座れ」.
- **糸** (いと), 金蔵's wife, the next house down the lane, forty-five (a woman of her year is registered in kana). Leads the women's line, counts the marks aloud and divides the hills. 〜だに, 〜ずら, 〜しな at full volume; calls 文子 文ちゃん and the bride 雪子さん. She sings the first line of the planting song on every planting day and the line follows; on the house's day she does not sing in the paddy, which is no custom but her own answer to what she has watched, and she sings at the evening meal instead. Speaks the day's count at the evening meal.
- **金蔵** (きんぞう), her husband, fifty, head of the 結 group, owner of the lane's horse. Does not speak; drives the far spike, writes in the notebook.

**SEASON: June, as a subject.** The 梅雨 arrives the week the 苗 come ready, and the lane's five days are set for the week before the 苗 overgrow. Every rain day pushes the order back and makes the last house's 苗 a day older. The house in this story is the last of the five. Nothing dries: the 手ぬぐい on the line, the 布団 in the back room, the 泥 on the step. The story cannot move to another month without changing the practice, because the practice is the month.

## CLIMAX

The house's day, 17 June 1955, the fifth and last of the lane's five, in drizzle. The rope (印のついたひも) is stretched across the house's big paddy from 金蔵's spike to 実's, and 糸 counts the marks aloud as she always does: seventy-two. Eleven women from the four houses and 雪子 stand on the 畦, and 糸 divides: 「十二人、六株ずつ」, and says each woman's six from 金蔵's spike outward, 雪子 last, the six nearest 実's spike. The children, and the half-hands, which this morning means 文子, are on the 畦 with the 苗 boxes. 文子 has been told she is the kitchen today, with her mother. The first row goes in and the rope lifts once. Then 文子 takes off her sandals at the 畦, wades in with the water to her shins, and walks down the line past 雪子 to where the hills end. There is nothing past the last six: the spike, and the bank. 糸 looks at the rope and says, to nobody, that the rope is the rope: the hills were given at the first row and are not given twice, and the host house put its daughter in the kitchen, and she will not stand twelve women over again against a host's word. The line does not move; 実 cannot lift the rope until the line is right. 雪子 steps out of her six hills, wipes her hands on the cloth at her waist, and says 「文子さん、ここ。六株です」, and climbs onto the 畦 and takes the 苗 box out of the children's hands. The 嫁 has left the line on her own house's day, in front of four houses, and what the lane will say about a bride who will not plant her own house's paddy is now standing on the 畦 with the whole lane looking at it. 実, with the rope's end in his hand, says it, in one breath and loud enough for the line, because the rope cannot move until the line is right and because the other thing the lane could be left to say is about his wife: 「おまえは来年から町の高校だ。雪子が親父に頭を下げたんだ。文子の分は毎年、わたしが暗いうちから苗を取りに出ますって。それで雪子は一人半だ。そういうことだで、おまえは台所に行け」. Then, to the bride: 「雪子、戻れ。ひもが動かん」. 雪子 does not go back. She throws 文子 a bundle of 苗, underhand, so it lands in the water beside her hand, which is the children's job done properly, and says 「ひも、動かしてください」. The rope lifts. 文子 plants her six, to the wrist, the way she has watched the bride do it since the tenth, and her hands go on alone while the rest of her is somewhere else; at the tenth row, when the rope lifts, she climbs out onto the 畦, puts the 苗 box in 雪子's hands and takes the bundles from her, and the bride goes back into the water to her six. 文子 throws 苗 to the line for the rest of the day, badly at first and then well, runs the ten o'clock おにぎり down from the house because her mother is alone in the kitchen, and nobody says anything about any of it, and 糸 does not sing.

**TWIST.** What the story keeps back: in May, the week after the 中学 teacher's visit, the family decided that 文子 will leave for the 松本 high school next spring, and 雪子, six weeks in the house, went to the father and asked for it, offering the only thing a 嫁 has, her hands: she would go to every house's day from the dawn 苗取り (半分) on top of her own day, every year, as the house's return (お返し) to the lane for the man's days it takes, which is why 金蔵 writes her as one and a half and why the mother has called her 一人半 since the late-May table, which 文子 laughs at as a joke about a bride who is up before the hens, and then, when the mother says it again in front of the lane on the first planting day, hears as her mother preferring the bride, who already stands in the place in the line meant for 文子. (Synced at ship, 2026-11-14: the round-1 draft revision replaced the 姑's-dig reading with this one.) 実 states it, aloud, on the 畦, in the lines above, and understands it fully; 糸 states the second half of it at the evening meal, that 雪子 is written in the book as 一人半 on all four days and that 文子's six hills today are written as the house's last owed day. Nobody deduces anything. The sister is told, in front of the lane, and the telling is the humiliation.

## PREMISE

June 1955, a rice hamlet in the hills of 安曇野. 文子, fourteen, is the daughter of the house: her father's back went in April, her brother's bride 雪子 came into the house the same month, and this year the house goes into the lane's planting exchange (結) three days in debt, with exactly the three hands a day to give back that every house gives. 文子 is a child, who carries seedlings and is not written in the book, and she means to be sent to the lane's planting days as one of her house's hands and written as one.

## ANCHOR

The planting line: the marked rope (印のついたひも) stretched across the paddy, the hills divided among the women, the count of hands written in 金蔵's notebook, and the phrase 一人半. One narrow cluster, in action on every planting page: 苗 sown, pulled, tied, carried, thrown and floating; the rope lifted and moved; marks, hills and hands counted aloud. New words it carries (have.py run; all four unknown, nothing else in the cluster is): 結 ×8 or so (the group, the days, the book), 田植え ×10 (the days, the holiday, the song, the rope, the machine), 苗 ×12 (seedbed, bundles, throwing, floating, overgrown, the shelf), 畦 ×7 (plastered, the spike, the おにぎり, the men with the rope, 雪子 now). Four was the brief's cap at Gate 2; it was raised to 7 at draft round 1. 結 will need ｜結《ゆい》 annotated at every occurrence, since Ichiran reads the bare kanji otherwise.

## WANT

To go to all four of the other houses' planting days as her house's fourth hand and be written in 金蔵's book (帳面) as a full hand (一人前) instead of not at all, because by her own sum that clears the house's three days of debt. (Synced at ship, 2026-11-14: the round-1 draft revision moved the want from 一人分 to the fourth hand and 一人前.)

## NEED

She can see herself in the house only as a pair of hands to be counted, and so she reads every change in the house, her brother's bride above all, as someone taking her place in the line.

## SHAPE

Three-act. Act I is beats 1 and 2, Act II is beats 3 to 6, Act III is beats 7 to 9. The memories are told in the order below, which is not the calendar's: the 17th first, broken off; then late May; then the 16th; then April; then May; then the 10th and the rain days; then the 17th again. Each beat hands the next an object, rope, book, 畦, seedbed, lamp, and that is the join.

## BEATS

1. **(Act I) Now, and the rope, 17 June.** The narrator, eighty-five, in 松本, in June 2026: her brother's grandson's planting machine (田植え機) does the hill house's big paddy in a morning and nobody counts hands; her brother, ninety-five, sits at the window and counts the machine's rows, which was her habit. She begins with the rope (印のついたひも): seventy-two marks, and she counted them. The morning of 17 June 1955, drizzle, the last of the lane's five days: 糸 counting the marks aloud and dividing the hills (「十二人、六株ずつ」), 雪子 given the six nearest 実's spike, 文子 told she is the kitchen today. The first row goes in and the rope lifts once; then she takes off her sandals, wades in, and walks down the line past the bride to where the hills end, and there is nothing past the last six but the spike and the bank. Yes, but: she is in the water in front of four houses, and 糸 has said that the hills were given at the first row and are not given twice, and that the host put its own daughter in the kitchen. The narration breaks off there: before she can say what happened at the end of the line, she has to say what the count was.
2. **The count, and the table, late May.** The five heads meet at 金蔵's house to set the order; 文子 listens at the door and hears her house put last of the five, and hears the three days already on its received side, 金蔵's horse two days at the harrowing (馬で田んぼをならす) and 金蔵 one day at the 畦. That night at the table the mother, dry: 「雪子さんは一人半だに。鶏より先に起きるでな」, and everybody but the bride laughs, 文子 too, because the bride has been up and out before the hens every morning for a fortnight, since the week of the teacher's visit, making the dawn round of the paddies' water that the father used to make, and the joke has a 姑's edge to it. 文子 counts the house: a brother, a mother, a bride at one and a half as a joke, a father on the 布団, and herself, who is not written. She goes down the lane to 糸 and asks to be sent as one of the house's three on the four days and written as one hand (一人分); 糸 laughs, 「十四で一人分はないに」, and tells her the book writes hands, and a child's 苗運び is not written. No, and: now 糸 knows the girl is sulking, and by the first planting day the lane knows it too.
3. **(Act II) The fourth day, the house at the top of the lane, 16 June.** Hands are short; a house two down sends an old man as a half, and the line is eleven. 文子, throwing 苗 (苗打ち) from the 畦, counts the marks against the women and for the first time the line does not divide: 糸 gives six women seven hills and five women six, and says, as the ordinary law of the paddy, that the rope is the rope and the hills are given once; the day runs late and nobody complains. 文子 sees how a short line is made right: not by adding a hand but by widening everyone's hills. Yes, but: she takes it the wrong way round, that if eleven can take seventy-two then thirteen can take it more easily, and that tomorrow she will be the thirteenth and the day will be shorter for it. The 畦 she stands on hands the story the 畦 her father was plastering.
4. **April: the 畦 and the bride.** Early April, 雪子 comes into the house from the next valley, wiping her hands on her cloth before she touches anything. The last week of April, the monk's snow shape (常念坊) on the mountain, and the father plastering the banks with mud (畦に泥を塗る) bent double from dawn; on the second day his back goes and 実 carries him in on his back, and he does not get up again that spring. 文子 stays home from the 中学 the week after to do the house's water with 実, which are her real absences. The 畦 is left half plastered, and 金蔵 comes and finishes it, one day, and later brings his horse for the harrowing, two days; nobody says what those days are. No, and: the house that was going to have five hands this year, with the bride, has three, and the lane has three days against it before the seedbed is sown.
5. **May: the seedbed, the teacher, the textbook.** On the eighth of May, after the 花まつり, 実 and 文子 sow the seedbed (苗を育てる田んぼ); another day off school. The following week the 中学 teacher comes to the house (家庭訪問) and 文子 is sent out to the seedbed while the adults talk; she takes it for the absences, which are real. That night and the nights after, the lamp (明かり) in the front room is lit late, and one night she finds 雪子 at it with her 国語 textbook (教科書) open and takes it back out of her hands without a word; the bride says 「すみません」 and wipes her hands on her cloth. No, and: from that week the bride is up before the hens and out of the house before it is light, taking over the dawn round of the paddies' water that the father used to make and 実 had made since April; from the 10th the dawn is the 苗取り at whichever house plants that day instead. 文子, who counts, counts the mornings and makes nothing of them but keenness.
6. **The first day, 金蔵's paddy, 10 June, and the rains.** The 中学 is closed for the planting week (田植えの休み). 文子 wakes in the dark to the door and sees 雪子 go down the lane toward 金蔵's seedbed with a lamp, two hours before the house's three leave; she thinks: the keen bride. She carries 苗 (苗運び) and throws bundles from the 畦; it is the one thing she is praised for, by 糸, with the saying that if you can throw 苗 right you are a full hand, which is the praise you give a child. She watches 雪子 in the line: to the wrist every time, never a floating 苗 (浮いた苗), and faster than her mother. She throws the next bundle hard enough to splash the bride's face; 雪子 wipes it with her cloth and plants on. The ten o'clock おにぎり go round and she eats hers with the children, and 糸 sings the first line of the planting song (田植え歌) and the line follows. Then the 梅雨 settles in; three days lost; the order slips and the last house's 苗 are the oldest in the lane, growing too tall in the seedbed (伸びすぎる). The father hits the 布団 with his fist when he hears the rain on the roof. In the kitchen 文子 overhears her mother to the bride, 「あんたは一人半だで、無理はしなさんな」, and the tone is not a joke, and 文子 takes it as the mother having chosen. At supper she says she will be in the line on the house's day; 実 says 「おまえは台所だ」; the father says nothing; 雪子 says 「お味噌汁、冷めます」. No, and: the house's day is now the 17th, the last day the 苗 will go in well before the 農休み, and the lane will come tired and short of hands from four days in the water.
7. **(Act III) The house's day, 17 June, resumed: the climax, as written above.** The first row is in, the hills were given once and there is nothing past the last six; 糸 will not stand the line over again against the host's word; 雪子 steps out of her six and gives them to 文子 and takes the 苗 box onto the 畦; 実 says the school and the bargain aloud with the rope's end in his hand, so the lane is not left to say what it would otherwise say about his wife; 雪子 throws her a bundle underhand and says 「ひも、動かしてください」. 文子 plants her six, ten rows, to the wrist. No, and: the want is surrendered in the act. At the tenth row she climbs out onto the 畦, puts the 苗 box in the bride's hands, and carries and throws 苗 for the rest of the day as a child does, and runs the late おにぎり down from the house, and 糸 does not sing, and the lane has watched the house's 嫁 and the house's daughter change places twice.
8. **The evening meal.** Three bundles of 苗 and a bowl of rice on the shelf (神様の棚), set there by the mother; the house feeds the lane; sake; 実 carries the father out to the front room on his back and sets him against the post, then sits by the door and is asleep against the wall before the sake has gone round once, a man after five days in the water. 金蔵 writes in the notebook and 糸 speaks the count aloud as she always does: twelve received today; given this June, 実 four, ナツ four, 雪子 six, 「四日とも暗いうちから苗を取りに来たで、六だに」; fifteen against fourteen; and then, 「文ちゃんの今日の六株で、残りの一日は付けんに」, and 金蔵 writes the girl's name on the given side, which the book does not do for a child. One day in the book, given by the lane, on the day she learned she is leaving. The father says the one thing he says in the story, to the bride, who has not sat down since the dark: 「雪子、座れ」. 雪子 sits, wipes her hands, and says to 文子, who is pouring, 「文子さん、あの本、また貸してください」. Then 糸 sings the first line of the song, and the mother follows, and the line that did not sing in the paddy sings in the house. Yes, but: 糸, loud, who stood in the line when 実 said it and says this anyway as a kindness, 「来年は文ちゃん、一人分で来てもらうに」, and the mother, pouring for her, declines it: 「文は来年、町だで」. The house says it at its own table, in front of the lane, as a plain fact with no bargain attached.
9. **Now.** She left in April 1956 for 松本, to her mother's sister's house (おばの家) and the school there, because the hamlet is an hour and a half's walk above the station and the aunt's house was the father's condition; she left her textbooks on the shelf by the lamp for 雪子, who had had six years of the old school and no more. A town 高校 has no planting holiday and a boarder is not home in June, and she never stood in the line again. The lane's 結 ended with the planting machine in 1974, and the notebook with it. 雪子 is ninety-three and in June she still sits on the 畦 untying bundles of 苗 for her grandson's machine, which is a job nobody has to do. The claim the story ends on, about a person and a number: the narrator thought for two months that 雪子 had taken her place. The bride was never written as one hand. In 金蔵's book she is 一人半, every June from 1955 to 1973, nineteen Junes, and 文子's name is in it once. Yes, but: she went, and she never stood in the line again.
