Round 1 sent the sheet back under PRACTICE and inside the culture at the level of fact (the planting rope's marks were made to count planters rather than hills, the one-and-a-half count was never said to be earned, the debt arithmetic did not add up, the plain's barley-field deadline was applied to a one-crop hill hamlet, and Osaka sourcing was cited as local), under plants and withhold, never confuse (the 一人半 line fell before the bargain it encodes, nothing gave the joke something to be about, and the textbook plant had no payoff), for the afterword (it misdated the teacher's visit and claimed an out-of-order telling the beats did not have), against Rob's 城の鐘 note on monotonic progression (a frame around a strict day-by-day chronology), for Characters and Rob's 猫を探す探偵 note (the brother vanished after the climax), and for ABSENT (the planting-season school closure, the village rest after planting and the seedling offering). The guesser reported no leak in either round; in round 2 it named the title phrase and the house's arithmetic, which the critic ruled anchor and theme, and no guess reached the school bargain. The locator placed it in a cold highland Japanese rice village at planting time and named the exchange unprompted. The transplanter broke the climax and the need-beat, named 恩 and お返し as the pressure lost, and found the family would say the plan at the table once it was gone. Round 2 passed with fixes applied before drafting: the climax's obstacle squared with the uneven division on the 16th, the evening meal squared with the reveal, the bride's dawns given a start, two unpaid words taken out of quoted lines, a reason to board in town, 糸's silence on the house's day made her own, an ambiguous afterword pronoun, and beat numbering. Five characters were renamed at drafting so that every name segments into known parts. Level 4 was taken as a stretch inside Rob's N3 ceiling: its constructions are N3 grammar, and Rob's notes on two earlier stories he read as a stretch support it. Draft stage: two Japanese-only readers and one English-only reader, two rounds. Draft round 1 was sent back by the reconciler under reveal, not puzzle (a marker that the mother's second 一人半 was not a joke, and a purpose clause on the bride's dawn work, which all three readers cited as clues) and because the readers named something other than the pressure (they took the bargain as labour cover and the silence as hierarchy or sulking, not as 恩 and お返し). With it went the evening tally (it did not add up on a first read), facts (the coda's machine seedlings, the planting water's depth), circumlocution where a native writer uses the term, translationese in the narrator's frame lines, flashbacks that read as dated captions against the afterword's own structure claim, energy after the climax, translation lines, names, the exchange's name in English script, the father left unresolved, and afterword sentences. The new-word budget was raised at that round so that the seedbed, the book and the full hand could be named rather than paraphrased; brief.py's per-page estimate had pinned it below the corpus rate. Draft round 2 passed, and its ship fixes were mechanical: an unattributed turn given to the mother, seedling boxes taken out of the scenes set in the year of the story, counters restructured away, the reason for the house's planting date made the seedlings' age, the lost days made a downpour, the aunt's-house and bedridden wording, object-fronted joins both Japanese-only readers heard as English cohesion, an aphorism in the coda, single translationese lines, the English tally and grandson, one clause on who 糸 is to 金蔵 and why she reads the book, the brother's long speech moved into the family's dialect, the sheet's WANT and TWIST synced and the premise refreshed, and afterword sentences (a need stated as a flaw, an ambiguous pronoun, an any-story moral clause, a stock phrase, and the ending told twice). Endings: in both rounds all three readers chose the last line, the narrator's name written once in the book, where intended; the English-only reader found the claim lines before it state the point, which the afterword owns as the correction of fact the ending rests on. Twist: in round 2 all three found it stated at the reveal, by the brother in speech on the bank with the bride's pledge quoted inside it. On the earlier lines the Japanese-only readers said hinted and not stated, and the English-only reader all but stated by the textbook scene; the reconciler ruled no leak, because every clue cited is planted setup and no earlier line states the bargain, the school or the ledger entry. The reconciler also ruled one objection non-blocking, raised by both Japanese-only readers, one as staged for the reader and one as social plausibility: whether an eldest son of that time would set out a private family arrangement, loud enough for the line, in front of four households. The staging is the sheet's own design, passed at Gate 2 (the sister is told in front of the lane, and the telling is the humiliation); the text gives the motive, since the bride of a house in debt has just walked out of the line before the group and her pledge not to put the group out is the lane's business as much as the sister's; and both readers took the reveal fully and stated it correctly. It is a plausibility objection, not a procedure error of the kind PANEL makes binding, and a different reveal setting would have been a creative rewrite with no round left for it. It is recorded here so that Rob's rating can calibrate it. Both Japanese-only readers named the practice in both rounds (the exchange's book, the full-hand reckoning, the half sent by another house, the snow-figure rule, the planting holiday, the offering). In round 2 all three put the house's debt to the exchange at the centre of the twist, one Japanese-only reader said the brother gives the reason the secret was kept, and the English-only reader named the inward half, that the sister must not owe her brother's bride, without either word for the pressure. Both Japanese-only readers found the speech natural for this household and hamlet, with the book doing real work in the plot. Naturalness rose by a step between rounds, the two Japanese-only readers agreeing each time. Left as flagged: the claim lines before the ending, the English-only reader's remaining dated-captions note on the April to June stretch, voices that blur for one reader (糸 with ナツ, the father with 実), ナツ's さん for the bride, ひも against the rope's proper name, horse days valued at one hand, the old man on the 16th read as having no function, and the father's line at the meal found a little tidy.

new_words.結: the planting labour exchange, five houses on one lane trading days of work and keeping the count in a notebook; annotated ｜結《ゆい》 at every occurrence because Ichiran reads the bare kanji otherwise. First occurrence is the women of the other four houses standing on the bank on the house's day, not a definition; recurs as the group, its notebook, its days, the evening meal, and its end when the machine came
new_words.田植え: rice planting, the days themselves. First occurrence is the grandson's planting machine (田植え機) in the frame; recurs as the first planting day, the school's planting holiday, the song, the house's own day, and the machine again
new_words.苗: rice seedlings. First occurrence is the bundles being thrown from the bank to the line; recurs raised in the seedbed, pulled before dawn, carried, floating, overgrown, and offered to the gods at the evening meal
new_words.畦: the paddy bank. First occurrence is where the women line up to be given their hills; recurs where the girl stands throwing bundles, plastered with mud in April, where the bride climbs out of the line, and where she sits now
new_words.苗代: the seedbed, read なわしろ and annotated at every occurrence. First occurrence is the men carrying seedlings up from it to the bank; recurs as the seedbed the girl and her brother make in May, where she is sent during the teacher's visit, where the bride is already pulling seedlings on the first day, where the house's last seedlings overgrow in the rain, in the brother's reveal and in the evening count
new_words.帳面: the exchange's book of days given and taken, read ちょうめん; replaces the postwar ノート. First occurrence is 金蔵 opening it and holding his finger on the house's line while 糸 reads the debt; recurs as the book that will not write the girl, her request to be written in it, the evening count, her name written on the given side, and its end with the machine
new_words.一人前: a full hand, the standard of a grown worker, read いちにんまえ. First occurrence is the girl counting her house at the table, her brother and mother each a full hand; recurs as her sum for clearing the debt, her request to 糸, 糸's refusal at fourteen, the throwing praise she knows is for a child, and the six hills 糸 credits as planted like a full hand

stories.title: 城の鐘
stories._feature: Nested time frames: a story told in the past about a casting forty years earlier. The distinction everything turns on is stated exactly once, in dialogue, on page 12. Level 5 is the sparse N2 edge, four such forms used once each.
stories._note: 王, 従う, 罰, 叫ぶ and 段/二百段 predate the per-story mechanism and remain in approved-words.json. 段 is the weakest of them as a teaching word: two of its six occurrences sit inside 二百段, which Ichiran parses as a single token, so the reader marks the unit rather than teaching the counter.

new_words.響く: to resound, carry — a bell story needs the verb. Framed p8 by explicit contrast: 形の良い鐘は打った後も音が長く響き、悪い鐘は音がすぐに途切れる. Recurs at the king's death, the princess's bad bell, the palm on the tower bell, and the apprentice's strike
new_words.金属: metal — framed p3 by melting and heat, 金属を溶かす日だけ、部屋は息ができないほど熱くなる, then poured, cooled, and made thin at the top. Accepted by check.py via the 金+属 fallback, so it must be declared to be marked

stories.title: 行かなかった人の地図
stories._feature: The longest story in the corpus and the first with a supernatural element. folktale register carries the magic for free: the 主 on the pass is furniture, nobody explains it, and it costs nothing from the new-word budget because 主, 姿, 影, 声, 問う, 通す are all known. The 主 scene also gives the にとって focus a structural home, asking all three travellers the same question.
stories._note: grammar_focus にとって was chosen because the construction and the theme are the same thing: one object meaning something different to each person who holds it. It lands four times, once per holder — 祖父 p5, 甚平 p19, 蓮 p24, 梓 p27 — which is the set the 主 scene is built to collect. 地図のとおりに is the other repeated frame and carries とおり. MEETS ITS PAGE BRIEF AT 44 (briefed 40, band 36-44). This note used to record a 48-page MISS and blame the brief: 'a twelve-beat structure with a six-page set piece in the middle does not fit in 40 pages'. That was wrong, and the 2026-09-19 revision is the proof — all twelve beats and the whole 主 scene are still here at 44. What did not fit was the over-explanation: the two definitional lines that handed the reader 峠 and 崖 outright (峠というのは、山と山の間の、一番低いところである / 崖とは、岩が真っ直ぐに立っているところである), and the narrator restating what a scene had just shown (人が歩けば足跡が残るのだから…). Both words are now framed by what happens to them instead. The brief was reachable; the prose was not yet tight.
stories._premise: 梓's grandfather spent fifty years drawing one map, of a mountain road he never walked, copied from his father's telling. Dying, he asks her to go and see whether the tree at the end of it is still standing. She hires 甚平, an old guide who crosses those mountains without maps, and every landmark on the paper turns out to be wrong. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) the dying grandfather asks her to check the tree / (2) 甚平 reads the map once and says the bridge is in the wrong place / (3) three days in, every landmark matches and 蓮 stops laughing / (4) PLANT: no bridge at the river, and four small 印 beside it on the map that she cannot explain / (5) the detour along the 岸 and up to the 峠 / (6) the 主 asks each of them what they came to do; 梓's answer is her grandfather's, not her own / (7) at the 崖 the road is missing, 蓮 says an old man drew a road out of stories, and 甚平 finds the road under the slide / (8) the village on the map is empty, no 足跡 / (9) TURN, once, in dialogue: 千代 remembers the bridge falling the year of the great snow, seventy-five years ago, five years before the grandfather was born / (10) PAYOFF: the 印 are counts of how many times his father told of each landmark, so the map is scaled to memory rather than distance / (11) the tree is there, and the sea, which on the map is one straight blue line / (12) home: he does not ask about the tree, he asks whether the sea was blue.

new_words.印: mark — the story's own subject matter and its plant. Framed p4 by the act of making one, 祖父が地図へ小さな印を一つ書き足すのを見たことがある, a page after the already-known 目印 it will turn out to be counting. Recurs at the bridge, the village, the rock and the tree, and is what the turn is made of
new_words.頼る: to rely on — framed p1 by the villagers who will not use the map, then sharpened p9 in 蓮's challenge, 行ったことのない人が描いた地図に頼るんですか, where the object of the reliance is the whole question of the story. Recurs whenever the map is trusted or set aside
new_words.導く: to lead, guide — framed p6 by the one name the whole village gives her, あの男が導いてくれる, and again p23 by 甚平's answer to the 主, この二人を北へ導くために来た, beside the already-known 案内 in the same breath. The guide's own word for what he does
new_words.峠: mountain pass — framed p17 without a definition: 甚平 draws two mountains in the dirt, presses his finger into the low place between them and names it, 岸を上って、ここを越える。峠だ. The setting of the 主 scene and the middle third of the journey
new_words.崖: cliff — framed p29 by what it does to the sky, 道の右側に岩が立ち上がって、上の方は空しか見えなくなった, one line before the map shows a road running beneath one. Carries the buried-road beat that proves the map is early rather than false
new_words.岩: rock, boulder — named p3 in the map's list of landmarks, then framed p11 as the first of them to match, with her hand on it: 真ん中から二つに割れていて、割れ目に草が生えている. Recurs as the split rock, the rock slope of the climb, and the slide at the 崖
new_words.岸: riverbank — framed p13 by the width of the water, 流れは速く、向こうの岸は遠い, then p14 by walking it and finding nothing standing on it. The detour is three days of that
new_words.足跡: footprint — framed p18 by 甚平 reading tracks in the earth and naming what is not in them, 動物の足跡ばかりで、人の足跡は一つもない. Marks the empty village p33, and the party's own are the last thing in the grass before the climb

stories.title: 廊下の鏡
stories._feature: First story in the retrospective (述懐) register, and the first in the corpus to end on a claim rather than an image. The register was added for it. Also the first multi-construction grammar_focus: ものの, 一方で and にとって together, chosen because concession, contrast and perspective are the three things a looking-back voice actually does, so the focus and the register reinforce each other instead of the focus being sprinkled on afterwards.
stories._note: THE RISK IS THE ENDING and it was named at Gate 2 before drafting. 'Ends on a claim' sits one step from the closing-thesis defect. The guard is that the claim corrects a fact about a PERSON — 祖母は、不思議なことを信じる人ではなかった — and contradicts a phrase the reader has already been given in dialogue on p10, 「おばあさんは、不思議なことを信じる人だから」. It is a correction, not a moral, and the narrator earns it by watching the hallway go dark rather than by concluding anything. THE MIRROR IS NEVER A FIGURE: it is cleaned, wrapped, carried, cracked, lifted and re-hung, and the prose never once uses it for memory or for looking back. That was a standing constraint from Rob, not a discovery. Every clue is physical and early: it hangs where nobody dresses, it faces a window rather than a room, it is polished on bright days and not dull ones, she is twice shown cleaning it and never once looking into it, and the child needs no lamp at the turn.
stories._premise: A mirror hangs at the turn of a dark hallway in one house for sixty years, through a grandmother, a mother and a daughter, each of whom polishes it, wraps it and hangs it back on the same nail. Only when the last of them takes the house apart and lifts it off the wall does she find out what it was for: hung at an angle to the one window, it carried light around the corner into the windowless back of the house. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) the narrator, 71, is emptying the house and leaves the heavy mirror for last / (2) she notices she has worked all day at the turn without a lamp and thinks nothing of it, because she never has / (3) the grandmother carried the mirror in when she married, chose its place herself, and asked one thing, 動かさないでください / (4) she polished it constantly and only on clear days; PLANT: 一方で, never once seen looking at her own reflection / (5) the family settled on 不思議なことを信じる人, stated in dialogue / (6) she died and nobody moved it, the instruction outliving the reason / (7) the mother kept the rule without the reason, and at the roof repair wrapped it herself and made the workmen return the nail to the same hole / (8) asked why, she could only say her mother had asked her not to / (9) the narrator read all of it as a keepsake and stopped thinking / (10) TURN, physical and not a realization: she lifts it off the nail to wrap it and the back of the hallway goes dark around her while she is holding it / (11) she puts it back three times, and by the third is counting years rather than checking / (12) PAYOFF: the polishing, the weather and the averted eyes all resolve at once / (13) the claim, once: 祖母は、不思議なことを信じる人ではなかった.

new_words.光: light, as a noun — the thing the mirror actually carries, and deliberately withheld until the payoff. 光る is already known, so the noun is the new form. Framed at the turn by 光が、曲がり角を回って奥に届いた, where the sentence before it has just shown the hallway going dark. Recurs through the resolution
new_words.斜め: at an angle — the mechanism of the whole story. Framed p7 by contrast with the flat alternative, 壁と同じ向きにまっすぐ掛けるのではなく、少し斜めにした. Recurs at the roof repair, where the mother restores the angle, and at the payoff
new_words.釘: nail — what fixes the position across three generations. Framed p2 by the act itself, 壁に釘を一本打って、そこに掛けた. Recurs as the same hole at the repair, as 三代、同じ釘, and at the lifting off
new_words.向き: the way a thing faces, orientation — distinct from 斜め, which is that the orientation is oblique. Framed p7 in the same sentence that introduces 斜め, 壁と同じ向きに, and fixed by the already-known 向く in the next line, 鏡は玄関の窓のほうを向いている. Recurs wherever the mirror is set or restored
new_words.埃: dust — why the polishing was frequent rather than fussy, and it is held back as an explanation until the payoff. Framed p9 by its own absence, 埃がついていなくても、晴れた日には必ず磨く, which makes the polishing strange before it makes it sensible

stories.title: 七つの窓
stories._feature: Second story in the ghost-story register, and the first at level 5. The wrong detail is a physical print rather than a document: the half-moon rubber patch the keeper glues onto the student's boot is planted as gruff care and pays off as the only thing in the snow anyone could recognise. One night with one flashback, answering the 城の鐘 note about stories that march through time.
stories._note: THE ORDINARY IS AIRTIGHT ON THE PAGE, because a reader who can explain the prints will: the keeper is awake all night feeding the fire two pieces an hour, the boots are the student's only pair and stand on the rack in sight, the door is at the keeper's back, the snow stops at three and he checks the boots at ten past, the newspaper is still inside at dawn. THE PRINTS ARE NEVER ATTRIBUTED and nobody theorises; there is no narrated fear or awe at the discovery, only walking, looking, going back in. THE 先代 FLASHBACK SITS BESIDE THE PRINTS AND IS NEVER TIED TO THEM: his rule (the keeper goes out first, alone, after a blizzard) and his cup in the rucksack are placed in Act I and Act II and left for the reader. THE WANT RESOLVES IN ACTION, NOT SPEECH: the keeper never asks the boy to come back; he shovels every print, his own included, and packs the cup. 先代 speaks わし-register (じゃ), the keeper 俺 and gruff, the student です・ます. Not a mourned relative: the 先代 is an employer, dead, named only as the source of a rule and a gesture.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: dawn after the storm; going out first and alone as the 先代's rule says, the keeper finds footprints that start at the door, walk the evening round clockwise, stop under each of the seven windows and return to the door, every right print carrying the half-moon patch he glued onto the student's boot; inside, the boots are where he watched them all night, newspaper still in them, the student asleep. He shovels every print away, his own too, and packs the student's cup into the bottom of his rucksack. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: early November, the last day of shutting a high hut for winter; the keeper of thirty seasons and the student who has worked three summers and starts a Tokyo job in spring are snowed in for one night in the hut's one heated room. WANT: for the student to come back next summer, never said; its visible form is the cup set back on the shelf. NEED: to admit the mountain is where he went because nothing below waited, and that wanting the boy here is wanting him to become the same; he has to let him go. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2, II 3-6, III 7-9. BEATS: 1 closing, early snow, trail shut; he returns the cup to the shelf; the 先代's rule on the wall (yes-but, veiled plant). 2 the student's sole splits; the keeper cuts a patch that comes out half-moon, glues it, sets the boots to dry: 朝までは履くな (yes-but, veiled plant). 3 he forbids the evening round in the blizzard (no-and). 4 fuel is short so he stays awake; asked why he has stayed so long, he talks about the wood (no-and). 5 flashback: thirty years ago the 先代 packed his cup on the last morning; he came back and it was on the shelf again (yes-but). 6 at three the snow stops; ten past, he checks the boots; he never sleeps (yes-but). 7 the prints (no-and, climax). 8 he shovels them all and packs the cup (yes-but, the turn). 9 walking down, the student finds the cup; the keeper talks about the snow; the student goes ahead leaving half moons and the keeper walks beside them, not in them (no-and).

new_words.小屋: hut — the setting every beat happens in or around. First occurrence is an act, 山の小屋を閉める, the closing the whole first page is a procedure for. Recurs throughout
new_words.小屋番: hut keeper — the narrator's job and the subject of the 先代's rule. First occurrence is inside the rule itself, an instruction being carried out, and again as 小屋番として、寝るわけにはいかなかった
new_words.足跡: footprints — the wrong detail. Held back until the climax, where the first occurrence is the discovery and the next sentences follow them round the hut; recurs as he erases them and in the last page's ordinary prints
new_words.吹雪: blizzard — first occurs in the 先代's rule on the wall, then as the keeper's reason for forbidding the round, 吹雪だ。窓は昼に俺が見た. The rule's 吹雪の次の朝 is restated at dawn
new_words.見回り: the evening round of the windows — the route the prints walk. First occurrence is the time arriving as the student reaches for his coat, and the next sentence is the round itself, done as a procedure
new_words.先代: the previous keeper — first occurrence is his handwriting on the closing list; recurs in the rule, the flashback and the cup

stories.title: 調律の埃
stories._feature: Second retrospective (述懐) story, and the first whose memories are told out of order: the frame is itself a past day (the last visit, 2011) seen from 2025, and the memory beats jump 1986, 1975, the 1990s, the 2000s. Chosen against the 城の鐘 review note that the corpus progresses through time monotonically. His speech is held to Kansai (わし, や, へん, はる, まへん) and the two women stay standard.
stories._note: THE LOCK IS HIS OWN HABIT. The dust check is planted p1-2 as a jealous craftsman's quirk and p9 as a secret shared with a seven-year-old, and pays off as the camouflage she used for twenty-five years. Fair clues, all physical and early: the piano holds through 梅雨 and winter heating (p13), the mother answers his boasting with the weather and the hydrangeas (p12, p15), 千夏 comes home in the summer holidays and at New Year, exactly between his spring and autumn visits (p16), red felt where his is green (p17-18), the treble cleaner in autumn than he left it in spring (p19). BRIEF: approved at 6 new words against a 600-token estimate; the story runs ~800 tokens, where the derived budget is 8, and check.py flagged ピン, フェルト and ハンマー as unknown. Those three katakana loans are declared rather than written around, and 響く was dropped for the known 鳴る, so 8 declared. The real reason for the refusal is never stated: p7-8 show her hearing the beats before he names them and him closing the lid early. The closing claim 千夏は、私の弟子だった。 corrects his own refusal on p11 and is earned by watching her tune; the last line is the felt.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: on his announced last visit the tuning pins of the Morimoto upright shine with no dust; he packs to leave, accusing the household of using another tuner; the mother looks past him; 千夏, 43, stands in the doorway with a hammer worn like his and says she did not put the dust back this time. For twenty-five years she tuned the piano between his visits and restored the dust he taught her to read. He detunes a string and hands her his hammer; she fixes it faster and cleaner than he could; he says only 埃は、もう戻さんでええ, tells the mother to call her from now on, and leaves his hammer. AFTERWORD: stories-index.md. PREMISE: a proud tuner judges every piano by the dust on its pins; he refused the daughter of his most loyal house as an apprentice; on his last visit the dust is gone. WANT: to end his career with the Morimoto piano as proof of his craft. NEED: his pride cannot bear being surpassed, and he refused her because her ear frightened him, not because she was a girl. SHAPE: three-act, memories out of order. BEATS: (I) 1 the dust habit, he walks out of houses with clean pins / 2 2011, the Morimoto pins shine / 3 1975, the child hears the beats before he names them, he closes the lid early, then shows her the dust check | (II) 4 1986, she asks to be his 弟子, he refuses and threatens never to return if another hand touches the piano; she leaves / 5 the piano holds its pitch, he boasts, the mother answers with the weather; she comes home at Obon and New Year / 6 the red felt; the treble cleaner than he left it | (III) 7 the climax / 8 the test, the hammer handed over / 9 2025 coda, 千夏は、私の弟子だった, the red felt among his green.

new_words.調律: tuning (a piano) — the trade itself. First occurrence is the verb in action, 町のピアノを調律して回った; recurs as 調律師, 調律が終わって, 調律のハンマー
new_words.鍵盤: keyboard, a key — first occurrence is the thing he will not touch before checking the dust, 鍵盤に触る前に; recurs at the climax as 鍵盤には一度も触らなかった and when 千夏 strikes one key over and over
new_words.弦: string — framed p7 by the act of tuning two strings together until they stop wobbling; recurs through the treble beats and the test
new_words.埃: dust — the plant and the lock. First occurrence is on his fingertip after he runs it over the pins; recurs at every check, the secret shown to the child, and her 埃を戻しませんでした
new_words.湿気: damp, humidity — framed p13 by wood soaking it up and pitch rising; recurs as the damp every other piano drifts in and the Morimoto piano does not
new_words.ピン: tuning pin — katakana loan, transparent to the reader. First occurrence is under his finger, ピンの頭を指でそっとなでてみる; it is where the dust sits and where the scratches shine
new_words.フェルト: felt (the tuner's mute) — katakana loan. First occurrence is the red strip found wedged between the treble strings; the colour is the clue, his is green, and it closes the story
new_words.ハンマー: tuning hammer — katakana loan. First occurrence is the fresh scratches its head leaves on the pins; then hers worn like his, and his handed to her and left behind
